pO7UlTVbOI.one_liner: Kombine benchmarks LLM combinatorial creativity through association, analogy and blending tasks with open-ended concept invention.
pO7UlTVbOI.problem: It is unclear whether LLMs can combine familiar ideas in unfamiliar and useful ways to invent new concepts, since prior work mostly tests recognition of known analogies or associations.
pO7UlTVbOI.method: Kombine asks models to discover surprising, original and useful associations, analogies and blends between unrelated entities, then to use them to invent new concepts by recombining parts of existing ones. Per reviews, outputs are scored by an LLM judge panel and an embedding-distance surprise measure.
pO7UlTVbOI.key_idea: Make models discover connections between unrelated entities and then invent concepts from them, scoring validity, surprise and originality relative to the pool of evaluated models.
pO7UlTVbOI.evidence: Large-scale study of 35 LLMs with an analysis of reused invented properties across models, and a human check on 60 outputs per a review.
pO7UlTVbOI.claimed_gains: LLMs are 10-15 percentage points better at associations and analogies than blends, one in five invented concepts reuses another model's properties, models are 14x more likely to reuse properties on blends than analogies, and same-provider models are 2.3x more likely to reuse them.
pO7UlTVbOI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is well motivated with clear cognitive-science grounding, defines association, analogy and blending formally, and gives a useful large-scale snapshot of 35 models.
pO7UlTVbOI.main_concern: Construct validity is weak: scores rely on unvalidated LLM judges (66% agreement with a single human annotator on 60 outputs) and originality is defined relative to the evaluated model pool.

lmTmF6H8Mx.one_liner: Trains coding agents from scratch on stronger-model demonstrations to speedrun SWE-bench and test what pre-training contributes.
lmTmF6H8Mx.problem: It is unclear how models acquire specialized skills and what pre-training adds beyond imitating a teacher on SWE-bench.
lmTmF6H8Mx.method: Speedruns SWE-bench by training coding agents from scratch on demonstrations from stronger models under a fixed compute budget, fits scaling laws on smaller runs, and runs controlled experiments including a model pre-trained only on text from before 1931.
lmTmF6H8Mx.key_idea: One-student hypothesis: pre-training helps a student imitate its teacher, but once imitation quality is known, how the student was pre-trained barely matters.
lmTmF6H8Mx.evidence: Training with 192 B200-hours, scaling laws fitted to smaller runs, comparisons with fine-tunes of a model pre-trained on trillions of tokens, web-versus-vintage pre-training comparisons, and MMLU evaluation of the speedrun model.
lmTmF6H8Mx.claimed_gains: With 192 B200-hours of training compute the agents reach 25.5% pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified, outperforming GPT-4o, and fitted scaling laws forecast this within 0.3 percentage points.
lmTmF6H8Mx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is carefully designed (small-scale runs, scaling-law forecasting, multiple test sets), the problem setting is interesting, and the one-student hypothesis is argued convincingly.
lmTmF6H8Mx.main_concern: Some claims go beyond the evidence, notably that the one-student hypothesis explains why a stronger teacher need not help a weaker student, and the in-domain loss-performance link is unsurprising.

4C7KaZ5JSA.one_liner: Shows language-pretrained transformers transfer to time-series forecasting through a reusable manifold that finetuning only aligns low-dimensionally.
4C7KaZ5JSA.problem: It is unclear whether and why language-pretrained transformers become effective time-series forecasters.
4C7KaZ5JSA.method: Linearly probes frozen LLM states to decode time-series trajectories without paired supervision, forecasts by retrieval in the projected space, and analyzes optimization (gradient coherence, loss landscape) and finetuning updates (low-rank, subspace alignment, shared periodicity and trend features) against random initialization.
4C7KaZ5JSA.key_idea: Language pretraining builds a reusable manifold in which temporal structure is already decodable, and finetuning merely projects numerical dynamics onto task-relevant directions.
4C7KaZ5JSA.evidence: Linear probes, retrieval forecasts, pretrained-versus-random-initialization comparisons across two model families, and low-rank and subspace analyses, with matched-noise and surrogate controls per reviews.
4C7KaZ5JSA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explaining why language-pretrained models transfer to time series is worthwhile and that the controls (2x2 ablation, surrogate controls) and comprehensive experiments support the manifold account.
4C7KaZ5JSA.main_concern: The central claim is not isolated from generic effects of well-conditioned pretrained weights (no shuffled-weight or spectrum-matched controls), and the retrieval experiment may leak future information through normalization.

khyAiOYkPl.one_liner: Chooses Kronecker factors of the Hessian for two-sided GPTQ quantization by minimizing a rate-distortion mismatch factor, giving the FlipFlop Hessian.
khyAiOYkPl.problem: It is unclear how to choose the Kronecker-factored Hessian approximation for post-training quantization, since common choices (input-only, marginal, Frobenius-based) lack a distortion-based justification.
khyAiOYkPl.method: WaterKron combines two-sided GPTQ with row- and column-dependent waterfilling scales and entropy coding, and derives its high-rate distortion with respect to the full Hessian through a Kronecker-Hessian mismatch factor Phi. Minimizing Phi gives a Gaussian covariance-fitting problem solved by classical flip-flop updates, which yields the FlipFlop Hessian.
khyAiOYkPl.key_idea: Pick Kronecker Hessian factors by minimizing the asymptotic Kronecker-Hessian mismatch factor, which reduces to Gaussian covariance fitting solved by flip-flop iterations.
khyAiOYkPl.evidence: A high-rate rate-distortion derivation plus empirical evaluation of KL divergence and perplexity against input-only, marginal, and Frobenius-based Hessian choices.
khyAiOYkPl.claimed_gains: The FlipFlop Hessian consistently improves KL divergence and perplexity over input-only, marginal, and Frobenius-based Hessian choices; no figures stated.
khyAiOYkPl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the information-theoretic framework well motivated, the mismatch factor an interpretable criterion for selecting Kronecker factors, and the FlipFlop Hessian a principled alternative to Frobenius-based approximation.
khyAiOYkPl.main_concern: The mismatch factor is not directly tested against measured distortion, the contributions are seen as incremental over WaterSIC and YAQA, and the operational rate accounting is underspecified.

e0JZEibtrY.one_liner: Shows via deep linear network and linear attention dynamics that Muon avoids saddle points but loses gradient descent's simplicity bias.
e0JZEibtrY.problem: Muon's training speed is widely validated, but the downsides of the mechanism behind that speedup, in particular its effect on inductive bias, are unexamined.
e0JZEibtrY.method: The paper analyzes the learning dynamics of simplified Muon on deep linear networks and multi-head linear attention, then runs experiments testing the consequences of losing the simplicity bias.
e0JZEibtrY.key_idea: Muon speeds optimization by avoiding saddle points, which removes the progressive complexity growth (simplicity bias) that gradient descent shows when learning solutions mode by mode.
e0JZEibtrY.evidence: Theory on deep linear networks and multi-head linear attention, plus small controlled experiments on shared structure across tasks and spurious features.
e0JZEibtrY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the optimization-versus-generalization trade-off meaningful and well supported by a clear theoretical toy setting and controlled experiments.
e0JZEibtrY.main_concern: Theory and experiments are small-scale with no clear link to large-scale practice, where Muon generally generalizes well.

BEVjf6rHRi.one_liner: Streaming framework combining coarse and refined sampling for fast-update, space-optimal clustering, subspace embedding and projection-cost preservation.
BEVjf6rHRi.problem: Near-optimal-space streaming algorithms for clustering and dimensionality reduction often need costly per-update computation, limiting their use on large datasets.
BEVjf6rHRi.method: A general framework filters stream items with a coarse sampling scheme before expensive refined sampling, applied to Euclidean (k,z)-clustering, Lp subspace embeddings and projection-cost preservation in insertion-only streams.
BEVjf6rHRi.key_idea: Run cheap crude sampling first to reduce the data reaching the expensive refined sampling step, amortizing update cost.
BEVjf6rHRi.evidence: Theoretical algorithms and analysis giving near-linear update time and space independent of stream length for three problems.
BEVjf6rHRi.claimed_gains: Exponential improvement in k in the update time for (k,z)-clustering over prior streaming algorithms, and input-sparsity total update time for subspace embedding and projection-cost preservation; no numeric values.
BEVjf6rHRi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework applies across several problems and addresses both update time and space, with a clear source of the speedup.
BEVjf6rHRi.main_concern: Reviewers report correctness gaps in the technical details (an inconsistent update condition in Algorithm 1, an approximation-guarantee mismatch for general z, and flawed matrix-sampling guarantees).

3Cog0c02TY.one_liner: Shows contrastive decoding for VLMs is classifier-free guidance with different references, then switches between prefix-conditioned and prefix-free references.
3Cog0c02TY.problem: Contrastive decoding methods for VLMs lack a unifying view, and references that use the model's own answer prefix leak image information and collapse the guidance signal.
3Cog0c02TY.method: They cast contrastive decoders as CFG with different references, analyze reference design and answer-prefix effects, and propose a switching scheme that alternates a prefix-conditioned reference with a prefix-free reference to balance signal collapse against stale over-guidance.
3Cog0c02TY.key_idea: Alternate between a reference conditioned on the model's own answer prefix and a prefix-free reference, countering guidance collapse and stale over-guidance in long answers.
3Cog0c02TY.evidence: Ten general benchmarks with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B (InternVL also per reviews) against four published contrastive decoders, with prefix-swap and prefix-window analyses.
3Cog0c02TY.claimed_gains: Improves Qwen2.5-VL-7B by 5.7 points and Qwen3-VL-8B by 1.7 points across ten general benchmarks at 1.04x the cost of unguided decoding, versus up to 2x for prior methods.
3Cog0c02TY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the CFG unification and the answer-prefix analysis are insightful and carefully done, and the resulting method adds almost no inference cost.
3Cog0c02TY.main_concern: Gains concentrate on short-answer benchmarks where switching rarely activates, and the guidance scale and switch threshold are fixed while baselines run at published settings.

iBaPFvIupo.one_liner: Benchmark of migrating whole ML repositories from PyTorch on GPUs to JAX on TPUs, graded by reproducing published results.
iBaPFvIupo.problem: ML code mostly lives in two ecosystems (PyTorch on NVIDIA GPUs, JAX on Google TPUs), and migrating repositories between them requires building and testing across frameworks and hardware.
iBaPFvIupo.method: XStack gives an agent a PyTorch repository on GPUs and requires a JAX codebase on TPUs that meets grading criteria based on the source repository's published result, authenticated and calibrated by the authors, with LLM judges and fresh-machine reruns per reviews.
iBaPFvIupo.key_idea: Grade a migrated repository by whether it reaches the source repository's calibrated published result on TPUs after retraining, with provenance and rule checks.
iBaPFvIupo.evidence: Seven agents on 16 repositories (112 cells) per reviews, with token cost, TPU usage and a frozen second phase reported.
iBaPFvIupo.claimed_gains: Claude Opus 5 passes 81%, GPT-5.6-sol 44%, and every other agent at most 38%.
iBaPFvIupo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the task is demanding and practically useful, with fresh-machine full retraining and detailed reporting that give an unsaturated signal.
iBaPFvIupo.main_concern: Each cell is a single run with no error bars, and LLM judges that reject many grader passes are not validated against human review.

wzXvuXRQH7.one_liner: RAD embeds a compact learned representation in the denoising process and feeds it back into the denoiser at each step.
wzXvuXRQH7.problem: Diffusion models reach high sample quality but have no built-in mechanism to learn semantic representations, and representation-alignment approaches overlook feeding the learned representation back into the denoiser.
wzXvuXRQH7.method: Training maximizes a variational lower bound on data likelihood in which representation-alignment models appear as special cases, and the learned representation is fed back into the denoiser; the framework also extends to text-to-image synthesis.
wzXvuXRQH7.key_idea: Include a latent representation in the denoising variational objective and feed the predicted representation back into the denoiser at every step.
wzXvuXRQH7.evidence: Class-conditional image generation at B, L and XL model scales against representation-alignment baselines such as REPA and REG, plus text-to-image synthesis, with FID and sampling-step analyses described in the reviews.
wzXvuXRQH7.claimed_gains: An order of magnitude gain in training convergence speed, data efficiency and sampling efficiency over the prevalent representation alignment framework, while enabling semantic discriminative representations.
wzXvuXRQH7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers cite strong practical results (faster training and sampling with competitive quality across scales), a simple core mechanism of representation feedback, and a clear link to representation alignment through a variational framework.
wzXvuXRQH7.main_concern: Efficiency claims are not established under matched, converged conditions (at most 400K steps; recall 0.49 to 0.50 versus about 0.65 for REPA), and the stochastic-latent contribution is not isolated from deterministic feature feedback.

1yBVddIkKK.one_liner: Organizes an LLM's reasoning-strategy memory as a hierarchical Dirichlet process mixture over behavior embeddings, updated online at test time
1yBVddIkKK.problem: Verbalized chain-of-thought reasoning is costly, and insights discovered while solving queries, such as through self-reflection, have limited mechanisms for being carried forward to later problems.
1yBVddIkKK.method: The Bayesian Cheatsheet fits an HDP-GMM over behavior embeddings that shares components across domains with domain-specific mixing weights, retrieves behaviors through the posterior predictive, and softly updates sufficient statistics after each sample while creating new components when synthesized behaviors are novel.
1yBVddIkKK.key_idea: A hierarchical Dirichlet process Gaussian mixture over behavior embeddings supplies retrieval by posterior predictive and cheap conjugate online updates, with new components spawned for novel behaviors.
1yBVddIkKK.evidence: Reasoning benchmarks including AIME'25, Omni-MATH, and PhysReason (per reviewers), compared with existing memory modules and k-means variants on a shared behavior corpus, retrieval budget, and backbones, with three seeds.
1yBVddIkKK.claimed_gains: Clear performance gains relative to existing memory modules across reasoning benchmarks such as AIME'25 and Omni-MATH; no numbers stated in the batch abstract.
1yBVddIkKK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formulation is principled, gives a clean retrieve, update, and refit abstraction, and shows strong benchmark gains under a fair shared-corpus comparison.
1yBVddIkKK.main_concern: Reviewers say the gains are not rigorously supported, with no variance or confidence intervals, hyperparameters tuned on the test benchmarks, and the benefit of the hierarchical Bayesian machinery over flat clustering never directly tested.

Vt5LnRPZlE.one_liner: Backward induction over auxiliary stage games, each solved as a constant-expectation correlated equilibrium, computes normal-form correlated equilibria in Markov games
Vt5LnRPZlE.problem: Existing work on correlated equilibria in Markov games covers concepts weaker than normal-form correlated equilibria (NFCEs), leaving their efficient computation open since Papadimitriou and Roughgarden (JACM'08).
Vt5LnRPZlE.method: The algorithm runs backward induction on a sequence of auxiliary stage games, computing in each step a constant-expectation correlated equilibrium, in which the conditional expected payoff from obeying is independent of the recommendation. The reduction also goes the other way, giving an equivalence between constant-expectation CEs and NFCEs in Markov games.
Vt5LnRPZlE.key_idea: Run backward induction over auxiliary stage games, solving each as a constant-expectation correlated equilibrium, a refinement equivalent to NFCEs in Markov games.
Vt5LnRPZlE.evidence: Theory only: a running-time bound for an ε-NFCE and PPAD-completeness under independent-across-states recommendations for many players or exponentially small precision; no experiments.
Vt5LnRPZlE.claimed_gains: Computes an ε-NFCE in time S(AH/ε)^{O(n)} with S states, horizon H, at most A actions per player, and a fixed number of players n; PPAD-completeness for many-player games or exponentially small precision.
Vt5LnRPZlE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the result is significant, the solution concept is natural, and the algorithm and proof are simple and clear, complemented by hardness results.
Vt5LnRPZlE.main_concern: Reviewers say the exponential dependence on the number of players makes the algorithm impractical beyond few players, the concept's relevance relative to standard correlated equilibria is unclear, and the paper has no experiments.

tZVMivkWpv.one_liner: Transformers on constrained lattice walks integrate moves into position and time in the first attention block; later layers predict
tZVMivkWpv.problem: It is unclear which predictive statistic emergent world representations in next-token predictors encode, and why they take the form they do.
tZVMivkWpv.method: The authors use constrained random walks on a 2D lattice that must reach a fixed endpoint after a predetermined number of steps, where position and elapsed time suffice to predict the future. They train decoder-only transformers on exactly sampled walks and probe which statistics are decodable and how they are used.
tZVMivkWpv.key_idea: In a process where position and time are sufficient statistics, the transformer's first attention block integrates moves into that state and later layers map it to the next-step distribution.
tZVMivkWpv.evidence: Decoder-only transformers trained on exactly sampled walks with decoding probes, steering and ablation experiments, comparisons across fully observed variants and seeds, a masked-step latent-variable variant, and RNN experiments.
tZVMivkWpv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the exactly computable predictive distribution gives a reliable reference, and that steering and ablation experiments show the representations are used for prediction, not just decodable.
tZVMivkWpv.main_concern: Reviewers say generality is unclear because the setting is simple additive motion on a fixed lattice, results are sensitive to initialization, and the two-stage conclusions may be specific to transformers since RNNs organize the state differently.

nwcUf3uik4.one_liner: Turns a memorization metric into a Kantorovich potential via the Moreau envelope; its proximal steers flow models at inference
nwcUf3uik4.problem: Flow-based models can reproduce training samples verbatim despite valid convergence, which hurts creativity, low-data use, and security, yet memorization could also be exploited deliberately for controlled generation.
nwcUf3uik4.method: The framework converts a memorization metric into a Kantorovich potential via the Moreau envelope and uses the envelope's proximal to build an attractive or repulsive memorization field applied as an inference-time perturbation, with a dial for how much memorization is mitigated or enforced. A proximal gradient descent algorithm computes the proximal during inference, and an optimal transport interpretation is given.
nwcUf3uik4.key_idea: The proximal of the Moreau envelope of a memorization metric defines an attractive or repulsive field added to the flow velocity at inference.
nwcUf3uik4.evidence: Illustrative use cases across modalities, including mitigating memorization in low-data image generation (a RetinaMNIST experiment with 1,000 low-resolution images per reviewers) and steering flow-based language models, plus an optimal transport interpretation.
nwcUf3uik4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and the training-free, mathematically principled inference-time method is simple, with experiments showing it can mitigate memorization.
nwcUf3uik4.main_concern: Reviewers say the empirical evaluation is too small in scale (a small RetinaMNIST experiment and a small text setup), the memorization score can miss duplicated data, and the added inference cost and scalability are not reported.

yUZKHTlbNE.one_liner: Benchmark testing whether agents follow requested work durations, predict their own runtime, and estimate elapsed time afterward
yUZKHTlbNE.problem: Controlling agent runtime requires time-awareness, but duration-following and control in native agent harnesses has remained unexplored.
yUZKHTlbNE.method: AgentTime appends a single instruction specifying how long to work (from about a minute to multiple days) to tasks from 18 sources spanning coding, computer use, agentic work, and automated research. It also tests runtime forecasting and retrospective elapsed-time estimation in native harnesses.
yUZKHTlbNE.key_idea: Request a fixed work duration through one appended instruction and measure deviation of actual runtime, while checking transcripts to separate on-time finishing from continued work on the task.
yUZKHTlbNE.evidence: Duration-following, forecasting, and retrospective experiments on 9 agents in native harnesses, with 1,991 duration-following runs per a reviewer and transcript classification of 79 Astra runs; the TLDR gives 222 tasks while the abstract text says 200.
yUZKHTlbNE.claimed_gains: Only GPT-6 models in Codex follow duration requests (GPT-6 Astra ends 88% of runs on time versus 16% for Fable 5.1), Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 in Claude Code deviate by more than 2× on average, and 9 of 79 classifiable Astra runs slept after appearing to finish.
yUZKHTlbNE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree runtime control is a practically important new evaluation axis, measured at realistic scale with careful analysis that separates on-time finishing from actually working.
yUZKHTlbNE.main_concern: Reviewers say each condition is run once so request effects are confounded with run-to-run variance, coverage is narrow (few agents and one instruction framing), and the paper measures but proposes no fixes.

MALCeMr8iJ.one_liner: An LM lists options for each semantic decision and an external RNG picks one, conditioning later choices on earlier ones
MALCeMr8iJ.problem: Language model diversity relies on token entropy, which suffers mode collapse and trades off against model capability, so sampling rarely surfaces distinct high-quality modes of an open-ended response space.
MALCeMr8iJ.method: Gacha Decoding treats diversity as an instruction-following problem: the LM enumerates options along decision axes, an external RNG tool selects among them ('planning with dice'), and later options are generated conditioned on earlier selections.
MALCeMr8iJ.key_idea: Diversity comes from instruction following combined with randomness from an external RNG tool over semantic choices, not from the LM's token entropy.
MALCeMr8iJ.evidence: Open-ended domains (in-the-wild chat, creative writing, planning for image generation, and protein design) across models, with quality-gated diversity evaluation and ablations including an independent-axes variant and a list-prompting baseline.
MALCeMr8iJ.claimed_gains: Up to 2.3x Vendi over the next-best prior approach (persona prompting) at an equal quality threshold, and 11.0x fewer samples to reach the same number of high-quality modes.
MALCeMr8iJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method shows consistently higher quality-gated diversity than baselines across domains and models, and that moving diversity from token entropy to instruction following is an interesting idea.
MALCeMr8iJ.main_concern: Reviewers say conceptual novelty is limited relative to prior work that generates diverse plans and conditions on them, and the method depends on the model enumerating a diverse option list, which is not directly evaluated.

qzknNfSf8U.one_liner: Estimates epistemic uncertainty of flow-matching robot policies from velocity-field disagreement across a small ensemble, for failure detection and active fine-tuning
qzknNfSf8U.problem: Generalist robot policies with flow-matching action heads lack a way to quantify confidence and detect unreliable actions, which limits deployment in non-stationary environments.
qzknNfSf8U.method: The authors derive an epistemic uncertainty estimator for flow-matching models from velocity-field disagreement (VFD) across a small ensemble. They also propose SAVE, an uncertainty-guided active multitask fine-tuning method that reduces the expert demonstrations needed to adapt generalist policies to new tasks.
qzknNfSf8U.key_idea: Ensemble disagreement between members' velocity fields is a KL-based epistemic uncertainty measure, computable alongside action sampling without changing training.
qzknNfSf8U.evidence: Simulation and real-world experiments across VLAs (reviewers name SmolVLA and X-VLA) and a world-action model (FastWAM), with benchmarks including LIBERO-Long and Push-T, evaluating calibration, failure detection, and active fine-tuning.
qzknNfSf8U.claimed_gains: VFD yields better-calibrated uncertainty estimates predictive of downstream performance and detects failures with at least 5 pp improvement; the rest of the sentence is cut off in the batch abstract.
qzknNfSf8U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important, the VFD estimator is theoretically motivated and cheap to compute, and experiments cover multiple VLA and world-action architectures in simulation and the real world.
qzknNfSf8U.main_concern: Reviewers say a two-member ensemble fine-tuned from the same checkpoint may not capture epistemic uncertainty, correlation with task success does not separate it from aleatoric uncertainty, and margins over strong baselines are small with a temperature tuned on evaluation runs.

70D4hbURD3.one_liner: Multi-agent LLM coordination through a shared datastore of linked messages with bounded search, citation-ranked retrieval, and persistence after agents leave
70D4hbURD3.problem: LLM multi-agent systems scale poorly: reading burden grows with group size, useful information is diluted by shared work of unknown quality, and systems are fragile to failed agents.
70D4hbURD3.method: In ScaleMAS, asynchronous agents interact with a shared datastore of linked messages through three operations: publishing messages with optional references to earlier ones, searching by content, and visiting by address. Each read returns at most k messages ranked by relevance and citation count, and messages persist after their producers leave.
70D4hbURD3.key_idea: Coordination happens in a shared linked-message store with reads capped at k results and ranked by relevance and citation count, so read size stays fixed as groups grow.
70D4hbURD3.evidence: Four agentic tasks against agent-centric and blackboard-style baselines, on two backbones with groups of up to 128 agents, plus stress tests and analyses separating the shared substrate's role.
70D4hbURD3.claimed_gains: ScaleMAS outperforms agent-centric and blackboard-style baselines at lower inference compute and keeps improving as more agents are added, saturating at 16 to 128 agents depending on the task.
70D4hbURD3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the three failure modes are concrete and mapped to simple design choices, and that experiments up to 128 agents with thorough analysis are valuable.
70D4hbURD3.main_concern: Reviewers say the evaluation is small and partly confounded (first 100 examples per benchmark, Pass@N accuracy, single-agent note-taking effects), and the method resembles a retrieval-augmented blackboard with error-propagation risk.

pfPGJ6T7ld.one_liner: Pipeline extracts assumptions from successful agent trajectories, injects targeted environment changes, and validates solvability to measure terminal-agent adaptation
pfPGJ6T7ld.problem: Agent strategies rely on assumptions about the environment, and it is unclear whether agents detect and adapt when those assumptions break while the task objective stays fixed.
pfPGJ6T7ld.method: AGNI automatically extracts trajectory-relevant assumptions, injects targeted environmental changes (novelties) across three terminal benchmarks, and validates that the resulting novel tasks remain solvable. The authors then evaluate multiple LLM agents, analyze trajectories, and post-train on environmental novelty.
pfPGJ6T7ld.key_idea: Break one assumption underlying an otherwise successful trajectory while keeping the task objective fixed, so the base-versus-novel performance gap is intended to measure adaptation rather than task competence.
pfPGJ6T7ld.evidence: Three terminal benchmarks with multiple LLM agents, trajectory analysis, and post-training experiments evaluated on held-out novel tasks and base tasks.
pfPGJ6T7ld.claimed_gains: Evaluation reveals a substantial adaptation gap between base and novel tasks, and post-training on environmental novelty improves adaptation on held-out novel tasks while also improving base-task performance; no numbers stated.
pfPGJ6T7ld.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree environmental novelty is a well-motivated framing and the pipeline is carefully designed, with paired environments, solvability checks, and validation, and that the evaluation separates task competence from adaptation.
pfPGJ6T7ld.main_concern: Reviewers say GPT-5.5 is involved in generating, filtering, solving, and judging the tasks without human audit, so the evaluation set may be biased toward it, and the base-novel gap does not isolate adaptation ability.

y7pGlnqLdE.one_liner: Multi-stream generative spoken language model over SpidR 2.0 discrete units from several encoder layers, narrowing the gap to text LMs.
y7pGlnqLdE.problem: Spoken language models lag far behind text models in capability and data scaling efficiency, due to weak speech units and reliance on a single stream of discrete units.
y7pGlnqLdE.method: The encoder SpidR 2.0 uses self-supervised learning with differentiable prediction heads to induce discrete units at multiple levels. A multi-stream SLM then models these units jointly with a shared temporal backbone, stream-specific predictors, and an autoregressive head that captures cross-stream dependencies.
y7pGlnqLdE.key_idea: Model several complementary discrete unit streams from different encoder layers jointly, with stream-specific predictors and an autoregressive head for cross-stream dependencies.
y7pGlnqLdE.evidence: Training data sizes and model scales up to 6M hours and 6.5B parameters, evaluated on sWuggy, sBLIMP, and tSC across read and conversational speech, plus unit-quality (ABX) analysis.
y7pGlnqLdE.claimed_gains: Shrinks the gap between spoken and text-based LMs by about two orders of magnitude (roughly 100x) on sWuggy, sBLIMP, and tSC, while outperforming competitive speech-text systems on all three tasks.
y7pGlnqLdE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clear and thorough, the multi-stream design is well motivated by layer-wise speech representations, and the results are very strong.
y7pGlnqLdE.main_concern: The claim that streams capture different levels of abstraction is weakly supported (layers 5 to 10 show near-flat unit duration and high overlap), and the design adds training cost without compute-controlled comparisons.

lDmTLLH3lz.one_liner: Discrete image tokenizer trained to reconstruct pretrained features, not pixels, so tokens are easier for generators to model.
lDmTLLH3lz.problem: Tokenizers trained for pixel reconstruction prioritize low-level fidelity and may disrupt the representation structure that makes token distributions easy for generators to learn.
lDmTLLH3lz.method: FeaTok trains discrete tokens by reconstructing features from pretrained encoders (SigLIP, SigLIP2, DINOv2, DINOv3) rather than pixels, with an encoder regularization loss that preserves the pretrained features.
lDmTLLH3lz.key_idea: Use a feature-predictive objective, as in self-supervised learning, to supervise discrete tokens, giving up pixel fidelity for token distributions that generators learn more easily.
lDmTLLH3lz.evidence: Ablations across four pretrained encoders with pixel, mixed, and feature targets under a BAR-style generator, class-conditional ImageNet generation, text-to-image on three benchmarks, and reward-model scores.
lDmTLLH3lz.claimed_gains: Reduces gFDr6 at 256x256 by up to 29% over the strongest discrete baselines and outperforms the strongest unguided continuous baseline (RAEv2) with 38x less sampling compute; surpasses continuous and discrete text-conditional baselines on three benchmarks with only 500 fine-tuning updates.
lDmTLLH3lz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea is simple and well motivated, supported by well-controlled ablations across four pretrained encoders and a strong quality-compute tradeoff.
lDmTLLH3lz.main_concern: Novelty is incremental relative to DINO-Tok, TA-Tok, and Holistic Tokenizer, and the evidence that tokens are more learnable rests on a weak spatial mutual-information proxy.

E6Pjxklgz0.one_liner: Tests whether language models infer, revise, and transfer predictive relationships when forecasting, using prediction markets and synthetic environments.
E6Pjxklgz0.problem: It is unclear whether LMs recover and use predictive relationships in judgmental forecasting rather than relying on base rates or surface cues.
E6Pjxklgz0.method: A battery of experiments on real-world prediction markets and controlled synthetic environments tests belief updating, recovery of predictive relationships, and transfer, including fine-tuning on families of relationships.
E6Pjxklgz0.key_idea: Isolate inductive forecasting with controlled tasks that test coherent belief updating, relationship recovery under sparse data, and transfer, with shortcut controls.
E6Pjxklgz0.evidence: Prediction-market data and synthetic environments, with mechanistic interventions and fine-tuning experiments across several models.
E6Pjxklgz0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled experiments are well designed, with ablations that isolate each capability and convincing evidence across models.
E6Pjxklgz0.main_concern: The real-world prediction-market result is hard to interpret since models approach the latest market price, and some findings overlap with prior work.

cfjgk1urWf.one_liner: Preconditions the physics-informed residual loss with multigrid so neural operators train label-free to supervised-level accuracy.
cfjgk1urWf.problem: Physics-informed neural operator training trails supervised training because differential operators make the loss ill-conditioned, worsening with mesh refinement.
cfjgk1urWf.method: A preconditioned residual loss realized with geometric and algebraic multigrid applies to linear and nonlinear, steady or time-dependent equations on structured and unstructured meshes, with no inference cost.
cfjgk1urWf.key_idea: Precondition the discrete residual loss with multigrid so its conditioning stays mesh-independent for elliptic problems, independent of the operator architecture.
cfjgk1urWf.evidence: Poisson, Allen-Cahn, and stationary Stokes experiments, plus a conditioning analysis for elliptic and saddle point problems.
cfjgk1urWf.claimed_gains: Label-free training matches supervised training and is four to twenty-five times more accurate than previous physics-informed operator learning methods.
cfjgk1urWf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method targets a clear numerical bottleneck, is architecture-agnostic with no inference cost, and improves substantially over unpreconditioned training.
cfjgk1urWf.main_concern: Experiments are small-scale with few, older baselines (PINO, physics-informed DeepONet) and do not directly test scaling with mesh resolution.

rXNJlCzWCL.one_liner: Learns instruction embedding spaces whose local support defines label-conditional conformal scores to predict whether an LLM succeeds on new instructions.
rXNJlCzWCL.problem: Aggregate benchmark scores hide per-instruction variation, and conformal prediction sets are only informative if the calibrated score is, so relating a held-out instruction to prior model behavior with uncertainty is hard.
rXNJlCzWCL.method: Conformal maps are learned embedding spaces whose local support is optimized for informative label-conditional conformal prediction while staying anchored to a pretrained semantic representation. The same local support organizes past successes and failures, defines the conformity score, and exposes the evidence around a new instruction.
rXNJlCzWCL.key_idea: Train an embedding space whose local neighborhood support serves simultaneously as training objective, conformity score, and explanation, anchored to a pretrained representation.
rXNJlCzWCL.evidence: Five QA and reasoning benchmarks and three target models, compared with the pretrained representation, frozen-embedding probes, and end-to-end classifiers.
rXNJlCzWCL.claimed_gains: The learned maps improve conformal singleton rate over the pretrained representation in most dataset-model pairs across five benchmarks and three target models while maintaining label-conditional coverage; no figures are stated.
rXNJlCzWCL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the conformal protocol is careful and clean, with label-conditional coverage verified, and that the experiments give useful evidence for instruction-level behavior assessment.
rXNJlCzWCL.main_concern: Novelty over neighborhood-components-style metric learning, assessor models, and conformal training is unclear, and gains over simple baselines are marginal and may reflect benchmark shortcuts.

O7el2Nt4yI.one_liner: A posterior-sampling algorithm for fixed-budget cluster identification with matching lower and upper bounds on the posterior error exponent.
O7el2Nt4yI.problem: Fixed-budget cluster identification from noisy pairwise Bernoulli observations, with unknown means p and q and an unknown number of clusters, lacked an algorithm matching an instance-dependent lower bound.
O7el2Nt4yI.method: The authors prove an instance-dependent lower bound on posterior error for every adaptive sampling rule, with the exponent given by a max-min allocation of weighted Bernoulli KL divergences. Their algorithm combines posterior sampling over neighboring alternatives, an exponential-weights learner over pairs, and vanishing uniform exploration.
O7el2Nt4yI.key_idea: Choose pairs by posterior sampling over neighboring incorrect partitions, with an exponential-weights learner over pairs tracking the max-min KL allocation.
O7el2Nt4yI.evidence: Theoretical lower and upper bounds, plus experiments on synthetic instances and real-world datasets (Birds20 with N=125 per a review).
O7el2Nt4yI.claimed_gains: Posterior error upper bound matches the lower bound at the exponential scale, giving the optimal instance-dependent error exponent almost surely; experiments show competitive performance, no numbers stated.
O7el2Nt4yI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is a strong, clean theory contribution whose matching upper and lower bounds come from an elegant combination of known ingredients.
O7el2Nt4yI.main_concern: The analyzed algorithm needs exact projection that is infeasible at Birds20 (N=125), the approximations used in experiments are not specified, and the guarantees are asymptotic.

NDNNYz5TrG.one_liner: Transformer that encodes each empirical measure as one finite-dimensional order-statistics token, with universal approximation guarantees for measure-to-measure maps.
NDNNYz5TrG.problem: Existing transformer layers for learning with empirical measures need all-to-all particle interactions or expensive optimal transport subprocedures.
NDNNYz5TrG.method: For measures on R, each empirical measure becomes a finite-dimensional token derived from order statistics, with universal approximation for continuous maps on compact classes. For measures on R^d, the construction extends to compact classes of elliptical distributions using finitely many one-dimensional projections.
NDNNYz5TrG.key_idea: Represent each empirical measure by a quantile-vector token, so a standard transformer attends across measures instead of across particles.
NDNNYz5TrG.evidence: Universal-approximation theorems for 1D measures and elliptical classes in R^d, plus preliminary synthetic experiments on learning performance and computational efficiency.
NDNNYz5TrG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the universal approximation guarantees are sound and that the quantile token avoids particle-level attention and optimal transport costs, with efficient implementation and honestly reported synthetic experiments.
NDNNYz5TrG.main_concern: There is a gap between theory and experiments: the synthetic results show no consistent advantage over the simpler Gaussian Moment Transformer, and the method is limited to 1D and elliptical distributions.

F97F54tj13.one_liner: Detects distribution shift in event-camera spiking networks from per-channel statistics of subthreshold membrane potential, using a Multi-Descriptor Deviation score.
F97F54tj13.problem: OOD detection for event-camera SNN object detectors is hard because existing methods depend on model outputs or computation that is unavailable or ill-suited to low-compute deployment.
F97F54tj13.method: Computes simple per-channel statistics of the subthreshold membrane potential and fits the Multi-Descriptor Deviation (MDD) method on clean data only. The authors also introduce Gen1-C, a corruption benchmark on Prophesee Gen1 with six sensor-motivated stress tests at five severity levels.
F97F54tj13.key_idea: Read membrane potentials the SNN already computes and score how far their temporal statistics deviate from clean-data fits, adding no forward or backward pass.
F97F54tj13.evidence: The Gen1-C benchmark with six corruptions at five severities; reviews also mention multiple corruption families, baselines, additional datasets and architectures, and a hardware implementation.
F97F54tj13.claimed_gains: At the highest corruption severity, MDD achieves an AUROC of more than 0.88 on five of the six corruptions using 64-frame score averaging.
F97F54tj13.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find membrane-potential monitoring a sensible, low-cost signal with a disciplined clean-only evaluation protocol and gains over baselines on Gen1-C.
F97F54tj13.main_concern: The added value of spiking dynamics over simpler input or spike-count statistics is not isolated, and the benchmark's realism and generalization to unseen corruption families and other hosts are not shown.

QiFKSiFLD6.one_liner: Dataset of about 100k protein-ligand pairs with six-type interaction maps for benchmarking binding-site localization beyond binary binding prediction.
QiFKSiFLD6.problem: Existing benchmarks test whether and how strongly proteins and ligands bind, not whether models localize binding sites or identify the non-covalent interactions behind recognition.
QiFKSiFLD6.method: InteractBind provides protein-residue and ligand-atom interaction maps for six non-covalent interaction types and protein-similarity-controlled splits, and evaluates whether model-derived interaction maps localize binding sites.
QiFKSiFLD6.key_idea: Score models on residue-level, interaction-type-specific localization maps rather than only on binary binding or affinity labels.
QiFKSiFLD6.evidence: Eight existing sequence-based and interaction-aware models evaluated on binary binding prediction and on binding-site localization.
QiFKSiFLD6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the research question and the comprehensive annotations, including residue-level, interaction-type supervision absent from existing benchmarks.
QiFKSiFLD6.main_concern: Baselines were not trained with a localization objective, so low localization scores may reflect missing supervision, and evidence for recognizing specific interaction types is limited.

ITMfeu805S.one_liner: Two-stage method: a contrastive teacher learns latent state from partial observations, then a student fits port-Hamiltonian dynamics in learned coordinates.
ITMfeu805S.problem: Imposing physical structure on latent dynamics learned from partial, high-dimensional observations is hard because representation learning and physics-aware modeling are coupled.
ITMfeu805S.method: A contrastive teacher jointly learns an encoder and a neural ODE to get predictive state representations from observation histories. A student then learns an invertible nonlinear coordinate transformation and port-Hamiltonian dynamics by matching encoded observed futures.
ITMfeu805S.key_idea: Freeze a contrastively learned latent state, then fit an invertible coordinate change plus port-Hamiltonian dynamics to its encoded futures.
ITMfeu805S.evidence: Ten clean and noisy datasets, with sufficient conditions for recovering the physical state up to a diffeomorphism; reviews note all data are simulated and the largest supervised horizon is 32 steps.
ITMfeu805S.claimed_gains: not stated (abstract reports only competitive or better long-horizon forecasts across ten datasets).
ITMfeu805S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the identification problem meaningful and the separation of representation learning from structured dynamics fitting well motivated.
ITMfeu805S.main_concern: The port-Hamiltonian structure adds little over an unconstrained second-stage student (advantage at 50 steps only 0.002-0.036), and baselines are seen as unequal in capacity and context.

I7PmmIpxb4.one_liner: Plug-in coarse-fine visual memory for robot policies; a learned recall map picks which patches retrieve detail and how far back.
I7PmmIpxb4.problem: Generalist robot policies need history when the current view is insufficient, but compressing history drops details and indiscriminate history conditioning adds irrelevant information.
I7PmmIpxb4.method: STAM combines compressed historical context with directly retrievable visual detail, uses a spatio-temporal recall map to choose which patches access memory and how far back to retrieve, and fuses both memories layerwise without changing the policy backbone. An action-guided three-stage training learns recall from action errors.
I7PmmIpxb4.key_idea: Learn a recall map, supervised only by action errors, that decides per image patch whether and how far back to retrieve fine-grained memory.
I7PmmIpxb4.evidence: Four simulation benchmarks and four real-world robot platforms, with the abstract citing MIKASA-Robo results on pi_0.5 and GR00T N1.5 policies.
I7PmmIpxb4.claimed_gains: On MIKASA-Robo, STAM improves average success by 33.2 and 28.0 percentage points over the original pi_0.5 and GR00T N1.5 policies, respectively.
I7PmmIpxb4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree selective, sparse memory is a reasonable and efficient approach, with gains across multiple benchmarks, VLA policies and real robots.
I7PmmIpxb4.main_concern: Positioning against closely related memory methods (for example MemER, MEM, GMP, MemoryVLA) is weak, making the contribution look incremental.

27HPPxb5wt.one_liner: Controlled comparison of four ViT-S objectives shows latent prediction improves physical probes only when it predicts the next clip.
27HPPxb5wt.problem: Reported JEPA advantages over masked autoencoders on physical systems confound prediction space with time horizon, architecture and training pipeline.
27HPPxb5wt.method: They train architecturally identical ViT-S encoders on three simulations from The Well with four objectives crossing pixel versus latent prediction and current versus next eight-frame clip, then probe all layers for regime parameters and physical quantities.
27HPPxb5wt.key_idea: Cross prediction space (pixels versus latents) with prediction horizon (current versus next clip) in otherwise identical models to isolate which factor helps.
27HPPxb5wt.evidence: Three spatiotemporal physical simulations from The Well, with probes at current and future times across encoder layers and robustness tests.
27HPPxb5wt.claimed_gains: Changing both prediction space and horizon (the Latent-Future objective) lowers probe error for future physical quantities by 43-70%.
27HPPxb5wt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled design that separates prediction space from horizon and find the JEPA-versus-MAE insight useful for scientific forecasting.
27HPPxb5wt.main_concern: The contribution is mainly empirical: the proposed explanation is not tested, active matter behaves differently, and only one architecture (ViT-S) with probe-based evaluation is used.

7lxVAeHiTm.one_liner: Learns continuous latent actions and a diffusion world model jointly from action-free video using adversarial latent regularization.
7lxVAeHiTm.problem: Latent action models learned from action-free video tend to leak future observations into the latent instead of capturing the structure of the action.
7lxVAeHiTm.method: CLAW trains a latent action model and a diffusion-based world model end to end, with adversarial latent regularization preventing the latent from encoding future observations. The world model predicts a distribution over future observations, and the latent actions support imitation from observation and goal-directed planning.
7lxVAeHiTm.key_idea: An adversary penalizes future-frame information decodable from the latent alone, pushing the latent toward action structure while it is trained jointly with a diffusion world model.
7lxVAeHiTm.evidence: Experiments across diverse tasks and embodiments, including a real robot, covering latent action quality, action transfer, imitation, and planning, plus an ablation on four environments.
7lxVAeHiTm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea is simple, easy to add to other methods, and evaluated broadly across many environments and a real robot with strong empirical results.
7lxVAeHiTm.main_concern: Reviewers say the adversarial mechanism is not convincingly validated: removing it lowers measured leakage in three of four environments, controls against VQ or variational bottlenecks are missing, and it may suppress useful action information.

ugQBs0hXdx.one_liner: Retrieves real reference videos, encodes them with V-JEPA2, and injects compact memory tokens into a frozen video diffusion model.
ugQBs0hXdx.problem: Text-to-video models struggle with prompts needing coherent motion, causal interactions or physically plausible evolution because text says what should happen but not how it unfolds.
ugQBs0hXdx.method: PhyMem retrieves prompt-relevant clips, extracts predictive representations with a frozen V-JEPA2 encoder, compresses the spatiotemporal tokens into compact memory tokens, and injects them into the self-attention layers of a frozen backbone through a 33.9M-parameter trainable memory module.
ugQBs0hXdx.key_idea: Use retrieved real-video predictive features (V-JEPA2) as key/value memory in the frozen generator's self-attention, supplying physical dynamics that text does not specify.
ugQBs0hXdx.evidence: Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B backbone, about 0.8K training videos, two physics-focused benchmarks (PhyGenBench and VideoPhy2 per reviews), ablations on shuffled or absent references and retrieval budget, and a small human study.
ugQBs0hXdx.claimed_gains: Improves physical plausibility and physical commonsense under matched inference settings while largely preserving semantic adherence; reviews cite PhyGenBench Final 0.48 to 0.55 and VideoPhy2 PC pass rate 51.7% to 61.7%.
ugQBs0hXdx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that retrieving real physical dynamics is a reasonable complement to text, that training only a small memory interface is practical, and that shuffled-reference ablations support the retrieval benefit.
ugQBs0hXdx.main_concern: Methodological novelty over DiT-Mem is limited (a new feature source and interface), and evaluation covers only Wan2.1-1.3B with few comparisons to other physics-aware methods.

ctcw0MaNfI.one_liner: Self-improving LLM forecasting agent that builds target-relevant proxy tasks, replays them leakage-controlled, and improves strategies from predictive and process feedback.
ctcw0MaNfI.problem: Recursive self-improvement for forecasting faces a feedback deadlock: the target outcome is unknown at prediction time, and backtesting gains on history do not reliably transfer to unresolved targets.
ctcw0MaNfI.method: RSI-FORECASTER constructs target-relevant historical proxy tasks, replays them in a leakage-controlled open-web environment, improves strategies hierarchically with predictive and process feedback, then applies held-out selection and transfers the chosen strategy to the unresolved target.
ctcw0MaNfI.key_idea: Resolve the feedback deadlock with target-relevant historical proxy tasks replayed under leakage control, and select strategies on held-out proxies before transferring to the live target.
ctcw0MaNfI.evidence: Three months of evaluation on two living forecasting benchmarks, including ForecastBench's cross-round leaderboard, with comparisons against other RSI methods and a baseline ensemble.
ctcw0MaNfI.claimed_gains: Ranks second among 400 submissions on ForecastBench's preliminary cross-round leaderboard as of the submission deadline and maintains leading performance on two living benchmarks (further comparison truncated in the abstract).
ctcw0MaNfI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the feedback-deadlock problem is real and that live, pre-outcome evaluation on forecasting benchmarks with information controls gives meaningful evidence for the complete system.
ctcw0MaNfI.main_concern: It is unclear which components drive the gains (no ablation of target adaptation or the selector, compute and search not controlled across compared methods), and overfitting to proxy tasks and the deadlock framing are questioned.

p9UbL2QwHP.one_liner: Open-set cross-network node classification that uses OOD scores on prediction-clustering conflicts to find unknown nodes and guide signed adversarial alignment.
p9UbL2QwHP.problem: In open-set cross-network adaptation, aligning unseen-class target nodes with known source classes causes negative transfer, and existing methods rely on prediction signals while under-using distributional evidence.
p9UbL2QwHP.method: OGSA takes agreement between classifier predictions and prototype-initialized clustering as initial target pseudo-labels. For conflicting nodes, structure-aware OOD scores identify likely unknown nodes, and the refined assignments supervise target predictions and signed domain-adversarial learning.
p9UbL2QwHP.key_idea: Use structure-aware OOD scores to adjudicate target nodes where classifier and clustering disagree, then align only the nodes judged known via signed domain-adversarial learning.
p9UbL2QwHP.evidence: Diverse graph benchmarks with 15 transfer tasks against baselines such as UAGA and GraphRTA, with ablations and a target risk bound.
p9UbL2QwHP.claimed_gains: Competitive performance in known-class classification and unknown-class recognition; reviews note best ACC and H-score on all 15 transfer tasks (no numbers in the abstract).
p9UbL2QwHP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem of negative transfer in open-set graph adaptation is meaningful and the experiments are extensive, with ablations.
p9UbL2QwHP.main_concern: The framework mainly integrates existing techniques (prototype clustering, graph OOD detection, signed adversarial learning), so novelty and the isolated contribution of OOD evidence are unclear.

eOgJWUUuiJ.one_liner: Normative signal-detection model showing optimal costly attention either ramps up with accumulating evidence or fluctuates rhythmically depending on attention cost.
eOgJWUUuiJ.problem: Attention improves performance but is metabolically costly, so it is unclear how a resource-efficient agent should allocate it over time.
eOgJWUUuiJ.method: The authors analyze optimal attention allocation in a signal detection task with attention costs and find two temporal patterns; rhythmic allocation frequency rises with reward magnitude, signal brevity and signal frequency. They argue rhythmic attention emerges when belief updates are dominated by a stable temporal prior.
eOgJWUUuiJ.key_idea: Optimal attention shifts between ramping and rhythmic patterns depending on how attention costs penalize intense focus, with rhythm arising from a prior-dominated belief update.
eOgJWUUuiJ.evidence: A normative signal-detection model with simulated optimal policies across cost functions and task parameters, plus robustness checks to parameter choices (per reviews).
eOgJWUUuiJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper communicates its core result clearly, the ramping versus rhythmic policies are intuitive, and the account may explain attention fluctuations seen in sustained attention tasks.
eOgJWUUuiJ.main_concern: It is a toy model whose results may depend on specific assumptions (cost form, guaranteed minimum signal duration, binary observations), and the model specification and quantitative comparisons are underspecified.

fFbZ3xcTAS.one_liner: Prior-fitted network pretrained across contextual-bandit tasks from LLM responses to estimate policy value in one forward pass without per-task fitting.
fFbZ3xcTAS.problem: Classical off-policy evaluation must be refit for every new logged dataset or reward definition, which is ill-suited to continual deployment with policy shift and reward shift.
fFbZ3xcTAS.method: PFN-OPE is pretrained once on contextual-bandit tasks built from a pool of LLM responses scored by several reward functions. At test time it maps a logged dataset and one sampled target response per prompt to a value estimate in a single forward pass.
fFbZ3xcTAS.key_idea: Amortize off-policy evaluation itself with a prior-data fitted network trained on synthetic tasks containing policy shift and reward shift, instead of fitting a regressor per task.
fFbZ3xcTAS.evidence: HelpSteer2 and UltraFeedback with Qwen, Llama and Gemma policies, with ablations on ground-truth correction and prior task coverage, using automated reward models.
fFbZ3xcTAS.claimed_gains: 2.0 to 9.3 times lower error than the best baselines across all tested configurations on HelpSteer2 and UltraFeedback.
fFbZ3xcTAS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that amortizing off-policy evaluation across changing policies and reward definitions is well motivated and practical, with consistent, broad improvements and informative ablations.
fFbZ3xcTAS.main_concern: Robustness beyond the engineered task prior is unestablished: evaluation uses automated reward models and between-model shifts, lacks a reward-predictor baseline on the same pool and model-selection tests, and transformer scaling to large logs is not discussed.

QDdWiaNkk2.one_liner: Re-evaluates automatic harness evolution for LLM agents against matched-budget test-time scaling baselines and held-out generalization tests.
QDdWiaNkk2.problem: Prior harness-evolution work skips comparison with simple task-level search under matched feedback and inference budgets, and tunes harnesses on verification signals from the same benchmarks it reports on.
QDdWiaNkk2.method: Compares automatic harness evolution with simple test-time scaling and discovery baselines under comparable feedback and inference budgets, and evaluates evolved harnesses on held-out tasks. Also examines long-horizon games as a setting where harness evolution may help.
QDdWiaNkk2.key_idea: Matching feedback and inference budgets across harness evolution and test-time scaling baselines, and testing evolved harnesses on held-out tasks, separates search gains from learned-harness gains.
QDdWiaNkk2.evidence: Terminal-Bench 2.1 experiments with and without test cases, plus long-horizon game experiments (ARC-AGI-3 ablations are mentioned in reviews); reviews say only AHE is run, with its explore agent disabled.
QDdWiaNkk2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the matched-budget controlled comparison, the finding that gains attributed to harness evolution may come from repeated sampling, and the pointer to long-horizon, rich-feedback tasks as a promising setting.
QDdWiaNkk2.main_concern: The critique targets a class of methods but the evidence comes from one variant (AHE with exploration disabled, one rollout per task per iteration), so the negative result may not generalize.

Oj94zxxkDK.one_liner: Clusters reference gradients and selects data stratified by cluster to reduce sampling noise in gradient-based LLM data selection.
Oj94zxxkDK.problem: Gradient-based data selection loses its gains on challenging coding tasks, sometimes falling below random selection, because the target gradient estimated from a limited reference set is noisy.
Oj94zxxkDK.method: SUADS clusters reference gradients, aggregates gradients within each cluster, and applies stratified selection to use more reliable local reference directions. A theorem in a stylized model shows reference uncertainty scales down the expected gain over random selection by a multiplicative factor, independent of selection fraction.
Oj94zxxkDK.key_idea: Aggregate gradients within clusters of reference examples and select stratified across clusters, so each selection uses a local reference direction less affected by finite-sample noise.
Oj94zxxkDK.evidence: Qwen3.5-4B, Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-9B evaluated on MBPP, HumanEval and LiveCodeBench under matched selection budgets, plus a stylized-model theory.
Oj94zxxkDK.claimed_gains: SUADS is the only selection method whose average exceeds random selection in every setting and has the highest average pass@1 under matched budgets; on Gemma-2-9B it matches full-data fine-tuning on average with 5% of the data.
Oj94zxxkDK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the sampling-uncertainty theory an interesting perspective and the method simple, with improvements over baselines including random selection.
Oj94zxxkDK.main_concern: The theory does not explain the clustering gain, since the appendix estimates global-reference gain retention is already near 1 (0.999 and 0.992), so improvements may come from task-scope effects rather than reduced sampling uncertainty.

IyFSQW1RcT.one_liner: Inference-time harness where a controller consolidates, explores, assesses, and dispatches worker computation with persistent memory for long-horizon agentic tasks.
IyFSQW1RcT.problem: As agents take on longer, more complex problems, controlling execution, such as which partial work to build on, whether to start fresh, or when to stop, becomes a task in its own right.
IyFSQW1RcT.method: In agentic meta-reasoning, workers carry out task-level computation while a controller consolidates what the run has established, explores next options, assesses what each is worth under the remaining budget, and dispatches work with context from persistent memory. Between decisions the controller carries only a compact account of the run.
IyFSQW1RcT.key_idea: Separate run control from task work: a controller assesses options under the remaining budget and dispatches workers, carrying only a compact run summary between decisions.
IyFSQW1RcT.evidence: ProgramBench plus other benchmarks spanning abstract reasoning, multi-domain long-horizon reasoning, and proof generation, against production coding agents, research harnesses, and a Direct Control Agent with the same workers and compute budget.
IyFSQW1RcT.claimed_gains: On ProgramBench, meta-reasoning achieves 71.5% with GPT-5.5 against 58.0% for Codex and 67.2% with Opus 4.8 against 65.5% for Claude Code, and on the other benchmarks it gains between 3.6 and 4.2 points over direct control, averaged across three frontier models.
IyFSQW1RcT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem of controlling long-horizon agentic inference is important and well motivated, and that the approach improves over commercial harnesses on the evaluated benchmarks.
IyFSQW1RcT.main_concern: Reviewers say the necessity of the four-stage controller is not shown against a single controller with the same state and memory, and the significance and engagement with prior work are unclear.

lW88UomaDf.one_liner: An LLM judge proposes pivotal trajectory segments, and continuation rollouts verify each before adding credit to its GRPO advantages.
lW88UomaDf.problem: GRPO assigns the same trajectory-level advantage to all policy tokens, so it cannot distinguish consequential decisions from less relevant ones in agentic training.
lW88UomaDf.method: ProVer has an agentic judge contrast successful and failed trajectories in a rollout group to propose a segment potentially responsible for the divergent outcomes, then estimates that segment's advantage from the difference in terminal success rates of current-policy continuations sampled before and after it. Positive estimates are added to the GRPO advantages of tokens within the segment.
lW88UomaDf.key_idea: Use the judge only to choose where to verify, and set the credit bonus from the difference in terminal success rates of continuations before and after the proposed segment.
lW88UomaDf.evidence: Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and SearchQA at two model scales (Qwen3.5-2B and Qwen3.5-4B), with controls such as budget-matched GRPO, random segment selection, and several judge models per reviews.
lW88UomaDf.claimed_gains: ProVer achieves the strongest average performance at both model scales, with relative improvements over GRPO of 9.91% and 7.12% for Qwen3.5-2B and Qwen3.5-4B, respectively.
lW88UomaDf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating judge-based segment selection from outcome-based credit estimation is a sensible design, with solid experiments across two scales, three benchmarks, several judges, and reported costs.
lW88UomaDf.main_concern: Reviewers say gains are not separated from training noise (apparently one training run per setting), the verification step's own contribution is not isolated, and novelty over SPO and CriticSearch-style credit assignment is limited.

58yka6P5sh.one_liner: Self-supervised pretraining that models camera viewpoint change as an SO(3) rotation and warps features into a canonical frame.
58yka6P5sh.problem: Visuomotor policies learned from human demonstrations are brittle to camera viewpoint changes, and existing remedies need rendering pipelines or 3D inputs, or suppress the viewpoint factor so nothing extrapolates viewpoint change.
58yka6P5sh.method: Canonical keeps viewpoint as a recoverable latent factor, modeling viewpoint change as an SO(3) rotation and warping features into a shared canonical frame before an unchanged behavior-cloned policy. Pretraining uses multi-view RGB and camera angle, and at deployment an angle predictor recovers the rotation from the image alone.
58yka6P5sh.key_idea: Keep viewpoint as a latent SO(3) rotation that is predicted from the image and used to warp features into a canonical frame, instead of learning view-invariant features.
58yka6P5sh.evidence: Experiments on MetaWorld and LIBERO-Goal with camera viewpoints unseen in policy training, plus a real-world xArm robot, against multi-view baselines such as ReViWo and VILA per reviews.
58yka6P5sh.claimed_gains: Canonical outperforms the strongest multi-view baseline by 83% and 56% at unseen viewpoints on MetaWorld and LIBERO-Goal, and remains the strongest method at unseen viewpoints on a real-world xArm robot.
58yka6P5sh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicitly warping viewpoint-dependent features into a canonical space is effective, with thorough evaluation on MetaWorld, LIBERO, and a real robot and useful ablations.
58yka6P5sh.main_concern: Reviewers say closely related work such as Sharma et al. (2022) and Canonical Policy is neither discussed nor compared, baseline protocols need clarification, and the method may depend on an available canonical view.

z2rbdvmX49.one_liner: Conditional flow matching learns distributions over parametric variational inequality solution sets, with finite-sample guarantees.
z2rbdvmX49.problem: Parametric variational inequalities must be solved repeatedly across instances, and when solution sets are non-singleton a single prediction discards alternatives useful for downstream criteria such as welfare or robustness.
z2rbdvmX49.method: A conditional flow-matching model learns distributions over PVI solutions, enabling solution sampling and post-hoc selection for unseen instances. Theory translates flow-matching error into Wasserstein distributional, feasibility, and stationarity errors, with finite-sample high-probability bounds covering approximation, optimization, and generalization errors.
z2rbdvmX49.key_idea: Amortize the solver by conditioning a flow-matching generator on the VI parameters to sample from the whole solution set, then select among samples afterward.
z2rbdvmX49.evidence: VI-specific theorems on distributional, feasibility, and stationarity errors, and three benchmarks: Braess traffic equilibria, nonconvex AC optimal power flow, and large-scale electricity-market bidding games with up to a billion pure strategy profiles.
z2rbdvmX49.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that solving many related variational inequalities is a well-motivated problem and that the paper combines theoretical and experimental analysis.
z2rbdvmX49.main_concern: Reviewers say experiments do not show benefits at scale because several benchmarks are toy-sized, and they find the sample-complexity bounds and reliance on an offline VI solver unclear.

RFqz2R4vUj.one_liner: Theory comparing Bayesian ridge and conformal prediction intervals for next-generation reservoir computing, including a high-dimensional phase transition.
RFqz2R4vUj.problem: Uncertainty quantification for efficient forecasting methods such as NGRC is underdeveloped, and it is unclear when Bayesian and conformal intervals agree or differ.
RFqz2R4vUj.method: The paper analyzes Bayesian ridge and conformal prediction intervals for NGRC, showing that in low dimensions their widths are governed by different summaries of the residual distribution, and that in high dimensions regularization creates a tradeoff between estimation variance, shrinkage bias, and posterior uncertainty. It extends the results to quadratic feature maps and, under sufficient conditions, to temporally dependent forecast windows.
RFqz2R4vUj.key_idea: Compare Bayesian and conformal interval widths asymptotically, showing agreement depends on residual shape in low dimensions and on a regularization-driven variance-bias tradeoff in high dimensions.
RFqz2R4vUj.evidence: Theorems and sufficient conditions for quadratic feature maps and temporally dependent windows, supported by simulations and real-data experiments on nonlinear memory-driven systems and diverse real-world time series.
RFqz2R4vUj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives a systematic theoretical comparison of Bayesian and conformal intervals across dimensional regimes, with a clear high-dimensional explanation and candid discussion of limitations.
RFqz2R4vUj.main_concern: Reviewers say the theory relies on strong assumptions (Gaussian data, independent samples, fixed regularization, known noise level) that differ from real NGRC forecasting, and its contribution beyond existing ridge-regression results is unclear.

pBwCfErZ5D.one_liner: Optimizer wrapper that fixes Frobenius norms of weight matrices and their updates, replacing weight decay for Muon or Adam.
pBwCfErZ5D.problem: Matrix-based optimizers such as Muon speed up language model pretraining, but their gains over AdamW shrink as model size and data scale grow under standard constant decoupled weight decay.
pBwCfErZ5D.method: Given a base optimizer such as Adam or Muon, Hyperball sets the Frobenius norms of weight matrices and of their optimizer updates to fixed constants, so weights move on a hypersphere of fixed radius. Per reviews, it constrains attention and MLP matrices while embeddings and normalization gains stay unconstrained.
pBwCfErZ5D.key_idea: Fix the Frobenius norm of each weight matrix and its update to constants, explicitly imposing the fixed-radius hypersphere motion that weight decay only drives toward in equilibrium.
pBwCfErZ5D.evidence: Qwen3-style models up to 1.2B parameters, with a 1.2B duration sweep, a 130M token-budget sweep, and width and depth learning-rate transfer experiments per reviews.
pBwCfErZ5D.claimed_gains: Muon Hyperball achieves 20--30% token equivalent speedup over weight decay baselines on Qwen3 style models up to 1.2B parameters, and improves learning rate transfer across widths and depths.
pBwCfErZ5D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and practical, replacing a weight-decay coefficient with explicit norm control, and that evidence spans several optimizers, model sizes, and learning-rate transfer experiments.
pBwCfErZ5D.main_concern: Reviewers say the speedup is conflated with a better effective learning-rate schedule, with no control matching absolute effective step sizes, and note that prior work such as nGPT also constrains norms.

lAtvtnnHed.one_liner: Predicts action-conditioned 3D robot scene flow from 2D images with a 3D foundation model, enabling kinematics-free inverse control.
lAtvtnnHed.problem: Controlling diverse robotic embodiments is hard because modeling complex robot structures requires significant time, dedicated sensors, and manual labeling.
lAtvtnnHed.method: Act4R builds on a 3D foundation model with a Spatial-Action Encoder that encodes the current 2D robot state and action signals into embeddings of the future 3D state, then decodes current and future embeddings into point maps to estimate action-conditioned scene flow. Spatial-action fusion and a spatial alignment loss train it, and inverse control optimizes the action signal to reach a desired scene flow.
lAtvtnnHed.key_idea: Fuse action embeddings with 3D foundation-model features to predict future point maps, then optimize the action signal to match a target scene flow.
lAtvtnnHed.evidence: A public real-world dataset and synthetic simulator data across various robotic platforms, including a pneumatic soft robot, compared with NJF per reviews.
lAtvtnnHed.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using pretrained geometric priors to predict dense action-conditioned motion for robots without known kinematics is useful, and that Act4R consistently beats NJF in scene-flow prediction and inverse-action estimation.
lAtvtnnHed.main_concern: Reviewers say generalization to out-of-distribution trajectories and real-time control are not evaluated, since inverse control needs iterative optimization and the closed-loop correction budget and latency are unspecified.

byWrQmX9t4.one_liner: Builds a small portfolio of aligned LLMs covering all reward weightings using a structured weight grid, lazy search, and pruning.
byWrQmX9t4.problem: Training, evaluating, and deploying many LLM policies across different reward weights is costly, yet the right balance of competing objectives varies across users and applications.
byWrQmX9t4.method: PALM combines a structured grid of weight vectors, a lazy search that optimizes policies only where needed, and pruning. Given target approximation tolerances, it returns a portfolio that provably contains a near-optimal policy for every weight vector, with an explicit upper bound on portfolio size.
byWrQmX9t4.key_idea: Optimize policies lazily only where needed on a structured weight grid, then prune, to obtain a provable near-optimal cover of all reward weightings.
byWrQmX9t4.evidence: Experiments on RLVR-GSM fine-tuning, HelpSteer LoRA, and decoding-time safety and helpful-assistant methods per reviews, plus scaling to higher-dimensional reward spaces.
byWrQmX9t4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that choosing which reward weights to train and deploy is a practical problem and that the grid, lazy search, and pruning give a simple, policy-method-agnostic approach with theoretical guarantees.
byWrQmX9t4.main_concern: Reviewers say the theory may not hold in the experiments, since a lemma assumes non-negative rewards while HelpSteer rewards are standardized and signed, and baselines such as equal-budget uniform selection and optimistic linear support are missing from the main text.

UhvUzDqm2k.one_liner: Two-stage pipeline generating synchronized multi-view talking videos from a portrait and audio, then reconstructing a full-head Gaussian avatar.
UhvUzDqm2k.problem: 3D talking avatar methods that rely on parametric face models such as 3DMM or FLAME have compact motion representations that limit extreme expressions and facial accessory modeling.
UhvUzDqm2k.method: AudioLift uses generated multi-view videos as the intermediate representation, combining a synchronized multi-view video generation stage with an inconsistency-robust Gaussian reconstruction stage to recover coherent full-head geometry from a single portrait image, without parametric face models or per-instance optimization.
UhvUzDqm2k.key_idea: Replace parametric motion with generated multi-view video, turning audio-driven 4D avatar generation into reconstruction of 3D Gaussians from synchronized views.
UhvUzDqm2k.evidence: Extensive experiments against baselines, with reviews citing a mouth-opening contrast on 16 curated in-the-wild clips and qualitative accessory results.
UhvUzDqm2k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the single-portrait-plus-audio setting is practically valuable and that splitting the problem into multi-view video generation and 3D reconstruction is a clean, carefully engineered design.
UhvUzDqm2k.main_concern: Reviewers say the closest prior art, VASA-3D, is cited but not compared, the method largely combines StableAvatar and FaceLift, and claims about extreme expressions and accessories are under-quantified.

cBDL3Ou0Mt.one_liner: Agentic RL for verified code using a dense reward from discharged proof obligations and an integrity audit against specification weakening.
cBDL3Ou0Mt.problem: Test-based code RL rewards passing tests that leave inputs uncovered, and training against a formal verifier is hard because pass/fail verdicts give little guidance when most attempts fail and models can weaken specifications or add unproved assumptions.
cBDL3Ou0Mt.method: VGA-RL's reward reads the verifier's diagnostics, scoring a candidate by the weighted fraction of proof obligations it discharges plus hidden probes from a reference proof's annotations. An integrity audit outranks the verifier, rejecting candidates that alter the specification or assume what they should prove, and the model acts as an agent against a live verifier over many turns with a frozen proof specialist.
