cBDL3Ou0Mt.key_idea: Reward the weighted fraction of proof obligations the verifier accepts rather than its pass/fail verdict, with an integrity audit that overrides the verifier on weakened specifications.
cBDL3Ou0Mt.evidence: Qwen3 models from 1.7B to 14B and a 35B Qwen3.6 mixture-of-experts model, evaluated on held-out verification for DafnyBench and SWE-Proof against other training signals.
cBDL3Ou0Mt.claimed_gains: Held-out verification on code generation rises from 66.1% to 93.5% on DafnyBench and from 56.3% to 100% on SWE-Proof.
cBDL3Ou0Mt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using verifier diagnostics as a dense reward and adding an integrity audit against reward hacking is a sensible, practical approach to an important problem, with extensive model coverage.
cBDL3Ou0Mt.main_concern: Reviewers say baselines are weak or missing, including an SFT baseline trained only on final proofs, no expert-iteration comparison, and no compute-matched test-time-scaling comparison.

ddTY9xjAY8.one_liner: Federated unlearning that localizes influence per client, sends one minimum-norm correction to every persistent copy, and certifies removal jointly.
ddTY9xjAY8.problem: Federated training leaves persistent model copies on clients, and current unlearning methods edit and certify only the server's global model, so each copy an edit misses returns the withdrawn content through later aggregation.
ddTY9xjAY8.method: LOCUS has each client report the retention cost of a candidate correction and what its copy still carries (Influence Localization), delivers one minimum-norm correction to every client in the correction set and gates a copy out of aggregation until it acknowledges (Correction Propagation), and assigns removal, retention, and application checks to the parties that observe them in one certificate (Divided Verification).
ddTY9xjAY8.key_idea: Run each unlearning step where its evidence lives: clients localize influence, one minimum-norm correction reaches every copy behind an acknowledgment gate, and split checks form one certificate.
ddTY9xjAY8.evidence: Experiments across two benchmarks, three deployments, five unlearning objectives, and seven published federated unlearning protocols.
ddTY9xjAY8.claimed_gains: LOCUS corrects 92--99% of the copies in the correction set (the comparison with server-side methods is cut off in the abstract).
ddTY9xjAY8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that persistent client copies are an important and under-explored problem and that executing each step where its evidence lives, with an acknowledgment gate and split certificate, is well motivated and empirically effective.
ddTY9xjAY8.main_concern: Reviewers say a broadcast-all control with the same gate nearly matches LOCUS, the persistent-copy premise is questioned, and the boundary with Lethe and veriFUL is unclear.

YwxDP9ffIz.one_liner: Introduces a distributed separation oracle model and gives query- and communication-efficient algorithms for linear programming over many servers.
YwxDP9ffIz.problem: Distributed optimization over s constraint sets accessed one at a time should need fewer than the naive s queries per round of simulating a separation oracle for the intersection, and prior communication bounds for distributed linear programming can be improved.
YwxDP9ffIz.method: In the distributed separation oracle model one queries a separation oracle for one of s constraint sets at a time, and the paper solves linear programs for constant dimension d with O(s + L log s) queries, where L is the bit precision. It also gives communication algorithms in the coordinator and blackboard models that improve on Vempala, Woodruff, and Wang (2020).
YwxDP9ffIz.key_idea: Solve the distributed convex program exactly by resolving only O(d) subproblems that involve subsets of servers, giving O(s + L log s) queries.
YwxDP9ffIz.evidence: Query-complexity theorems for the bit-limited and general models, an Omega(s + L) lower bound, and coordinator and blackboard communication theorems, with synthetic experiments in dimension 3 per reviews.
YwxDP9ffIz.claimed_gains: Linear programming for constant d with O(s + L log s) queries instead of s queries per round, and O(s d^3 L + poly(d log n) L sqrt(s)) communication in the coordinator model and O(sd) + (L log n + log^2 n + sqrt(s)) log(sd) poly(d) in the blackboard model.
YwxDP9ffIz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is fundamental and the results are sound and broad, covering query and communication complexity across several settings, with an Omega(s + L) lower bound close to the upper bound.
YwxDP9ffIz.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical motivation for the oracle model, which seems tailored to the results, and note that the bounds need fixed small dimension while experiments are synthetic with d=3.

STf4IB4IDc.one_liner: Proves that a shared-attention Transformer trained jointly on token-selection and XOR tasks learns token selection first, then XOR.
STf4IB4IDc.problem: Existing theory analyzes attention-based token selection and nonlinear composition separately, leaving open whether joint training alone can induce a structured acquisition order (an implicit curriculum).
STf4IB4IDc.method: The paper studies a stylized multi-task Transformer in which a softmax attention layer shared across tasks feeds task-specific ReLU heads, trained by SGD on a fixed mixture of a token-selection task and an XOR task with informative tokens among distractors. Both tasks and all parameters update in parallel with no imposed curriculum; the abstract's statement of the mechanism is cut off.
STf4IB4IDc.key_idea: Prove that under joint SGD on a fixed task mixture with a shared softmax attention layer, token selection is learned before XOR, with no imposed curriculum.
STf4IB4IDc.evidence: A proof of the learning order for the stylized model, plus experiments on synthetic and MNIST-based tasks and on Pythia-6.9B, Amber-7B, and OLMo-2-7B checkpoints per reviews.
STf4IB4IDc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives a rigorous, carefully structured analysis of simultaneous training of shared attention and ReLU heads, with experiments that partly support the predicted learning order.
STf4IB4IDc.main_concern: Reviewers say the theory relies on restrictive structural assumptions and a reduced architecture, leaving a gap to modern LLMs, and that the basic phenomenon is not new.

zcS9GUXMF1.one_liner: Federated multimodal unlearning that excises update directions unique to forgotten data across both modalities, then locks them against later training.
zcS9GUXMF1.problem: Federated multimodal unlearning is hard because modalities and client gradient subspaces are entangled: current methods cannot break the cross-modal reconstruction pipeline caused by bilinear coupling and do not separate unlearn-exclusive update directions from those shared with remaining clients.
zcS9GUXMF1.method: EASE updates the visual and language branches simultaneously so neither can reconstruct the cross-modal alignment alone, uses Cosine-Sine decomposition to filter update directions unique to unlearning while preserving those shared with remaining clients, and applies a direction-selective unlearn lock so later training does not revert toward the removed directions.
zcS9GUXMF1.key_idea: Use principal-angle (Cosine-Sine) decomposition to split unlearning updates into directions exclusive to the forgotten data versus shared with retained clients, excising the former in both branches.
zcS9GUXMF1.evidence: Experiments across three datasets, three backbone architectures, and three unlearning scenarios against nine baselines, plus appendix theory and LiRA privacy tests per reviews.
zcS9GUXMF1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important and under-studied, and that decomposing gradient directions into forget-exclusive and shared components with principal angles is well conceived, with comprehensive experiments and ablations.
zcS9GUXMF1.main_concern: Reviewers say novelty is incremental because the components are standard tools, the most relevant prior work is missing from the baselines, and the theory does not establish the empirical unlearning objective.

0yRVNbUjFM.one_liner: Generative model learning finite-time Poisson-birth and Binomial-death transitions in count space for one- or few-step generation.
0yRVNbUjFM.problem: Most diffusion and flow models are designed for continuous or categorical data, so generating the high-dimensional count data common in science requires many sequential model evaluations.
0yRVNbUjFM.method: Count Flow Map learns stochastic transitions over finite time intervals using Poisson births and Binomial deaths, preserving nonnegative integer counts without a predefined maximum. The transition models are trained to match local birth-death dynamics and to stay consistent across step sizes, with a derived bound on generation error.
0yRVNbUjFM.key_idea: Parameterize finite-time transitions as Poisson births plus Binomial deaths and train them for consistency across step sizes with the local birth-death dynamics.
0yRVNbUjFM.evidence: Simulations, single-cell drug perturbation prediction, and neural population forecasting, with baselines including Count-FM per reviews, plus a generation error bound.
0yRVNbUjFM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the stochastic transition kernel naturally extends count flow matching to finite-time generation, with convincing low-NFE results on synthetic and real-world datasets and clear presentation.
0yRVNbUjFM.main_concern: Reviewers say the individual contributions are not isolated, the model uses more parameters than Count-FM without matched-capacity comparisons, and the research increment is moderate, with neural forecasting showing undercoverage.

ILt4R26tdS.one_liner: Off-policy RLVR objective minimizing a log-mean-exp contrast of KL-adjusted rewards among same-prompt responses, avoiding learner-to-behavior importance weights.
ILt4R26tdS.problem: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards often trains on responses from a different, possibly stale behavior policy, and correcting the mismatch with importance weights can have high variance for long responses.
ILt4R26tdS.method: GGPO minimizes a log-mean-exp contrast of KL-adjusted rewards among responses to the same prompt, derived from KL-regularized policy optimization so that its on-policy population loss is exactly the KL-regularized optimality gap. A reference refresh schedule is analyzed through exact Gibbs-target composition.
ILt4R26tdS.key_idea: Replace importance-weighted policy gradients with a log-mean-exp contrast of KL-adjusted rewards within each prompt's response group, whose on-policy loss equals the KL-regularized optimality gap.
ILt4R26tdS.evidence: Derived guarantees under coverage assumptions, and mathematical-reasoning experiments on five benchmarks against GRPO and AGRO under training-inference mismatch, fixed offline data, and controlled policy staleness.
ILt4R26tdS.claimed_gains: In an ablation, fixed-reference GGPO scores 32.96 on the five-benchmark problem-weighted average versus 46.58 with the default refresh schedule, and GGPO outperforms GRPO and AGRO under training-inference mismatch and on fixed offline data.
ILt4R26tdS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the objective is principled and justified both analytically and empirically, with a clear relation to AGRO, simple implementation, and robustness under policy staleness and offline training.
ILt4R26tdS.main_concern: Reviewers say experiments are limited to small dense models on single-turn math with simulated staleness, practical benefits over GRPO and AGRO are unclear, and some bounds may be vacuous at the experimental settings.

F9RSsSAFP8.one_liner: Controlled comparison showing a VLM teacher helps visual document retrievers most by judging mined hard negatives, not by enriching positives.
F9RSsSAFP8.problem: Visual document retrievers are trained contrastively with one labelled positive per query, and because labels are incomplete, mined negatives are often relevant, so training pushes the retriever away from relevant pages.
F9RSsSAFP8.method: With student, data, optimizer, and evaluation fixed, the study compares supervision signals from a VLM teacher: teacher-judged hard negatives, score distillation over those candidates, description alignment, and attention grounding. A ten-annotator audit checks label incompleteness and teacher reliability.
F9RSsSAFP8.key_idea: Spend the VLM teacher on judging the retriever's mined negative candidates, filtering false negatives, rather than on enriching the positive with attention or descriptions.
F9RSsSAFP8.evidence: Controlled comparisons on ViDoRe v2 and v3 with a ColQwen2.5-3B late-interaction student and a smaller second student, teacher-free control rules, and a ten-annotator audit.
F9RSsSAFP8.claimed_gains: Teacher-judged hard negatives raise ViDoRe v2 nDCG@5 from 55.2 to 62.6 and score distillation over those candidates raises it to 63.0, while at identical training compute the teacher's judgement adds 4.1 points on v2 and 1.7 on v3 over the best teacher-free rule for choosing negatives.
F9RSsSAFP8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is controlled, with student, data, optimizer, and evaluation fixed and a teacher-free control suite that isolates which negatives the teacher picks, and that the human audit supports the label-incompleteness claim.
F9RSsSAFP8.main_concern: Reviewers say the scope is narrow (one student family, one corpus, one teacher family, 2-3 seeds per arm), so effect sizes are imprecise and rankings depend on how each supervision strategy was adapted.

M0U0oFBtCG.one_liner: Forks tree-structured RLVR rollouts just before the step where the model's answer belief shifts most, detected by lightweight probes.
M0U0oFBtCG.problem: Tree-structured RLVR can afford only a few forks per chain, and forks placed where the outcome is already settled yield agreeing siblings and almost no credit signal, while existing placement relies on structure or next-token entropy.
M0U0oFBtCG.method: Belief-shift branching formalizes fork placement as locating pivots of the chain's value curve, reading the model's answer belief at candidate boundaries and forking just before the step where consecutive beliefs diverge most. Three instantiations need no step-level supervision: a black-box probe, a logit-lens depth profile, and a learned activation direction used only in validation before RL training.
M0U0oFBtCG.key_idea: Score each candidate step boundary by how much the model's answer belief changes across it, and fork before the largest change instead of by structure or entropy.
M0U0oFBtCG.evidence: Validation of selectors against Monte-Carlo value curves, then RL experiments on mathematics and code with several model families (OLMo, Qwen3-4B, and Nemotron per reviews), tree-budget ablations, and compute-cost estimates.
M0U0oFBtCG.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract only reports that the probe costs about 1% of step compute on mathematics and under 5% on code when run inside the rollout engine.
M0U0oFBtCG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing fork placement as locating pivots of the value curve is the right reframing, and that validating selectors against Monte-Carlo value curves before RL and testing several model families strengthens the evidence.
M0U0oFBtCG.main_concern: Reviewers say the RL evidence is thinner than claimed, with single seeds on some models, gains on Qwen3-4B within seed spread, and unclear compute-matched efficiency.

6RIl9QzFfV.one_liner: Multi-turn LLM router trained on pivotal steps, found by counterfactual rollout trees, where model choice changes final outcomes.
6RIl9QzFfV.problem: Agent inference costs accumulate across model calls, and the value of choosing among models is concentrated at a small subset of steps, so treating every step equally wastes supervision and cost.
6RIl9QzFfV.method: The paper identifies pivotal steps, where candidate models at the same agent history lead to substantially different final outcomes, through counterfactual rollout trees, and uses their model comparisons to guide data collection, router training, and inference.
6RIl9QzFfV.key_idea: Mark a step pivotal when swapping the model at the same history changes the final outcome, and train the router on those steps only.
6RIl9QzFfV.evidence: Six interactive benchmarks with a 473-task evaluation suite, plus ablations such as pivotal-only versus all-state training per reviews.
6RIl9QzFfV.claimed_gains: The router matches or outperforms the strongest fixed-model baseline on five of six interactive benchmarks and reduces total inference cost by 47.8% across the 473-task evaluation suite.
6RIl9QzFfV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the pivotality concept cleanly separates task difficulty from routing value, and that training on only the pivotal 32.7% of states beating all-state training gives direct evidence for the data-selection idea.
6RIl9QzFfV.main_concern: Reviewers say pivotal labels depend on the candidate model pool and costly rollout trees, and that comparison with the closest sequential routers such as DialRouter, MTRouter, and Hera is missing.

vJgG20sjea.one_liner: Shows weight tying elicits iterative computation in looped transformers through gradient pooling across repeated block uses.
vJgG20sjea.problem: Looped transformers learn iterative, staircase-like solutions that progress roughly one step per iteration, but it is unclear how weight tying leads to such solutions.
vJgG20sjea.method: The study trains models with a hop curriculum on directed permutation traversal, tracking progress per iteration and layer with linear probes and causal interventions. It gives each iteration its own copy of the block and varies how much of each copy's update comes from the pooled gradient, and also trains on a single iteration's gradient.
vJgG20sjea.key_idea: Weight tying works through gradient pooling, summing gradients across repeated block uses, which favors a reusable one-hop operation that is composed across iterations.
vJgG20sjea.evidence: Models trained on directed permutation traversal with a hop curriculum, analyzed with linear probes, causal interventions, and gradient-routing ablations that vary the amount of pooling.
vJgG20sjea.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the research question is clear, the task allows exact tracking of intermediate states, and the gradient-pooling intervention is novel and well designed.
vJgG20sjea.main_concern: Reviewers say the experiments do not isolate gradient pooling from weight reuse, since the two are inseparable, and that evidence is indirect and limited to one synthetic task with small models and few seeds.

jDeUV5xUt6.one_liner: Critic-free RLVR loss from Policy Mirror Descent via Bellman equations, replacing GRPO's importance ratio with a smoothed complementary-token ratio
jDeUV5xUt6.problem: RLVR for LLM reasoning typically relies on value/critic estimates of intermediate states, which are costly and can be unreliable over long reasoning trajectories.
jDeUV5xUt6.method: Uses the Bellman equations to reformulate Policy Mirror Descent into a trajectory-level objective that needs no intermediate state values, then approximates it to obtain the BPO loss, which swaps GRPO's importance-sampling ratio for a smoothed ratio of complementary token probabilities.
jDeUV5xUt6.key_idea: Bellman telescoping converts the PMD objective into a trajectory-level one without intermediate values; the loss uses a smoothed ratio of complementary token probabilities in place of GRPO's ratio.
jDeUV5xUt6.evidence: A proof that the trajectory-level objective has the same unique optimum as the PMD objective, plus experiments on long chain-of-thought and multi-turn tool-integrated mathematical reasoning against GRPO-ClipHigher, GSPO, CISPO, and DPPO, with ablations.
jDeUV5xUt6.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract only says BPO achieves the highest average accuracy over the evaluated benchmarks among all compared methods.
jDeUV5xUt6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the critic-free motivation, the simple memory-light update, the martingale/Bellman equivalence proof, and a reasonably broad RLVR comparison with ablations.
jDeUV5xUt6.main_concern: The equivalence theorem covers only the exact trajectory-level objective, not the practical BPO loss built with further approximations, and the loss closely resembles Kimi k1.5 and VIMPO objectives that are not compared against.

FG476Lwadh.one_liner: Black-box teacher distillation into a natural-language skill document by contrasting paired teacher and student rollouts, with no weight updates.
FG476Lwadh.problem: Parameter-based distillation of frontier agents into smaller models needs access to student weights and extra training compute, and encodes the transferred knowledge implicitly in the parameters.
FG476Lwadh.method: D-Skill analyzes paired teacher and student rollouts to find behavioral divergences and agreements, then consolidates the lessons offline, with any compatible skill-update backend, into a skill document given to the student at inference time. It uses only fixed trajectories, with no labels, further environment interaction, or weight updates.
FG476Lwadh.key_idea: Contrasting paired teacher-student trajectories yields natural-language lessons about where behavior diverges, which are consolidated offline into a skill document the student reads at inference.
FG476Lwadh.evidence: Experiments on SpreadsheetBench-Verified, ALFWorld, and chess puzzles across multiple teacher-student pairs, compared with one-epoch and multi-epoch SFT, plus an ablation of skills extracted from student, teacher, and paired trajectories.
FG476Lwadh.claimed_gains: Closes 82%-95% of the teacher-student gap without touching model weights, outperforms one-epoch SFT baselines, stays competitive with multi-epoch SFT, and lowers inference cost per task by 5.7x-8.3x versus the teacher.
FG476Lwadh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea of contrasting paired teacher-student rollouts simple and clear, and credit consistent improvements across benchmarks and teacher-student pairs, including gains over one-epoch SFT.
FG476Lwadh.main_concern: The method is heuristic and depends on a strong analyst model and prompts, so the source of gains is not isolated, and SFT comparisons are not matched on compute or tested for generalization.

Y4FVfTdczG.one_liner: 400K-dialogue multimodal dataset and 400-dialogue benchmark testing whether unified models track and update dialogue state across turns.
Y4FVfTdczG.problem: Existing unified multimodal datasets are mostly single-turn, and in multi-turn ones many turns can be solved independently, so stateful interaction that requires tracking, updating, and realizing evolving dialogue state is under-supervised and under-evaluated.
Y4FVfTdczG.method: YANAMI-400K has 400K multi-turn multimodal dialogues (more than 2M images, 2.6M turns) across Multi-Image Fusion, Image Editing, World Modeling, and Visual Reasoning; YANAMI-Bench has 400 dialogues that jointly score Dialogue State Understanding and Visual Realization.
Y4FVfTdczG.key_idea: Dialogues are built so later turns depend on earlier state, and the benchmark scores state understanding separately from visual realization to expose the gap between them.
Y4FVfTdczG.evidence: Models from several categories are scored on YANAMI-Bench, BAGEL is fine-tuned on YANAMI-400K and checked on external image-editing benchmarks such as GEdit-Bench-EN, and a human-rating study checks the automatic judge.
Y4FVfTdczG.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract (it reports dataset scale only); reviews cite BAGEL's YANAMI-Bench score rising from 65.02 to 78.25 after fine-tuning.
Y4FVfTdczG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that multi-turn stateful interaction is a practically important problem and that the large dataset and human-verified benchmark, with state understanding separated from visual realization, are valuable resources.
Y4FVfTdczG.main_concern: Novelty is not clearly differentiated from prior multi-turn work such as Visual Dialog, MMDU, MMCR, and WEAVE, and overall benchmark scores are not comparable across model types.

LHR9v7Ba56.one_liner: Rating model that judges video camera-motion alignment from frames plus optical-flow and global-motion cues, guiding test-time prompt refinement.
LHR9v7Ba56.problem: Test-time scaling for camera-motion control needs a reliable rating model, but geometry-based methods struggle when object motion dominates and VLMs fine-tuned on real video do not transfer to synthetic clips.
LHR9v7Ba56.method: CamRM feeds video frames together with motion cues to a VLM (built on Gemini and Qwen), with a training-free agentic variant CamRM-A, and serves as the rater in a loop that generates a clip, rates its alignment, and revises the prompt.
LHR9v7Ba56.key_idea: Providing inexpensive optical-flow and global-motion measurements as text alongside frames grounds a VLM's judgment of camera-motion alignment.
LHR9v7Ba56.evidence: A benchmark of 1,064 human-labelled real and synthetic videos, cue ablations on Qwen and Gemini, and a motion-guided refinement loop judged by humans on Veo 3.1 and Omni Flash.
LHR9v7Ba56.claimed_gains: CamRM reaches 80.7% accuracy and improves balanced accuracy over the strongest baseline by 6.6%, with consistent improvements of over 10% across Gemini and Qwen; in the refinement loop it improves human-judged alignment by 13.2% for Veo 3.1 and 18.4% for Omni Flash at 2.2x the generation cost.
LHR9v7Ba56.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark shows that rating skill on real video does not transfer to generated clips, and that swapping in CamRM improves delivered videos, with cue ablations showing gains beyond fine-tuning.
LHR9v7Ba56.main_concern: Generalization to unseen video generators is untested because training and testing use the same two generator families, and some reported numbers differ across figures and tables.

rFdoUHHQGj.one_liner: Benchmark of 2,640 videos over 110 tasks testing goal-directed egocentric manipulation in video generation, with a reference-free judge.
rFdoUHHQGj.problem: Existing video-generation benchmarks cover single short actions or step-by-step instructions, leaving multi-step physical reasoning toward high-level goals in egocentric video underexplored.
rFdoUHHQGj.method: Given an initial scene image and a high-level goal, models must generate an egocentric video of a hand carrying out the task; Ego2ActJudge is a reference-free pipeline that scores task completion and physics plausibility and is checked against human consensus.
rFdoUHHQGj.key_idea: Goal-only prompts without step instructions force models to infer and execute full action sequences, scored by a reference-free judge that separates task completion from physics plausibility.
rFdoUHHQGj.evidence: Six video generators are evaluated on 2,640 videos from 110 real-world tasks varying in clutter and step count, and the judge is checked against human ratings with positive and negative controls.
rFdoUHHQGj.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports no performance numbers beyond benchmark size, only that generated videos often skip or partially execute steps and that Ego2ActJudge aligns better with human consensus than baselines.
rFdoUHHQGj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that goal-level evaluation of egocentric video generation is well motivated and that separating task completion from physics plausibility, with positive and negative controls, is a useful design.
rFdoUHHQGj.main_concern: Ego2ActJudge is unreliable for individual videos (r=0.69 with humans, 22-point MAE, about 24-point physics overestimate, detects only 7-10% of temporal violations), and the 15-second generation cap confounds results.

xwKOY8kYGT.one_liner: Bayesian time warping with monotonic piecewise-linear priors, GP regression, and blocked HMC-within-Gibbs, fitting warps per neuron.
xwKOY8kYGT.problem: Trial-to-trial timing heterogeneity in neural dynamics, often tied to latent events such as decision time, limits trial-averaging, and a shared population warp can hide single-neuron timing differences.
xwKOY8kYGT.method: Combines efficient Gaussian process regression for templates, a prior over monotonic piecewise-linear warping functions, and a parallel blocked Hamiltonian Monte Carlo-within-Gibbs sampler to learn a full posterior over parameters, including warping-function posteriors for individual neurons.
xwKOY8kYGT.key_idea: A prior over monotonic piecewise-linear warps, combined with scalable GP templates and parallel blocked HMC-within-Gibbs sampling, gives full posteriors over warps for single neurons.
xwKOY8kYGT.evidence: Synthetic data where template and warps are recovered and hidden subpopulation structure appears, plus rat orbitofrontal cortex recordings from a temporal wagering task, with PSIS-LOO model comparison.
xwKOY8kYGT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem matters for neural data analysis, the Bayesian approach is principled with an efficient sampler, and synthetic results recover templates and warps.
xwKOY8kYGT.main_concern: Real-data evidence rests on a single rat OFC dataset, and the assumption of one template per neuron across all trials limits use in multi-condition experiments.

vfpdaLnIu8.one_liner: Activation steering through a learned encoder-decoder that maps hidden states to task-structured coordinates, applies transformations there, and maps back.
vfpdaLnIu8.problem: Steering by adding a fixed vector imposes translation and ignores task structure such as the cyclic order of weekdays, so it cannot compose fractional steps or close the cycle.
vfpdaLnIu8.method: An encoder-decoder interface maps a frozen LM's hidden states into task-structured coordinates, applies transformations there, and returns model-readable states; coordinates are either prescribed (weekdays) or induced by matching geometry-derived output distributions, and a steerer-aligner system is built for modular arithmetic.
vfpdaLnIu8.key_idea: Steer in a learned task-coordinate space where operations such as rotation act, then decode back to hidden states, instead of adding a fixed vector in activation space.
vfpdaLnIu8.evidence: Weekday, number, and color tasks showing rotation, composition, cycle closure, and emergent geometry, perturbation controls, and a modular arithmetic system compared with parameter-matched PEFT baselines (including LoRA and Prefix Tuning) across eight models.
vfpdaLnIu8.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract only says the modular-arithmetic steerer-aligner outperforms parameter-matched PEFT baselines across eight models.
vfpdaLnIu8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea intuitive and the experiments extensive across models, baselines, and ablations, including repeated-step, cycle-closure, and failure-case analyses.
vfpdaLnIu8.main_concern: The arithmetic gains are hard to attribute to the learned interface because the system uses operand-level supervision and an explicit modular-addition rule that the PEFT baselines lack, and the practical need for structured steering is unclear.

xy7UqEXvHA.one_liner: Robots share region-tagged, versioned attention states from a frozen VLM planner so teammates reuse computation instead of re-encoding rooms.
xy7UqEXvHA.problem: Robots that share a semantic map still each spend computation encoding the same regions in their onboard planners.
xy7UqEXvHA.method: Each room has an owner that encodes it using only a shared prefix and that room's evidence; the resulting attention state is tagged with room identity, evidence version, and owner, and receivers accept it only when tags match the current map, then use it directly through the planner's native attention, with no training.
xy7UqEXvHA.key_idea: Per-room attention states tagged with room identity, evidence version, and owner are accepted by receivers only when tags match the current map, so reused states equal self-computed ones.
xy7UqEXvHA.evidence: Experiments on HM3D and MP3D with teams of two to four robots compared against cached re-perception and a centralized shared cache, plus real-world navigation experiments.
xy7UqEXvHA.claimed_gains: With two robots, attention messages reduce planner GPU time by 45% compared with cached re-perception, and across teams of two to four robots they match the computational cost of a centralized shared cache while keeping planning onboard.
xy7UqEXvHA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the redundant planner computation problem is well motivated and that explicit message validation cuts planner GPU time (about 45%) with comparable navigation performance.
xy7UqEXvHA.main_concern: Novelty over existing KV-cache reuse work (Prompt Cache, EfficientNav, KVCOMM) is unclear, with no comparison against KVCOMM-style correction or CacheBlend-style recomputation.

8VY24YVrIj.one_liner: Neural operator transformer that tokenizes CAD NURBS patches and predicts physical fields at arbitrary query points, skipping meshing.
8VY24YVrIj.problem: Meshing CAD geometry before simulation is expensive, brittle under geometric variation, often manual, and lossy, and existing AI surrogates still rely on meshes, point clouds, or voxels that approximate the geometry.
8VY24YVrIj.method: Formalizes CAD-to-physics surrogate modeling as operator learning from sequences of parametric NURBS patches to function spaces of physical fields, using a NURBS-native tokenization and predicting continuous fields and engineering quantities at arbitrary query locations.
8VY24YVrIj.key_idea: Parametric NURBS patches (control nets and knot vectors) are tokenized directly as transformer input, and fields are decoded continuously at arbitrary query locations.
8VY24YVrIj.evidence: Validated on automotive and aircraft aerodynamics benchmarks (AhmedML and WindsorML in the abstract; reviews also cite HiLiftAeroML and DrivAerML), with an inverse-design case checked by re-running the original CFD setup.
8VY24YVrIj.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract (it is cut off before results); a review cites about 20% lower surface-pressure error than AB-UPT on HiLiftAeroML.
8VY24YVrIj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning operators directly from CAD is a well-motivated representation idea that scales to industrial geometries and is tested on several sizable CFD datasets, with inverse-design results verified by CFD re-runs.
8VY24YVrIj.main_concern: The no-meshing and representation-invariance claims look overstated: volume anchors still come from CFD volume meshes, different patch splits cause substantial error, and the source of gains versus design-parameter baselines is unclear.

XrEbjPHYoe.one_liner: On-policy self-distillation where each token's target is the KL projection nearest the student that satisfies a teacher-information budget.
XrEbjPHYoe.problem: On-policy self-distillation fine-tuning (SDFT) always distills toward the full demonstration-conditioned teacher, giving no control over how much demonstration information transfers at each prediction state.
XrEbjPHYoe.method: At each token, iSDFT selects the distribution closest to the current student that satisfies a prescribed teacher-information constraint, giving a closed-form exponential target with a locally determined tilt, and anchors the student to its frozen base policy to limit cumulative drift.
XrEbjPHYoe.key_idea: A per-token KL I-projection onto a teacher-information budget gives an exponentially tilted target whose tilt is set by the budget, plus anchoring to the frozen base policy.
XrEbjPHYoe.evidence: Four LLM backbones and two specialisation tasks versus vanilla SDFT and other baselines, retention on the original SDFT benchmark suite, ten additional mathematics, coding, and competition-mathematics benchmarks, and ablations of the scheduled target and anchor.
XrEbjPHYoe.claimed_gains: Improves vanilla SDFT in 7 of 8 model-task settings and matches it in the remaining one; 73% of retention evaluations stay within 0.5 points of the base model versus 52% for the strongest baseline, with the largest mean improvement on all ten additional benchmarks.
XrEbjPHYoe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem and motivation are clear, the KL I-projection gives a sound mathematical foundation, and experiments across four backbones and many benchmarks show gains with good retention.
XrEbjPHYoe.main_concern: Continual-learning evidence is thin (a single two-task sequential study), and ablations do not isolate token-wise information control from simpler teacher warmup or tuned adaptive interpolation.

S5zuWHaImI.one_liner: Evolves a router and specialist programs in one search, merging branches by aligning specialists on the requests they handle.
S5zuWHaImI.problem: One shared program for heterogeneous requests leaves the division of work implicit in source-code search, while a separate program per request family fixes that division in advance.
S5zuWHaImI.method: Adaptive-GEPA evolves a router and a library of specialist programs under one search budget, with router instructions, specialist descriptions, and program code kept as human-readable text edited from feedback; when combining branches it aligns specialists by the requests they handle and inherits descriptions together with programs.
S5zuWHaImI.key_idea: Specialists from different search branches are aligned by the validation requests they actually handled, so descriptions and programs are inherited together during merging.
S5zuWHaImI.evidence: A fixed mixture of four task families with a Qwen3-8B run (651 test requests) compared against GEPA's full-program adapter and GRPO, plus a GPT-4.1 run; the final method is evaluated with a single seed.
S5zuWHaImI.claimed_gains: Family-mean test score rises from 52.6 to 70.6, versus 62.5 for GEPA's full-program adapter and 54.0 for GRPO at a nominal budget of 18,000 scored calls, and routing matches the task partition on all 651 test requests.
S5zuWHaImI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly learning routing and specialist programs, with request-based alignment when merging branches, targets a practical heterogeneous-workload problem and improves over single-program GEPA on the mixed workload.
S5zuWHaImI.main_concern: The gain is not isolated from execution-profile choices and merging design: the GEPA-FPA-ALL comparison changes both structure and profiles, aligned-merging ablations are missing, and results use one seed on one task mixture.

FKbF3CIszY.one_liner: Latent-based music source separation model that extends cross-source interaction and a sparse-supervision training recipe to isolate 12 stems.
FKbF3CIszY.problem: Most music source separation systems use the four-stem convention (drums, bass, vocals, other), and moving to 12 stems demands sensitivity to sparse, imbalanced, and spectrally entangled instrument sources.
FKbF3CIszY.method: DeFormer combines an architecture that extends cross-source interaction during separation with a training recipe adapted to sparse and skewed supervision; reviews describe a 15k-song dataset annotated to expand the task from 4 to 12 stems.
FKbF3CIszY.key_idea: An architecture that extends cross-source interaction during latent separation, paired with training objectives adapted to sparse and skewed supervision across 12 stems.
FKbF3CIszY.evidence: A held-out internal set with four baselines retrained at 12 targets, the MoisesDB and MUSDB18-HQ benchmarks, component ablations, and a human listening study with expert annotators.
FKbF3CIszY.claimed_gains: Reaches 6.59 dB mean cSDR over 12 targets, 1.06 dB ahead of the closest of four baselines retrained at the same target count, with a notable gap in subjective audio quality and adjacent source bleeding in a human study.
FKbF3CIszY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating 12 stems end-to-end in a single model, the component ablations, the thorough perceptual evaluation, and the new 12-stem data and demo page.
FKbF3CIszY.main_concern: Novelty is incremental, with gains over BSRoformer marginal and mostly from losses and engineering, and the dataset origin and internal held-out evaluation protocol are poorly documented.

mZWct2zYMF.one_liner: Small VLMs edit scientific figures as TikZ code, trained on 391K revision-mined edit pairs and then RL.
mZWct2zYMF.problem: Scientific figure editing is largely unexplored, and existing approaches rely on costly proprietary agentic systems, focus on evaluation, or build training supervision from synthetically generated edits.
mZWct2zYMF.method: Mines 391K plausible TikZ edit pairs from arXiv, GitHub, and TeX SE and infers 781K edit instructions with a VLM conditioned on rendered figures and TikZ code (DaEdiTikZ), then trains compact Qwen3.5-based models (4B and 9B) jointly on image-to-TikZ reconstruction and instruction-conditioned editing, followed by RL with rewards for rendered fidelity and edit application.
mZWct2zYMF.key_idea: Naturally occurring figure revision trajectories supply edit-pair supervision, and RL with separate rewards for rendered fidelity and edit application refines models trained on joint reconstruction and editing.
mZWct2zYMF.evidence: DaEdiTikZ-Bench (690 human-refined instances), automatic evaluation against baselines, and human evaluation with 9 annotators and 4,320 ratings.
mZWct2zYMF.claimed_gains: The 9B model is above all tested baselines in automatic evaluation, and in human evaluation with 9 annotators and 4,320 ratings it is above GPT-5.6-Sol and on par with a further system (the abstract is cut off).
mZWct2zYMF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that mining human-authored revisions addresses a practical data bottleneck, the human-refined benchmark is valuable, and EdiTikZ-9B-RL scores highest among the evaluated models.
mZWct2zYMF.main_concern: About 50% of the inferred training instructions contain at least one error, and the effect of this noise and of figure-pair selection on training is not quantified.

yyPDGf8fN9.one_liner: Small trusted commit layer: alarms name their repair calls, and agents sign medical measurements only when evidence preconditions hold.
yyPDGf8fN9.problem: LLM agents running medical imaging pipelines explain away quality signals and sign plausible but wrong measurements, and runtime enforcement blocks actions without saying what evidence would make a blocked measurement reportable.
yyPDGf8fN9.method: MedGauge is a small commit layer in which observation channels compute evidence without executing the stage they audit, sources sharing an origin count as one witness, each alarm names the call that clears it, and a commit protocol accepts a report only when preconditions checked on the tool-call record hold.
yyPDGf8fN9.key_idea: Sign-off authority moves from the agent to a small trusted program whose alarms name the repair call that clears them, with acceptance checked on the tool-call record.
yyPDGf8fN9.evidence: A benchmark of 1,068 cases spanning cardiac MRI, abdominal CT, and chest radiography, tested with several reasoners and ablations of observation channels, repair instructions, and commit enforcement.
yyPDGf8fN9.claimed_gains: Signs no wrong value across the 812 covered fault-and-reasoner combinations of its two primary reasoners, and across four reasoners releases none of 416 conflicts that the available evidence cannot resolve.
yyPDGf8fN9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important, that separating reasoning from commit authority is a good design, and that the ablations show gains in both safety and usable output.
yyPDGf8fN9.main_concern: Evaluation relies mostly on injected errors and covered fault types (54 of 62 actual CT measurement errors fall outside coverage), and there is no direct comparison with ToolGate or AgentSpec-style enforcement.

InGCsIAFlz.one_liner: Research harness whose outer loop curates context and picks the next objective, trained by actor-critic over meta-reasoning decisions.
InGCsIAFlz.problem: Long-horizon research needs meta-reasoning about what to investigate next, but those decisions are embedded in long execution traces and their consequences are delayed, which makes them hard to learn.
InGCsIAFlz.method: MIRA is a hierarchical harness whose outer loop curates context from a persistent Git-based research state and selects the objective for the next inner-loop execution agent; MIRA-AC pretrains the LM as a generative critic that forecasts expected remaining return from partial research states, then uses the same model as actor and critic in single-rollout asynchronous policy optimization over meta-reasoning decisions.
InGCsIAFlz.key_idea: Isolating the outer-loop decision of what to investigate next lets one model act as its own critic of expected remaining return and receive policy-gradient updates only on those decisions.
InGCsIAFlz.evidence: IMOProofBench Advanced with GPT-5.5, neural-architecture hill-climbing, and four autoresearch environments, with Qwen3.6-27B-Instruct trained as MIRA-AC and a token-matched continuation control.
InGCsIAFlz.claimed_gains: On IMOProofBench Advanced MIRA raises GPT-5.5's performance from 67.1% to 100%, and in neural-architecture hill-climbing it discovers improvements to both Residual Matrix and Loop Transformers.
InGCsIAFlz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the decision-level formulation is concrete and backed by broad results, with MIRA-AC improving outcomes over untrained MIRA across the autoresearch environments and a useful token-matched control.
InGCsIAFlz.main_concern: Evidence on reliability and generalization is limited: one trained policy per configuration, training and evaluation reuse task identities, and single-environment MIRA-AC regresses on BNLearn (48 vs. 76 solved).

XSjPe6NrqH.one_liner: Controlled benchmark of seven SSL methods from five paradigms on time-series anomaly detection, classification, and forecasting under matched budgets.
XSjPe6NrqH.problem: The benefits of self-supervised pre-training for time series are under-investigated and often confounded by inconsistent experimental controls.
XSjPe6NrqH.method: Benchmarks seven representative methods from five SSL paradigms under parameter- and data-matched budgets, comparing linear probing and fine-tuning against non-pre-trained controls, and distills the results into evaluation and development guidelines.
XSjPe6NrqH.key_idea: A common backbone with parameter- and data-matched budgets and non-pre-trained controls isolates whether SSL pre-training itself, not experimental setup, drives downstream gains.
XSjPe6NrqH.evidence: Seven methods across anomaly detection, classification, and forecasting on a Transformer backbone pre-trained on the Monash corpus, with linear-probing, fine-tuning, random-feature, and from-scratch controls, plus depth scaling on three forecasting datasets.
XSjPe6NrqH.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract reports substantial gains in anomaly detection, effective initializations for classification under fine-tuning, and limited to no advantage in forecasting.
XSjPe6NrqH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is systematic and well controlled, with matched baselines and multiple adaptation protocols that give useful guidance on when time-series SSL transfers.
XSjPe6NrqH.main_concern: Generality is limited: conclusions rest on a single Transformer architecture, depth scaling covers only three forecasting datasets with one seed, and some paradigms are represented by only one method.

D0V9QM7SFU.one_liner: Hybrid diffusion-LLM decoding that runs parallel diffusion and switches to autoregressive repair only on high-coupling, failure-prone token spans.
D0V9QM7SFU.problem: Autoregressive decoding gives high quality but is sequential, while diffusion LLMs decode in parallel but often degrade, with errors stemming from a few high-coupling tokens poorly suited to simultaneous updates.
D0V9QM7SFU.method: At inference FlexDLLM alternates between a diffusion mode that decodes in parallel while identifying high-risk positions and an AR mode that revises those tokens conditioned on the global denoising state; per reviews it uses two LoRA adapters on a shared backbone, trained with o3 error annotations and Qwen3-4B-Instruct repairs.
D0V9QM7SFU.key_idea: Learned triggers flag high-risk positions during parallel diffusion decoding, and a switched-in autoregressive mode revises only those spans conditioned on the global denoising state.
D0V9QM7SFU.evidence: Experiments on LLaDA 1.0 over six benchmarks spanning mathematical reasoning, code, and multiple-choice tasks, with comparisons to ReMeDi and ReMDM, a vanilla SFT baseline, trigger ablations, and wall-clock latency and memory measurements.
D0V9QM7SFU.claimed_gains: not stated numerically in the visible abstract (it is cut off at 'It improves accuracy over the'); it claims FlexDLLM marries the performance of AR with the speed of diffusion.
D0V9QM7SFU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find spending sequential computation only on a few difficult spans intuitive, with learned triggers beating random and low-confidence ones and clear gains over the original LLaDA on reasoning, coding, and multiple-choice tasks.
D0V9QM7SFU.main_concern: Gains are not isolated from teacher supervision, since training relies on o3 annotations and Qwen3-4B-Instruct repairs and the vanilla SFT baseline lacks clearly matched teacher data, and only LLaDA 1.0 is tested.

yPQE25by4V.one_liner: Benchmark and method for routing LLMs by execution environment, using an offline agent that compiles environment-property extractors.
yPQE25by4V.problem: Query-only LLM routers overlook that the preferred model for an agentic task can change with available tools, data scale, and execution feedback even when the query is fixed.
yPQE25by4V.method: EARoute pairs queries with varied environments (tools, data scale, interface organization, feedback) while holding query, answer, and evaluation fixed; the method uses an offline environment-understanding agent that explores environments and compiles routing-relevant properties into reusable extractors that give compact descriptions with no LLM call at routing time.
yPQE25by4V.key_idea: An offline agent writes reusable extractor programs that condense large heterogeneous environments into compact descriptions a router can use without an LLM call at routing time.
yPQE25by4V.evidence: EARoute covers 16k query-environment pairs from seven datasets spanning question answering, coding, and tool use, with a repeated-execution check on 3,000 pairs and comparisons of environment-representation baselines such as hand-crafted extractors.
yPQE25by4V.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract gives no router performance numbers, only that environmental changes can reverse model preferences for the same task.
yPQE25by4V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled benchmark isolates a real limitation of query-only routing and that the environment-representation findings are insightful.
yPQE25by4V.main_concern: The benchmark uses predefined environment knobs with limited realism (only two candidate models, unexplained sourcing of distractor resources), and the agent-compiled extractors are not cleanly separated from the specificity of the representation baseline.

JIBPfGq1AO.one_liner: Online conformal prediction on graphs combining a global threshold with kernel-based local correction and a mutual-information nonconformity score.
JIBPfGq1AO.problem: Marginal coverage guarantees do not say where prediction errors occur on a graph, so different neighborhoods can have very different reliability even when aggregate coverage hits its target.
JIBPfGq1AO.method: GLocalCP is an online CP framework for inductive node classification and edge prediction that uses a nonconformity score based on mutual information from Monte-Carlo dropout predictions and augments a global online threshold with a kernel-based local correction that propagates coverage feedback among similar graph queries.
JIBPfGq1AO.key_idea: A kernel-weighted correction of the global online threshold propagates coverage-error feedback among similar graph queries, with prediction sets scaled by MC-dropout mutual-information uncertainty.
JIBPfGq1AO.evidence: Theory giving pathwise O(N^-1/2) marginal calibration error without exchangeability or stationarity and an O(N^-1/2) graph-localized guarantee for the exact-kernel form, plus experiments on seven node-classification and seven edge-prediction benchmarks.
JIBPfGq1AO.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says GLocalCP keeps coverage near the target while consistently reducing graph-local calibration error on seven node-classification and seven edge-prediction benchmarks.
JIBPfGq1AO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that local reliability beyond marginal coverage is a meaningful problem on graphs and that combining a global online threshold with kernel-based local feedback is intuitive, with clear ablations over 50 seeds.
JIBPfGq1AO.main_concern: The local-calibration metric closely mirrors the method's own objective and the baselines are not online methods, and the theory covers the exact kernel while experiments use random Fourier features.

ZJsdzprrDB.one_liner: Latent flow matching with repulsion-guided sampling generates multiple valid solution branches of high-dimensional bifurcating physical systems.
ZJsdzprrDB.problem: At a symmetry-breaking bifurcation one input admits multiple equally valid solutions, which violates the one-to-one assumption of most learned physical surrogates.
ZJsdzprrDB.method: Bi-FORK generates complete trajectories through latent flow matching, preserving space and time coherence, and uses repulsion-guided sampling to recover distinct solution branches in a single amortized pass; per reviews, an autoencoder compresses the high-dimensional field into the latent space.
ZJsdzprrDB.key_idea: Flow matching in an autoencoder latent space generates whole trajectories, while repulsion (particle) guidance pushes samples apart so distinct branches are recovered in one pass.
ZJsdzprrDB.evidence: Buckling beams, mechanical metamaterials, and Allen-Cahn phase separation, with discretizations up to 260,000 points, evaluated with multimodal metrics such as MCon-MAE and per-input JSD.
ZJsdzprrDB.claimed_gains: Recovers the multimodal solution structure while scaling several orders of magnitude beyond prior approaches, with discretizations up to 260,000 points; a review cites about 18x faster inference than STFlow on Beam3D.
ZJsdzprrDB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the one-to-many bifurcation problem is under-explored and well posed, and that latent flow matching with particle guidance scales to large grids where baselines are infeasible.
ZJsdzprrDB.main_concern: The closest predecessor (Hendriks et al., equivariant flow matching for bifurcations) is not compared, and coverage and JSD metrics partly measure the guidance objective against a small set of reference modes.

l1ixaTpsKD.one_liner: Lifelong knowledge editing that picks layers per edit via Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion and projects gradient updates onto weight null-space.
l1ixaTpsKD.problem: Lifelong editing methods modify a fixed set of layers for all new knowledge, which reduces flexibility and increases catastrophic forgetting, and they require access to previous knowledge and extensive preprocessing for data statistics.
l1ixaTpsKD.method: LOKI selects layers dynamically with the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion and projects gradient updates onto the null-space of the model weights, so it needs no stored previous knowledge, memory module, or additional parameters.
l1ixaTpsKD.key_idea: Per-edit layer selection with the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion, plus projecting gradient updates onto the null-space of the model weights instead of that of stored old-knowledge activations.
l1ixaTpsKD.evidence: Experiments on Llama-3, Mistral, and GPT-J across ZsRE, SelfCheckGPT, and Temporal, compared with AlphaEdit, WISE, and GRACE, with edit sequences of up to 1k edits.
l1ixaTpsKD.claimed_gains: Achieves up to a 14% improvement in average accuracy over existing approaches.
l1ixaTpsKD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the practical motivation of avoiding stored activations and memory modules, the layer-selection proxy, and strong results across models and datasets.
l1ixaTpsKD.main_concern: The null-space theorem does not establish that historical knowledge is preserved (the stated inclusion does not imply the projection leaves old features unchanged), and the evidence stops at 1,000 edits.

x9msPF2MuD.one_liner: Simulated urban benchmark measuring VLM agent safety when the world keeps moving during inference and action execution.
x9msPF2MuD.problem: Embodied-agent safety evaluations mostly ignore decision latency, yet an action that looks safe at observation time can become unsafe before execution as pedestrians and vehicles move.
x9msPF2MuD.method: RT-SAFE combines navigation tasks with moving actors, environmental hazards, and traffic rules in a simulator where the world evolves throughout inference and action execution, and it records safety events separately during inference and during action execution.
x9msPF2MuD.key_idea: Inference latency is built into a continuously evolving simulation, so decision quality and decision latency are scored together and safety events are logged by phase.
x9msPF2MuD.evidence: Eight VLMs evaluated across difficulty levels and execution modes, with matched static and real-time evaluations, a seed analysis, and RL versus behaviour-cloning results.
x9msPF2MuD.claimed_gains: Benchmark findings rather than method gains: in the hardest setting only 0.7% of episodes finish without a safety event, and matched static and real-time task completion is 91.3% and 94.1% while real-time execution increases collisions by 12.3x.
x9msPF2MuD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that real-time embodied safety is an important evaluation gap and that the matched static/real-time design, with eight VLMs and simulator-derived event categories, gives interpretable results without an LLM judge.
x9msPF2MuD.main_concern: The static versus real-time comparison is confounded by different timing prompts, and collision counts lack controls for stationary-agent exposure, pedestrian avoidance, and repeated-contact counting.

O0eayhNGip.one_liner: Two-sided GPTQ with Kronecker-factored Hessians made cubic-cost via anti-diagonal parallelism and recursive divide-and-conquer.
O0eayhNGip.problem: Two-sided GPTQ-style rounding that captures output-channel correlations is costly: BoA uses a large number of sequential steps and YAQA still has quartic total cost.
O0eayhNGip.method: FastKron combines anti-diagonal parallelism with a recursive divide-and-conquer construction, is modular over the base quantizer and the Hessian estimator, and adds an efficient technique for computing the Hessian approximations.
O0eayhNGip.key_idea: Anti-diagonal parallelism combined with recursive divide-and-conquer reorders two-sided adaptive rounding to O(m+n) sequential steps while producing the same output.
O0eayhNGip.evidence: Complexity analysis, a proof (Theorem 2.1) that the recursive and anti-diagonal variants preserve the underlying two-sided procedure's output, and runtime benchmarks against GPTQ's core rounding and the earlier anti-diagonal implementation; reviewers note no end-to-end LLM quantization results.
O0eayhNGip.claimed_gains: For an m x n weight matrix, uses O(m+n) sequential steps and reduces total work from O(m^2n^2) to O(mn(m+n)), matching the cubic scaling of GPTQ.
O0eayhNGip.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the quartic-to-cubic reduction is a clear algorithmic improvement that provably preserves the underlying algorithm and is orthogonal to the choice of base quantizer.
O0eayhNGip.main_concern: There are no end-to-end quantization results on representative LLMs, and no direct comparison with GPTQ-2D, which also reaches cubic-time two-sided rounding.

NZ78mRBqgv.one_liner: Benchmark of 155 multi-session trajectories tracing how poisoned information propagates through five agent memory systems, plus a poison optimizer.
NZ78mRBqgv.problem: Memory gives LLM agents an attack surface where malicious instructions seen in one session are stored, then retrieved and acted on in later sessions, and the effects vary across memory architectures.
NZ78mRBqgv.method: MemoryDojo traces the lifecycle of poisoned information (insertion, retrieval, persistence, propagation, downstream behavior) with 155 multi-session long-horizon trajectories across four domains and five memory systems, and adds a memory-aware poison optimization process.
NZ78mRBqgv.key_idea: A fixed attack is run against interchangeable memory systems over many sessions, with lifecycle metrics separating insertion, retrieval, persistence, and downstream effects.
NZ78mRBqgv.evidence: Evaluation of five memory systems on 155 trajectories of up to 60 sessions, scored with an LLM judge, plus a comparison of the memory-aware optimizer against baselines.
NZ78mRBqgv.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract only says all memory systems are susceptible to poisoning with substantial variation, and that the memory-aware optimizer increases poisoning efficacy.
NZ78mRBqgv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark targets an important memory-security risk and that its longitudinal, lifecycle-level metrics across five memory systems give more insight than a single attack success rate.
NZ78mRBqgv.main_concern: Memory systems differ in retrieval budgets and configuration, so lower attack success may reflect less information reaching the agent, and both the novelty over prior memory-poisoning work and the contribution of memory-aware optimization are unclear.

AYe8Ec8oAo.one_liner: Jacobian-aligned featurizer that identifies planted compositional features inside a transformer where reconstruction-based sparse autoencoders fail.
AYe8Ec8oAo.problem: Reconstruction objectives may recover a basis that merely reconstructs activations rather than the intermediate features a network composes, and nothing guarantees that a reconstruction-trained featurizer isolates them.
AYe8Ec8oAo.method: Plants a ground-truth feature DAG inside a transformer through per-layer supervision to make feature identification measurable, then constrains the featurizer dictionary to features relevant to downstream computation by pressuring them to align with the Jacobian; the approach is also applied to DINOv3.
AYe8Ec8oAo.key_idea: Pressuring featurizer dictionary elements to align with the Jacobian ties features to downstream computation, rather than relying on reconstruction alone.
AYe8Ec8oAo.evidence: A synthetic transformer with a planted Boolean feature DAG compared against reconstruction-based featurizers including SAEs and supervised controls, plus experiments on DINOv3 with interventions across 668 linked feature pairs.
AYe8Ec8oAo.claimed_gains: not stated numerically in the abstract; on the synthetic model the featurizer identifies the ground-truth basis and planted hierarchy where baselines could not, while a review cites SAE reconstruction accuracy of about .999 but a Hungarian F1 of .05.
AYe8Ec8oAo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question of whether reconstruction identifies computation features is well posed and the planted-DAG setup makes the failure measurable, with an intuitive objective supported by controls and interventions.
AYe8Ec8oAo.main_concern: The advantage over the closest methods (Jacobian SAEs and gradient SAEs) is unclear because neither is compared, and nothing validates that Jacobian pressure recovers the actual circuit rather than matching feature values.

5BEO6qQYVA.one_liner: Training-free multi-agent LLM framework inducing communication topology from recipient-specific refinement relations among agents' reasoning states.
5BEO6qQYVA.problem: Existing multi-agent communication relies on task or query information or overall agent assessments, which do not identify which reasoning states can usefully correct a particular peer.
5BEO6qQYVA.method: In LoRIT, agents assess how their current reasoning states can correct or complete one another, and these local directional relations induce a global communication structure (built with strongly connected components and transitive reduction, per reviews) that evolves with reasoning, without a global agent ranking or a graph-level objective.
5BEO6qQYVA.key_idea: Pairwise assessments of how one agent's reasoning can correct another's yield a directed refinement graph, condensed into strongly connected components, that sets who communicates with whom.
5BEO6qQYVA.evidence: Experiments across diverse reasoning and coding tasks with weak and strong LLM backbones against single-agent and multi-agent baselines such as G-Designer, TopoDIM, MacNet, and SelfOrg, plus token-cost analysis and a pairwise update study.
5BEO6qQYVA.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract reports broad improvements over single-agent and multi-agent baselines, and says that with stronger refinement assessment, groups of smaller models match or exceed larger single-agent models.
5BEO6qQYVA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that recipient-specific refinement is a sensible basis for communication that a single agent ranking cannot express, and that evaluation across tasks and model scales shows generally consistent gains.
5BEO6qQYVA.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate the benefit of the communication mechanism or the SCC-based readout, since a baseline with the same agents and readout model is missing, and token cost exceeds several baselines.

x0p9eA7vZN.one_liner: Optimization risk bounds for two-layer Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks trained by clipped mini-batch DP-SGD with temporally correlated noise.
x0p9eA7vZN.problem: Theory for DP-SGD with temporally correlated noise is limited, especially for non-convex networks, because existing arguments break under temporal dependence, projection, and active clipping.
x0p9eA7vZN.method: Proves optimization risk bounds for two-layer KANs under clipped mini-batch DP-SGD with correlated noise, using shifted and auxiliary dynamics, a weighted empirical loss, and a high-probability localization argument, then derives population risk guarantees via algorithmic stability.
x0p9eA7vZN.key_idea: Shifted and auxiliary dynamics, a weighted empirical loss, and a high-probability localization argument repair the conditional-centering, cross-iteration cancellation, and gradient-structure steps that correlated noise and clipping break.
x0p9eA7vZN.evidence: Theorems with explicit dependence on temporal correlation, clipping, mini-batch sampling, and network width, plus experiments on synthetic data and MNIST testing the predicted effect of temporal correlation, and a population-risk application via algorithmic stability.
x0p9eA7vZN.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports theoretical results only: for a fixed noise multiplier, temporal correlation reduces the leading noise terms and the clipping threshold enters essentially through an effective step size.
x0p9eA7vZN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is valuable to the DP field and that the technical ideas (shifted iterate, weighted loss, localization) address the identified failure points of existing arguments.
x0p9eA7vZN.main_concern: Scope is narrow (two-layer KANs with only the first layer trained and logistic loss), and the benefit of correlation is shown at a fixed noise multiplier rather than at matched privacy budgets under mini-batch calibration.

Qn3raWg2t7.one_liner: Binding-affinity predictor whose output is an exact sum of signed ligand-atom-residue contact terms over twelve channels, context-rescaled.
Qn3raWg2t7.problem: Structure-based affinity predictors return one number with post-hoc explanations of contested reliability, while empirical scoring functions give each physical term one global weight regardless of local context.
Qn3raWg2t7.method: PACT decomposes predicted affinity exactly into signed ligand-atom-residue contributions in pK over twelve interaction channels, with local chemistry and pocket context rescaling each contribution, and evaluates the stability of contributions under model retraining and contact removal.
Qn3raWg2t7.key_idea: Each named contact term keeps its prescribed sign and chemical basis while a learned local-context factor rescales its magnitude, so the prediction is an exact additive sum.
Qn3raWg2t7.evidence: A leakage-reduced split compared with strong baselines (including PIGNet2), with stability checks of contributions under model retraining, small geometric perturbations, and removal of high-ranked contacts.
Qn3raWg2t7.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says PACT matches the accuracy of the strongest baselines evaluated while producing faithful and reproducible contributions.
Qn3raWg2t7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the intrinsic, exactly additive decomposition in affinity units is more direct than post-hoc attribution, with contributions that are stable under retraining and consistent with contact removal.
Qn3raWg2t7.main_concern: Evidence shows faithfulness to the model but not physical meaning or design utility, and baselines were not uniformly tuned, including a PIGNet2 implementation that differs from the original.

nrgo0M6vmS.one_liner: Diffusion policy for online RL using the Q-gradient as score, preconditioned by Q-gradient covariance across parallel sampling chains.
nrgo0M6vmS.problem: Conventional diffusion policies for online RL rely on separately trained score networks and do not adapt exploration to the geometry of the action-value landscape.
nrgo0M6vmS.method: Approximates the score by the gradient of the learned Q-function, motivated by Boltzmann exploration, and adds a state-dependent preconditioner built from the covariance of Q-gradients across parallel sampling chains with no additional network evaluations, giving structured anisotropic exploration.
nrgo0M6vmS.key_idea: Replace the learned score network with the Q-gradient, and rescale both guidance and noise by a diagonal covariance of Q-gradients across parallel chains as a curvature proxy.
nrgo0M6vmS.evidence: Evaluation on Gymnasium benchmarks (six MuJoCo tasks per a review) against diffusion-based and standard off-policy RL baselines, with a theoretical analysis resting on an error assumption for the Q-gradient approximation.
nrgo0M6vmS.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says it attains the highest aggregate normalized return among diffusion-based and standard off-policy RL baselines on Gymnasium benchmarks.
nrgo0M6vmS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the actor-free, geometry-aware formulation is practical and clearly presented, with a low-overhead preconditioner and strong aggregate normalized performance.
nrgo0M6vmS.main_concern: Substituting the clean Q-gradient for the noise-dependent score rests on an error assumption that is not shown to hold, and novelty over existing Q-gradient sampling and preconditioning methods is unclear.

bZXUddyKmp.one_liner: Fast-weights-in-fast-weights test-time-training layer: chunk-parallel first layer plus token-level delta-rule output layer with feature transport.
bZXUddyKmp.problem: Practical test-time training evaluates every gradient in a chunk at chunk-entrance weights, discarding the effect of earlier within-chunk updates, and what this approximation loses is not well understood.
bZXUddyKmp.method: Block-level backward error analysis identifies the leading-order gap between sequential and mini-batch TTT as a causal interaction term that splits into four layer-wise parts for a two-layer fast-weight MLP. FF-TTT keeps the first layer as a chunk-level fast weight and makes the output layer a token-level delta-rule memory computed with a chunkwise WY solve, plus a causal linear-attention feature-transport pass.
bZXUddyKmp.key_idea: Recover the output-layer parts of the omitted within-chunk interaction: the delta-rule memory by a chunkwise WY solve, the first-layer influence by causal feature transport.
bZXUddyKmp.evidence: Backward error analysis with a proof that the design matches the sequential output-layer update through second order for small step sizes, plus language-model experiments at 340M, 760M, and 1B scales against LaCT and Transformer baselines on zero-shot benchmarks with throughput and memory comparisons.
bZXUddyKmp.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract (it is cut off); a review reports average zero-shot gains over LaCT of 0.51, 0.49, and 0.60 points at 340M, 760M, and 1B.
bZXUddyKmp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the backward-error-analysis framing is rigorous and the design follows directly from it, decomposing the omitted interaction into parts that can be recovered while keeping chunk parallelism.
bZXUddyKmp.main_concern: Gains over LaCT are small (0.5 to 0.6 points) with no seeds or error bars, and little ablation shows which of the several simultaneous changes drives them.

fzxETbxmjw.one_liner: Controllability-evaluation query design that sets non-swept attributes from conditional distributions, scoring feasibility, obedience, realism, and novelty jointly.
fzxETbxmjw.problem: Controllability evaluations take request feasibility for granted, and the dominant OFAT-mu query design ignores attribute correlations, issuing requests that rarely or never occur in the data, so generators are penalized for infeasible queries.
fzxETbxmjw.method: Introduces a closed-form measure of query atypicality and COFAT, a family of correlation-aware query designs that set non-swept attributes from their conditional rather than marginal distribution, within a framework that jointly scores feasibility, obedience, realism, and novelty.
fzxETbxmjw.key_idea: Setting non-swept attributes by their conditional rather than marginal distribution keeps queries near the data's correlation structure, which a Mahalanobis-radius measure of atypicality quantifies.
fzxETbxmjw.evidence: A synthetic generator with known obedience, plus three real tasks (lesion inpainting, lesion insertion, and molecule generation) compared against seven baseline query designs.
fzxETbxmjw.claimed_gains: For a synthetic generator that is perfectly obedient on feasible requests, switching from OFAT-mu to COFAT raises measured obedience from 0.15 to 0.99.
fzxETbxmjw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the OFAT limitation under correlated attributes is real and that COFAT is a simple, intuitive fix inside a comprehensive evaluation framework, with consistent gains over OFAT-mu across domains.
fzxETbxmjw.main_concern: Mahalanobis radius measures statistical atypicality rather than true infeasibility, and the evidence is thin: one generator per task, no seed variation or significance tests, and close results against other correlation-aware designs.

rVXjEd0dmE.one_liner: Benchmark of 820 expert-written problems needing several coordinated cognitive operations, scored by rubrics on a calibrated IRT scale.
rVXjEd0dmE.problem: LLM benchmarks that raise difficulty by escalating knowledge demands conflate memorization with capability, while knowledge-free abstract reasoning benchmarks divorce reasoning from the practical contexts in which it matters.
rVXjEd0dmE.method: GIM has 820 original expert-authored problems (615 public, 205 private), each requiring coordination of several cognitive operations over broadly accessible knowledge, with rubric-decomposed scoring (median 6 judged criteria); models are scored by fitting a judge-aware continuous-response 2PL item response theory model to judge-scored data from 53 test configurations and five LLM judges.
rVXjEd0dmE.key_idea: Problems are authored to require coordinating several cognitive operations over accessible knowledge, and a calibrated judge-aware 2PL IRT scale puts new models on a shared ability axis.
rVXjEd0dmE.evidence: 203,800 epoch-averaged prompt-judge cells (over 1M judge-scored observations) from 53 test configurations and five LLM judges, with a balanced public-private split as a contamination diagnostic.
rVXjEd0dmE.claimed_gains: not stated as performance gains; the abstract reports construction figures (820 problems, 615 public and 205 private, median 6 criteria, 203,800 cells, 53 configurations, five judges) and a released calibrated scale.
rVXjEd0dmE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the human-authored, partly held-out problem set that targets integration rather than obscure knowledge, and the rubric-decomposed scoring and careful dataset construction.
rVXjEd0dmE.main_concern: The central claim that difficulty comes from integration is not directly tested (no single-operation ablation or comparison showing GIM measures more than general reasoning), and a reviewer flags numerical inconsistencies in text and figures.

2edihBesnJ.one_liner: Common training and evaluation framework comparing flow-map language-model distillation recipes across quality metrics, training budgets, and inference settings.
2edihBesnJ.problem: A distillation recipe's apparent advantage can depend on how quality and computation are measured, so recipe comparisons made under one metric, update count, or inference budget may not hold under another.
2edihBesnJ.method: DistillScope trains and evaluates flow-map LM distillation recipes (including semigroup and Lagrangian distillation) in one framework, varying quality criteria, training budgets (equal updates versus measured time), and inference computation, with initialization and objective ablations and an exposure-matched sampling control.
2edihBesnJ.key_idea: The unit of comparison is a trained checkpoint at a stated inference budget, quality criterion, and cost convention, so reversals across metrics and budgets become visible.
2edihBesnJ.evidence: Controlled comparisons on masked OpenWebText and short-form LM1B (length 128) using external perplexity, MAUVE, degeneration checks, and equal-update versus equal-time accounting, with 2-3 seeds for headline results.
2edihBesnJ.claimed_gains: Findings rather than gains: semigroup distillation achieves lower external perplexity than Lagrangian distillation while their ordering reverses under MAUVE, accounting for measured training time reverses a recipe advantage seen at equal updates, and extra inference computation lets the same student pass degeneration checks it fails at tighter budgets.
2edihBesnJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that comparing recipes under explicit quality, training-cost, and inference-budget conventions is a valuable framing, and that the metric reversals are concrete and informative.
2edihBesnJ.main_concern: The flow-map configurations are not shown to be well tuned (PSD reaches PPL 620.1 versus 104.5 for released SDTT), and headline claims rest on 2-3 seeds without statistical significance.

yWr2a5z1sp.one_liner: Benchmark of 32 prediction tasks from six U.S. household surveys testing whether LLMs predict household economic behavior and policy responses.
yWr2a5z1sp.problem: Existing evaluations of LLMs as models of household decision making cover few surveys and outcomes and do not study how households adjust to changing economic conditions.
yWr2a5z1sp.method: HouseholdBench unites 6 U.S. household surveys into 32 numeric, categorical, and probabilistic prediction tasks on consumption, income, labor, expectations, and housing, gives LLMs past behavior, demographics, and macroeconomic conditions, and evaluates 13 LLMs against a no-change baseline and a gradient-boosted tree model.
