yWr2a5z1sp.key_idea: Harmonized survey tasks that include policy-response settings compare LLM predictions with no-change and gradient-boosted-tree baselines across numeric, categorical, and probabilistic outcomes.
yWr2a5z1sp.evidence: 13 proprietary and open-weight LLMs evaluated on 32 tasks against a no-change baseline and XGBoost, with bootstrap standard errors, bias analysis, and fine-tuning plus aggregation of 16 predictions for a 4B open-weight model.
yWr2a5z1sp.claimed_gains: Most LLMs outperform the no-change baseline, with the best LLM lowering error for numeric outcomes by 12.2%; gradient-boosted trees rank first across most tasks, and fine-tuning plus aggregating 16 predictions per observation lets a 4 billion parameter open-weight model match proprietary models on baseline tasks with numeric and probabilistic outcomes.
yWr2a5z1sp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark's scope (six established surveys, 32 tasks, 13 LLMs) is a substantial step beyond prior work, with careful data harmonization and honest reporting that XGBoost wins.
yWr2a5z1sp.main_concern: The abstract overstates results (12.2% is for the best LLM while XGBoost reduces error by 18.9%, and the 4B match holds only on eight baseline numeric tasks), and no code or benchmark release is provided.

2oXQBpAs9J.one_liner: Green's function as a sum of offset kernels, each scaled by separate source and evaluation weights, applied via FFT.
2oXQBpAs9J.problem: Existing neural Green's operators use basis expansions whose spatial functions stay fixed as the source point moves, which can need many terms to resolve local features.
2oXQBpAs9J.method: SMNO represents the Green's function as a sum of learned offset kernels, each multiplied by separate spatial weights at the source and evaluation points; the kernels depend only on the offset and are shared across PDE instances, both weight sets are predicted from the domain shape and coefficient field, and on uniform grids the operator is applied with FFTs without building a dense kernel matrix.
2oXQBpAs9J.key_idea: Translation-invariant offset kernels, modulated by separately predicted weights at source and evaluation points, let the Green's function shift with the source while FFTs avoid a dense kernel matrix.
2oXQBpAs9J.evidence: Poisson problems with unseen 2D and 3D geometries, Darcy flow with unseen coefficient fields, and the Mechanical Components Benchmark, compared with NGF-style basis-expansion controls, FNO, DeepONet, and Transolver++, plus runtime on a 341x341 grid.
2oXQBpAs9J.claimed_gains: Reduces higher-frequency-source error by 71-94% relative to NGF-style basis-expansion controls on Poisson problems and by 82% relative to FNO on Darcy flow; on the Mechanical Components Benchmark it reduces NGF's error by 34%, or 41% with a learned boundary map; on a 341x341 grid, building the operator and applying it to 64 sources takes 69 ms versus 135 ms for FNO.
2oXQBpAs9J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the structured source-offset parametrization improves generalization to unseen geometries, coefficients, and higher-frequency sources, with a useful FFT-based implementation.
2oXQBpAs9J.main_concern: Some baselines look under-trained or adapted (DeepONet near relative L2 of 1 in 3D, Transolver++ below its original paper, mostly single training runs), and the Mechanical Components Benchmark result uses a separate boundary-map extension rather than the core representation.

qECwbBiULR.one_liner: Agentic on-policy distillation that adds selective teacher world-knowledge supervision on student-generated action-state pairs, gated by a lightweight predictor.
qECwbBiULR.problem: Action distributions alone do not tell a student how the environment changes, how tools respond, or what an action's consequences are, and such world knowledge is hard for a small student to infer from multi-turn trajectories.
qECwbBiULR.method: Alongside standard action OPD, WorldOPD distills the teacher's environmental knowledge through student-generated action-state pairs, supervising both candidate actions and their anticipated consequences, and a lightweight predictor trained on sparse probes selects when to apply this extra supervision.
qECwbBiULR.key_idea: A gate learned from sparse probes applies teacher world-knowledge supervision only at states where it reduces teacher-student divergence, since its effect is state-dependent.
qECwbBiULR.evidence: Experiments on function-calling and multi-turn search tasks across three benchmarks and three student models with several student-teacher pairs, including an OPD+ supervised-token control and a selective versus uniform world-knowledge comparison.
qECwbBiULR.claimed_gains: not stated numerically in the abstract, which says WorldOPD consistently improves student performance; a review cites the 4B<-32B search average rising from 41.6 (OPD) and 42.3 (OPD+) to 47.2.
qECwbBiULR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the diagnostics showing a state-dependent effect of world knowledge motivate selective supervision, and that gains hold across several student-teacher pairs and both task families.
qECwbBiULR.main_concern: The contribution of consequence knowledge is not isolated from added action candidates or rationale supervision, and the gate lacks validation (accuracy, calibration, oracle comparison) and seed variation.

rB2xjPvBAn.one_liner: One-model stereo video generation that predicts a baseline-independent disparity ratio, supporting supplied disparity, known baseline, or neither.
rB2xjPvBAn.problem: Geometric information available at inference varies (dense depth or disparity, only a camera baseline, or nothing), existing stereo-video methods commit to one case, and those without geometric input cannot control the stereo geometry they produce.
rB2xjPvBAn.method: UniGenStereo synthesizes the right view from a monocular video with one set of weights: a lightweight head predicts the baseline-independent ratio of focal length to metric depth, which is scaled by a calibrated baseline or a standard interpupillary value, or supplied disparity is used directly, and the disparity warps the input view into shared conditioning channels.
rB2xjPvBAn.key_idea: Because focal length over metric depth is baseline-independent, one predicted ratio, scaled by the baseline when known, feeds a single warp-conditioned backbone for all three geometry settings.
rB2xjPvBAn.evidence: Experiments in all three conditioning settings, including real-world capture, with ablations of warped-latent conditioning (Table 4) and the second training stage (Table 5).
rB2xjPvBAn.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract only claims top results in all three settings, including on real-world capture.
rB2xjPvBAn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified conditioning interface is simple and flexible, letting one model handle supplied, inferred, and default geometry with convincing results.
rB2xjPvBAn.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate the central design choices, namely joint optimization through the Differentiable Self-Warp and direct f/Z prediction, and evaluation relies mainly on reconstruction metrics.

jY4qYRHpAV.one_liner: Short harness-injected model calls manage context and state between agent turns and are discarded afterward, for multi-hop retrieval agents.
jY4qYRHpAV.problem: Long-running retrieval agents must decide what context and state to preserve, compress, rank, or discard, and many harnesses use fixed programmatic rules for truncation, hand-written compression, or capacity-based eviction.
jY4qYRHpAV.method: A micro-turn branches from the current trajectory, has the model perform a scoped management operation, returns a compact state update, and is then discarded rather than recorded; it is instantiated on the Harness-1 retrieval framework to summarize retrieved chunks, resolve curated-set overflow, and order curated evidence.
jY4qYRHpAV.key_idea: Model-mediated context management runs in scoped, branched calls whose prompts and responses are discarded after the state update, so the main trajectory never grows or sees them.
jY4qYRHpAV.evidence: A diverse suite of retrieval benchmarks (including BrowseCompPlus) with Qwen3.5-4B and BM25 retrieval, five-seed means, and efficiency accounting of cache-aware attention operations and peak context.
jY4qYRHpAV.claimed_gains: not stated numerically in the visible abstract; it says micro-turns improve recall while reducing the persistent-context token and attention cost of every episode, and ordered curation strengthens ranking at a bounded, dataset-dependent comparison cost.
jY4qYRHpAV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the micro-turn primitive is simple, general, and clearly framed, with consistent recall gains over five seeds and thorough efficiency accounting.
jY4qYRHpAV.main_concern: Evaluation is limited to a single model (Qwen3.5-4B) with BM25 retrieval, so transfer to larger models is unknown, and some ablations and baselines (query-only summarization, in-trajectory micro-turns, reranking alternatives) are missing.

9a6xwD3iq7.one_liner: RL that turns symbolic-tool failure certificates into reusable constraints pruning invalid regions of neutrino flavor model search.
9a6xwD3iq7.problem: RL for scientific discovery over combinatorial hypothesis spaces uses scalar rewards that say little about why candidates fail, so agents repeatedly explore invalid regions.
9a6xwD3iq7.method: When a candidate violates domain constraints, symbolic reasoning tools produce certificates identifying the responsible actions, and CDRL converts them into reusable constraints that eliminate classes of invalid solutions; per reviews it combines these with MCTS, neural guidance, and SAT propagation.
9a6xwD3iq7.key_idea: Certificates naming the actions responsible for a constraint violation are converted into reusable constraints that eliminate whole classes of invalid candidates from later search.
9a6xwD3iq7.evidence: Neutrino flavor model discovery in theoretical particle physics (hypothesis space above 10^26 models) across three theory spaces against the previous RL approach for the task, with ablations over certificates, MCTS, and the neural component across seeds, and 40 rules extracted post hoc.
9a6xwD3iq7.claimed_gains: Up to 1.95x higher valid model rates and up to 6.33x higher neutrino model rates while evaluating up to 4x fewer candidates, and a valid model rate 2.1-2.8x higher when the prior approach is rerun with the same budget and hardware.
9a6xwD3iq7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is useful and the mechanism of reusing structured failure information is well motivated, with ablations supporting each component.
9a6xwD3iq7.main_concern: Novelty is limited because converting failure feedback into reusable constraints has precedents in conflict-driven synthesis and neuro-symbolic RL, and the efficiency counts and the comparison with the prior system are not fully matched or consistent.

Hw4XpEKH4C.one_liner: Multi-turn red-teaming agent that steers coding agents toward vulnerable yet functionally correct patches by selecting task-relevant vulnerabilities.
Hw4XpEKH4C.problem: Coding agents that modify repositories can be induced by adversarial users to introduce exploitable vulnerabilities, and existing red-teaming ignores that patches must preserve utility or they are rejected before deployment.
Hw4XpEKH4C.method: SWE-RedAgent reasons over the repository and task request to identify task-relevant vulnerability opportunities, then adaptively steers the coding agent over multi-turn interactions toward vulnerable but functionally plausible implementations, using utility and vulnerability gates in a multi-agent architecture.
Hw4XpEKH4C.key_idea: Selecting task-compatible vulnerabilities and gating each multi-turn attack step on both functional utility and vulnerability keeps injected flaws inside patches that would be accepted.
Hw4XpEKH4C.evidence: Web-application development tasks across multiple coding-agent harnesses and backend models, compared with existing red-teaming baselines, with a validation study confirming 46 of 50 sampled findings and a single-agent ablation.
Hw4XpEKH4C.claimed_gains: Introduces 93 verified vulnerabilities over 70 tasks while preserving 97.33% base functionality, outperforming all baselines.
Hw4XpEKH4C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly evaluating utility and vulnerabilities in repository-level coding tasks fills a real security gap, and that the approach is reasonable with promising results over baselines.
Hw4XpEKH4C.main_concern: Attribution to adversarial interaction is incomplete (no security outcomes for the benign-user control), the threat model looks unrealistic, and related-work claims about prior single-turn methods are partly incorrect.

N6KZVMK80w.one_liner: Sign language production conditioned on sentence plus timed lexical anchors extracted from signing video by an isolated-sign dictionary model.
N6KZVMK80w.problem: Gloss conditioning improves sign language production but needs expert annotation that large signing corpora lack, and glosses derived from text alone carry no information about when each sign occurs.
N6KZVMK80w.method: A sign-identity model trained on isolated sign dictionaries extracts timed lexical anchors from signing video, which are combined with the sentence as a hybrid condition (anchors give timing, the sentence gives remaining content); at inference the anchors are predicted from the sentence alone, and ATLAS is a continuous-latent flow-matching generator trained on more than 600 hours of ASL.
N6KZVMK80w.key_idea: Spotting dictionary signs in unannotated video yields timed pseudo-gloss anchors that, paired with the sentence, supply sign timing without any gloss annotation.
N6KZVMK80w.evidence: SMPL-X parameters extracted for more than 1,700 hours of YouTube-SL-25 video, training on more than 600 hours of ASL, back-translation evaluation at several data scales against baselines (How2Sign per reviews), and an audit of the SLP evaluation protocol.
N6KZVMK80w.claimed_gains: Anchors improve back-translation at every data scale tested; an anchored model trained on a fraction of the data surpasses a sentence-only model trained on all of it, and relative to each system's ceiling ATLAS reaches more than twice the back-translation score of the strongest baseline.
N6KZVMK80w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that annotation-free timed lexical supervision from isolated-sign dictionaries on large unannotated corpora is a well-motivated way to improve sign language production, with useful hybrid conditioning.
N6KZVMK80w.main_concern: Anchor accuracy is not evaluated against ground truth, BLEU-4 gains are small (about 1 to 2 points at very low scores), and the benchmark's one-to-one sentence-clip pairing may already supply the alignment the method claims to recover.

HdmpksqRLM.one_liner: Empirical and linear-model study showing AdamW overtakes Muon after fine-tuning once pretraining data budget grows large enough.
HdmpksqRLM.problem: Muon speeds up pretraining loss minimization relative to AdamW, but it is unclear whether that advantage persists after fine-tuning.
HdmpksqRLM.method: Pretrains models with Muon and AdamW across data budgets and model sizes, compares fine-tuning outcomes and robustness to Gaussian weight perturbations, and analyzes a linear associative-memory model with a margin-to-noise-ratio proxy for robustness.
HdmpksqRLM.key_idea: As pretraining data budget grows, the margin-to-noise ratio, a second-order robustness proxy, shifts from favoring Muon to favoring gradient descent, mirroring AdamW overtaking Muon after fine-tuning.
HdmpksqRLM.evidence: About 600 pretrained models from 30M to 600M parameters at 5 to 2,560 tokens per parameter and about 29,000 fine-tuning runs on four datasets, Gaussian-perturbation tests, and a theorem plus experiments in a linear model.
HdmpksqRLM.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports a trend, that beyond a sufficiently large pretraining data budget AdamW outperforms Muon after fine-tuning and overtakes it at progressively smaller token-parameter ratios as model size grows.
HdmpksqRLM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is large, systematic, and carefully controlled, with a clear finding that holds across datasets and is supported by Gaussian-perturbation and linear-model proxies.
HdmpksqRLM.main_concern: The linear-model theory compares Muon with gradient descent rather than AdamW and does not explain the size-dependent crossover, and the paper offers no mechanism or benchmark-score evaluation.

UF5C43bOgq.one_liner: Protein language model of intrinsically disordered regions post-trained with RL that rewards activating specified sparse-autoencoder features.
UF5C43bOgq.problem: Structure-based design does not readily apply to intrinsically disordered regions, and protein language models trained on full-length sequences learn a prior biased toward folded domains.
UF5C43bOgq.method: IDiom is an autoregressive protein language model trained on IDiom-DB, 54 million predicted IDRs curated from the AlphaFold Database, and RL-SAE is a post-training method that rewards generating sequences that activate specified sparse-autoencoder feature sets.
UF5C43bOgq.key_idea: Selected SAE features of the language model's hidden states become an explicit sequence-level RL reward, so multiple function-linked features can be installed and combined in one sequence.
UF5C43bOgq.evidence: Eight IDR design tasks compared with activation steering and supervised fine-tuning, predicted subcellular localization and transcriptional activity, and composition, patterning, motif, and predicted-disorder checks of generated sequences; validation is computational only.
UF5C43bOgq.claimed_gains: Across eight IDR design tasks, RL-SAE sequences activate on average 90% of 30 targeted features versus 24% for activation steering, and improve predicted subcellular localization and transcriptional activity over steering and supervised fine-tuning.
UF5C43bOgq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that training exclusively on disordered regions removes folded-domain bias and that turning SAE features into an RL objective gives interpretable, composable control with competitive results against SFT and steering.
UF5C43bOgq.main_concern: Validation is computational only, and dataset curation and splits are weakly validated (pLDDT-based IDR calls, 90% identity clustering, and possible leakage between prompted and unprompted copies of the same IDR).

f7QYPo46EM.one_liner: Auto-regressive flow-matching head-motion generator post-trained with RL whose reward normalization is decoupled across FLAME parameter groups.
f7QYPo46EM.problem: Listener head-motion generation suffers from regression to the mean, collapsing into static faces, and existing methods lack a parameter space for complex nonverbal motion.
f7QYPo46EM.method: An auto-regressive flow-matching architecture gives stable supervised learning, then Group reward-Decoupled Policy Optimization (GDPO) normalizes rewards separately per FLAME parameter group to encourage high-variance expressive motion, with explicit text control added for customizable responses.
f7QYPo46EM.key_idea: Isolating reward normalization across FLAME parameter groups lets policy optimization explicitly reward high-variance expressive motion, countering regression-to-the-mean collapse into static faces.
f7QYPo46EM.evidence: Evaluation on the Seamless Interaction and DualTalk datasets against existing baselines, including standard GRPO, on long-term kinematic variance, visual expressivity, and semantic controllability, with reward-term ablations.
f7QYPo46EM.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract claims superior performance over existing baselines on long-term kinematic variance, visual expressivity, and semantic controllability.
f7QYPo46EM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the listener-motion problem is relevant and the pipeline combining flow matching with reward-driven post-training is coherent, with extensive experiments and an expanded FLAME parameter space.
f7QYPo46EM.main_concern: Gains may largely reflect fitting the reward, since the velocity-variance reward term equals the FDD/PDD/JDD metrics and drives almost all improvement, and novelty over GRPO and the need for RL are not established.

1uKiakJHan.one_liner: Process reward for retrieval agents that scores each step by the gain in correct-answer likelihood, with no extra rollouts.
1uKiakJHan.problem: Retrieval agents are mostly trained with outcome rewards, and step-level labels for process reward models are costly: human or LLM-judge labels need substantial resources and Monte-Carlo estimation triggers extra search interaction per step.
1uKiakJHan.method: DeltaPRM scores each retrieval call and the reasoning after it by how much the information raises the model's likelihood of the correct final answer (one forward pass per step), then trains a PRM to predict the discounted return of this label from the reasoning prefix alone, so no ground-truth answer is needed at inference.
1uKiakJHan.key_idea: The change in the model's likelihood of the correct answer between steps serves as a rollout-free step label, which a PRM then learns to predict from the prefix alone.
1uKiakJHan.evidence: Multi-hop agentic search benchmarks (including HotpotQA) tested on best-of-N selection, step-level guided generation (greedy, beam, and MC tree search), human-labeled verification, cross-generator transfer, and online RL, against matched ORM and ThinkPRM controls.
1uKiakJHan.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract (it is cut off); reviews cite 278x and 217x labeling-cost savings and HotpotQA MCTS accuracy of 59.6% with the matched ORM versus 63.2% with DeltaPRM.
1uKiakJHan.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the label construction is simple and needs no extra rollouts, retrieval calls, or judge model, and that distilling it into a prefix-only PRM supports multiple uses with broad evaluation.
1uKiakJHan.main_concern: The headline efficiency ratios come from a modeled fused-cache estimate (the implementation actually run costs 70-89x that), and the likelihood-gain labels are not validated directly against human judgments or compared with Implicit PRM or AutoPSV.

ssxJb2MQoS.one_liner: Video diffusion transformer conditioned on paired source-target 3D point tracks re-renders videos from new camera trajectories.
ssxJb2MQoS.problem: Camera-controlled video re-rendering methods either inject camera parameters, leaving source-to-target correspondence implicit, or render estimated geometry frame by frame, so neither gives an explicit, temporally continuous link between source and target pixels.
ssxJb2MQoS.method: Track2View conditions a video diffusion transformer on sparse 3D point tracks projected into both source and target views, using a dual-view track conditioner that transfers visual context through parameter-free geometric operations and learned temporal aggregation; a data pipeline extracts one-to-one track correspondences by running a 3D point tracker on temporally concatenated multi-camera view pairs.
ssxJb2MQoS.key_idea: Sparse 3D point tracks projected into both source and target cameras give explicit, temporally continuous correspondences that a dual-view conditioner uses to transfer source appearance to the target view.
ssxJb2MQoS.evidence: A 400-video benchmark spanning static and dynamic scenes, comparisons on RealCam-Vid and Kubric-4D, cross-dataset tests from synthetic MultiCamVideo to RealEstate10K and MiraData, and ablations.
ssxJb2MQoS.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract (cut off) claims the best results on a 400-video benchmark across visual quality and further metrics.
ssxJb2MQoS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that paired 3D point tracks for explicit spatiotemporal correspondence are a clean, reasonable alternative to camera embeddings, with competitive camera-control accuracy and convincing cross-dataset generalization.
ssxJb2MQoS.main_concern: The camera-accuracy evaluation is hard to interpret (errors computed only on videos GLOMAP can register, kept counts unreported, unequal frame conditioning versus baselines), and 4D consistency is not directly evaluated.

xgsDy5l4kp.one_liner: Probabilistic Concordance Correlation Coefficient: Brier score normalized by independent-label error, giving chance-corrected prediction-label agreement in [-1, 1].
xgsDy5l4kp.problem: Common classifier metrics miss parts of performance: AUROC ignores calibration, calibration error ignores case-specific information, and the Brier score's magnitude depends on class prevalence and case mix, limiting comparison across prediction problems.
xgsDy5l4kp.method: Extends the repeated-measures concordance correlation coefficient to prediction-label agreement on the probability simplex; equivalently it is one minus the Brier score divided by the error against independent labels, with an exact O(nK) U-statistic estimator and asymptotic theory.
xgsDy5l4kp.key_idea: Dividing the Brier score by the error a forecaster would incur against independent labels gives a bounded, prior-independent, chance-corrected agreement score.
xgsDy5l4kp.evidence: Theory (properties, theorems, a calibrated-forecast identity relating the metric to the Brier skill score, and a proposition on what the metric rewards) plus a temperature-scaling illustration.
xgsDy5l4kp.claimed_gains: not stated; the paper claims a bounded [-1, 1] metric with exact O(nK) inference that should accompany, not replace, the Brier score.
xgsDy5l4kp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the metric is principled and mathematically clean, with a clear equivalence to a Brier score normalized by an independence baseline and transparent analysis of what it rewards.
xgsDy5l4kp.main_concern: Novelty and practical added value are limited: it is a monotone transform of the Brier skill score for calibrated models and reduces to Cohen's kappa for hard predictions, and it can rank an overconfident miscalibrated forecaster above the true posterior.

i4dRfFQJdM.one_liner: Anytime-valid rank confidence sets from pairwise betting e-processes and closed testing over orderings, valid for all models simultaneously.
i4dRfFQJdM.problem: Rank confidence intervals recomputed while a leaderboard evaluation runs, or stopped once decisive, exceed their nominal error rate, and no anytime-valid method gives ranks when all models are scored on the same items, which makes their scores dependent.
i4dRfFQJdM.method: Constructs, for every model, a set of ranks that contains its true rank simultaneously for all models and at all times at level alpha, by combining betting e-processes for each ordered pair of models with closed testing over possible orderings, allowing any dependence between the models' scores on an item.
i4dRfFQJdM.key_idea: Betting e-processes for each ordered model pair eliminate candidate orderings through closed testing, and the ranks consistent with surviving orderings form the confidence set at any stopping time.
i4dRfFQJdM.evidence: Finite-sample theory for rank sets, top-k sets, and tiers, plus experiments E1-E4 including a six-tied-model setting and OpenLeaderboard data with 395 models.
i4dRfFQJdM.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract claims guarantees valid at every stopping time, so a leaderboard can be inspected after every item and each model's evaluation can stop once its question is settled.
i4dRfFQJdM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory fills a gap by extending anytime-valid inference to rank objects with dependent scores, with an intuitive construction that connects e-processes to LLM evaluation.
i4dRfFQJdM.main_concern: Empirical support is limited (a tied-model worst case, relatively wide intervals, costly exact computation), and the dense, appendix-heavy paper is hard to read.

2w6E5ddPeX.one_liner: Information-theoretic bounds on summary mutual information needed in neural posterior estimation, showing stochastic summaries beat deterministic time-sharing.
2w6E5ddPeX.problem: Neural posterior estimation conditions on a fixed-dimensional summary that imposes an implicit finite information budget set by architecture and training, so better performance may reflect a larger budget rather than better encoding.
2w6E5ddPeX.method: Models the summary as a possibly stochastic channel from data to summary, measures the budget by mutual information I(Y;S), bounds the budget needed for bounded posterior distortion from above by quantizing posteriors and from below by converses, and shows that a finite budget is best spent stochastically under a common-support condition; a Bernoulli-channel BNPE architecture is tested on simulators.
2w6E5ddPeX.key_idea: Treat the summary as a channel and measure its budget by I(Y;S): the required budget grows like (d/2) log n, and stochastic channels strictly beat the deterministic time-sharing frontier.
2w6E5ddPeX.evidence: Theorems (including Theorem 4.2 on strict separation for general standard-Borel experiments), analytic examples, a count experiment enumerating deterministic alternatives, and simulator experiments comparing NLL for a stochastic BNPE architecture.
2w6E5ddPeX.claimed_gains: not stated as empirical gains; the abstract states that in regular d-dimensional models bounded posterior distortion requires (d/2) log n - O(1) nats, even when a fixed-dimensional sufficient statistic exists.
2w6E5ddPeX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree Theorem 4.2, the strict separation between stochastic summaries and the deterministic time-sharing frontier, is the main contribution and is rigorous, general, and carefully scoped.
2w6E5ddPeX.main_concern: The link between the general theory and the BNPE architecture and simulator experiments is weak (NLL mixes decoder error with summary information, and mutual information as the cost measure is not justified).

pScfmUrMH1.one_liner: Taxonomy and evaluation of nine model-selection algorithms for assembling LLM teams for multi-LLM collaboration.
pScfmUrMH1.problem: Multi-LLM collaboration systems depend on pre-defined, hand-crafted model pools, and how to select which models to include is unexamined.
pScfmUrMH1.method: Proposes and evaluates a taxonomy of 9 selection algorithms spanning diversity of model descriptions, capability-aware behavioral diversity, and LLM-based recruiters, tested on candidate pools of 10 and 32 models in four collaboration algorithms across math, coding, QA, and reasoning.
pScfmUrMH1.key_idea: Selectors combine a signal (descriptions, ability estimates, behavioral diversity, or a trained LLM recruiter) with a search procedure that builds teams from candidate pools.
pScfmUrMH1.evidence: Two candidate pools (10 and 32 models), four model collaboration algorithms, tasks in math, coding, QA, and reasoning, plus tests with malicious models and unseen tasks and an SFT recruiter transfer study.
pScfmUrMH1.claimed_gains: Successful selection algorithms outperform random or heuristics-based teams, such as selecting the models with top individual performance, by up to 36.1% across settings.
pScfmUrMH1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that model selection is a practical, under-studied part of multi-LLM system design and that evaluation across four collaboration mechanisms, malicious models, and unseen tasks gives a useful comparison.
pScfmUrMH1.main_concern: Gains are not isolated from retaining strong models or from the search procedure, uncertainty comparisons mix variation across teams with test-item resampling, and novelty over existing ensemble-selection methods is unclear.

a4P0BVyYKv.one_liner: Training-free multi-agent framework where curriculum, actor and verifier agents explore an environment and freeze a reusable memory.
a4P0BVyYKv.problem: Digital agents must adapt to new environments whose interfaces, tools and failure modes are not fully captured by pretrained models.
a4P0BVyYKv.method: RSIAgent coordinates curriculum, actor and verifier agents that continually explore the environment, validate outcomes and retain environment-specific knowledge, including causal relationships between actions, conditions and consequences. It explores broad-then-deep (parallel broad exploration, then focused deep exploration of hard cases and hidden constraints) and freezes the resulting memory for downstream reuse.
a4P0BVyYKv.key_idea: Verifier-validated exploration builds a frozen memory of reusable action-condition-consequence causal relations, using broad-then-deep self-exploration, with no parameter updates.
a4P0BVyYKv.evidence: Experiments on OSWorld 2.0 and Agents' Last Exam with open-source models (Kimi-K3, GLM-5.3) compared against frontier closed-source models.
a4P0BVyYKv.claimed_gains: Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3 outperform frontier closed-source models including GPT-6 Astra on OSWorld 2.0 and Agents' Last Exam; no numeric gains are stated.
a4P0BVyYKv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the practical motivation (adapting agents without parameter updates) and the sensible curriculum/actor/verifier design with information separation.
a4P0BVyYKv.main_concern: The evaluation reuses target tasks during memory construction, so held-out generalization is not established and comparisons may be unfair; one reviewer also says the recursive-self-improvement label overclaims for an external memory.

nok7VXglzK.one_liner: Two-stage diffusion language model that caches an expensive anchor network's latent and fuses it into a lightweight denoiser.
nok7VXglzK.problem: Anchored diffusion language models need supervised important-token targets, and anchor hidden representations become stale as the token canvas evolves.
nok7VXglzK.method: Time-based self-supervised anchoring: an expensive anchor network is evaluated periodically to produce a cached latent state, and a lightweight denoising network fuses the cache with the current state at each reverse step through a fusion module. It is instantiated as TADM:Post-train (time-anchorizes pretrained DLMs) and TADM:Pretraining.
nok7VXglzK.key_idea: Reuse a periodically computed anchor latent across nearby diffusion steps, with a learned fusion module combining stale anchor content with the current canvas state.
nok7VXglzK.evidence: TADM:Post-train applied to DiffusionGemma-26B on math, code and STEM benchmarks (GSM8K, AIME26 and others; list truncated in the input); reviews also cite a ReMDM comparison for TADM:Pretraining.
nok7VXglzK.claimed_gains: TADM:Post-train improves throughput by approximately 49% to 79% on DiffusionGemma-26B across several math, code and STEM benchmarks.
nok7VXglzK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the simple, well-motivated learned temporal reuse and the cheap post-training of a small fusion module on a frozen 26B model, trained on rollout states to match cached inference.
nok7VXglzK.main_concern: Gains over matched-compute baselines such as ReMDM are marginal, there is no clean ablation of the fusion module or rollout training, and comparisons with other cache accelerators are missing.

nTHoR4dSMe.one_liner: Conditional rectified flow reconstructs single-channel ECG from wearable PPG and IMU signals with motion-aware conditioning and curriculum.
nTHoR4dSMe.problem: Wearable PPG is easy to collect continuously but is an indirect, motion-sensitive cardiovascular measurement, so ECG-level rhythm and waveform information is hard to obtain outside clinics.
nTHoR4dSMe.method: A convolutional encoder-decoder with a transformer bottleneck and flow-time conditioning models conditional transport from noise to ECG, with IMU-derived conditioning features, motion-dependent loss weighting, and an easy-to-hard training curriculum.
nTHoR4dSMe.key_idea: Model PPG-to-ECG reconstruction as conditional rectified-flow transport, injecting IMU motion information through conditioning features, loss weighting, and a curriculum.
nTHoR4dSMe.evidence: Leave-one-subject-out evaluation on PPG-DaLiA and WESAD against deterministic, adversarial, and diffusion-based baselines, with regional, motion-stratified, and ablation analyses.
nTHoR4dSMe.claimed_gains: Pearson correlations of 0.983 and 0.986 and R-peak F1 scores of 0.946 and 0.955 on PPG-DaLiA and WESAD, with L1 error versus Conditional DDPM-1D falling from 0.085 to 0.062 and from 0.074 to 0.055.
nTHoR4dSMe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses a relevant wearable-monitoring problem with a coherent motion-aware pipeline and a reasonably comprehensive leave-one-subject-out evaluation.
nTHoR4dSMe.main_concern: The architecture is borrowed from prior work and comparisons are not controlled (PPG-only baselines versus PPG+IMU), with z-score-normalized targets leaving amplitude fidelity unassessed.

lV7wnRJDIM.one_liner: Benchmark scoring LLM-generated CUDA against human-expert systems, from single kernels to full applications, on Ampere, Hopper, Blackwell GPUs.
lV7wnRJDIM.problem: Even strong coding models may fall short of expert-level, architecture-aware CUDA optimization, and benchmarks that measure speedup over a functional baseline do not expose this gap.
lV7wnRJDIM.method: Defines tasks spanning single kernels, module-level operators, full applications and unsolved challenge tasks, with end-to-end tasks gated by domain-specific semantic validators. Evaluates models such as Claude-Opus-4.6 and GPT-5.4, including iterative and tool-augmented feedback settings.
lV7wnRJDIM.key_idea: Score generated CUDA against end-to-end human-expert reference systems, with semantic validators gating application-level tasks, instead of measuring speedup over a functional baseline.
lV7wnRJDIM.evidence: Evaluation of models such as Claude-Opus-4.6 and GPT-5.4 on a benchmark (195 tasks per reviewers) across Ampere, Hopper and Blackwell GPUs, with direct generation, refinement and tool-augmented variants.
lV7wnRJDIM.claimed_gains: Semantics-valid solutions are found for only three of ten end-to-end applications, at no more than 0.74x expert speed.
lV7wnRJDIM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark fills a practical gap by comparing against human-expert code across diverse domains, task scopes and GPU generations.
lV7wnRJDIM.main_concern: The claims are not fully substantiated: agentic baselines and framework choices are limited, the understanding-to-implementation gap is shown only qualitatively, and one reviewer reports evaluation-script bugs that could invalidate results.

talcM0NCjb.one_liner: Scales JEPA latent world models to 8B parameters on 12 robot embodiments and fits compute scaling laws for imagination error.
talcM0NCjb.problem: There is no principled way to estimate how latent world model capabilities scale with model size, data and compute.
talcM0NCjb.method: Trains RoboJEPA, a JEPA-based world model, on a large-scale dataset spanning 12 robotic embodiments, fits scaling laws to imagination error (the error of latent rollouts) and studies downstream planning. It is also deployed zero-shot on real hardware, planning toward a single goal image.
talcM0NCjb.key_idea: Fit a second-order power law of latent-rollout imagination error against training compute, selected by held-out extrapolation to larger models, and test planning when training horizon matches planning horizon.
talcM0NCjb.evidence: Model sizes from 22M to 8B (fit on 22M-2B and tested on held-out 4B and 8B per reviewers) trained on real multi-embodiment robot data, with downstream planning tasks and real-hardware zero-shot long-horizon goal-image planning.
talcM0NCjb.claimed_gains: Imagination error follows a second-order power law in compute that predicts model quality beyond the scale at which it is fit, and the 8B-parameter RoboJEPA is the largest JEPA predictor trained to date.
talcM0NCjb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a careful, systematic and large-scale scaling study of robot world models, with a held-out extrapolation protocol, direct FLOP counting and promised release of checkpoints and code.
talcM0NCjb.main_concern: Two reviewers say the claim that imagination error is a reliable proxy for planning performance is stronger than the evidence, because obstacle-reach reward does not consistently follow compute and greedy tasks saturate early.

UKcOAAa0lD.one_liner: Scores long-context training documents by sink-corrected attention look-back distance to select data for context extension.
UKcOAAa0lD.problem: Long-context training is expensive and needs data selection that separates cohesive documents with long-range dependencies from simple concatenations, but naive attention-distance measures are dominated by attention sinks.
UKcOAAa0lD.method: AttentionSpan measures the look-back distance covered by attention during a forward pass, with simple tricks to ignore attention sinks, and uses it to filter data when extending a model's context.
UKcOAAa0lD.key_idea: Measure attention look-back distance after discounting attention-sink tokens, and keep documents with high sink-corrected span.
UKcOAAa0lD.evidence: Extending OLMo-3-7B from 8K to 32K with 5B tokens sampled from its own long-text mixture, plus a domain-matched experiment with the same code, arXiv, and book proportions.
UKcOAAa0lD.claimed_gains: AttentionSpan curation improves HELMET-Recall from 62.0 to 75.7 when extending OLMo-3-7B from 8K to 32K using 5B tokens.
UKcOAAa0lD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the metric clearly outperforms other filtering baselines for long-context extension across base models, addresses a real cost problem, and is backed by thorough data-mixture experiments.
UKcOAAa0lD.main_concern: The evaluation covers few long-context benchmarks, and baseline comparisons do not clearly separate the metric's benefit from other selection choices such as domain balancing.

EL6zzNrB62.one_liner: Monte Carlo tree search for POMDPs that plans over learned belief embeddings instead of particle sets or summary statistics.
EL6zzNrB62.problem: Sampled-state belief approximations suffer particle impoverishment, and prior learned-network planners rely on hand-chosen summaries of the sampled states.
EL6zzNrB62.method: BETS keeps a BetaZero-style search loop but represents each node's belief with a learned generative embedding computed from the parent node's embedding using the POMDP dynamics, trained to support sampling and to condition policy and value networks.
EL6zzNrB62.key_idea: Each search node holds a learned generative belief embedding that is computed from the parent embedding, can be sampled, and feeds the policy and value networks.
EL6zzNrB62.evidence: Per reviews, comparisons against baselines including BetaZero at equal numbers of simulations; the abstract is cut off before the experiments.
EL6zzNrB62.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find learned belief embeddings that avoid particle collapse and feed search, policy, and value networks a well-motivated, elegant design.
EL6zzNrB62.main_concern: Comparisons at equal simulation counts do not equalize compute or report training cost, and the paper lacks formal guarantees and underspecifies the variable-coupling encoder.

shpQH24STD.one_liner: Logit-lens readout of Qwen3-Omni audio-token positions shows verbalizable, sound-driven concepts in early and middle layers.
shpQH24STD.problem: Verbalizable, global-workspace-like representations in middle layers have been characterized for text inputs, but it is unknown whether audio language models form them from sound.
shpQH24STD.method: Applies a logit lens at the audio-token positions of an off-the-shelf Qwen3-Omni, which precede and cannot see the question, with a waveform-swap control (real, mismatched or silent audio) and activation patching of audio-position activations into a run with the audio removed.
shpQH24STD.key_idea: Read audio-token hidden states with a logit lens before the question appears, and use waveform-swap and patching controls to show the readout is sound-driven and used.
shpQH24STD.evidence: Qwen3-Omni with waveform-swap controls (real, mismatched, silence), depth-wise tracing, activation patching, and qualitative clip examples.
shpQH24STD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the audio-position readout and the waveform-swap control are well motivated and show that the signal depends on the actual audio.
shpQH24STD.main_concern: The evidence does not show what is distinctive about the middle-layer workspace, since the sound-dependent signal persists across depth and whole-residual patching is not concept-specific.

6d49LBQlIk.one_liner: Shows Muon scaling rules fail across settings and optimizer rankings flip with batch size, explained by a noisy quadratic model.
6d49LBQlIk.problem: New adaptive optimizers are typically benchmarked at a single batch size, and hyperparameter scaling rules are assumed to preserve optimizer rankings as batch size and gradient noise change.
6d49LBQlIk.method: An empirical study of Muon scaling rules and optimizer comparisons in language-model pretraining across batch sizes after extensive tuning, plus analysis of a noisy quadratic model and a bias-variance tradeoff in preconditioning under gradient noise.
6d49LBQlIk.key_idea: The critical batch size beyond which a scaling rule breaks varies across loss-landscape directions, and gradient noise creates a bias-variance preconditioning tradeoff that can reverse optimizer rankings.
6d49LBQlIk.evidence: LM pretraining experiments across batch sizes (reviews cite KL-SOAP versus Shampoo crossovers and a sharp-subspace intervention), a noisy quadratic model analysis, and a proof that noise can reverse rankings even under optimal learning-rate and momentum tuning.
6d49LBQlIk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating optimizers at a single batch size is limiting, that the optimizer-crossover finding under extensive tuning is useful, and that the curvature-noise analysis explains benefits and costs of preconditioning.
6d49LBQlIk.main_concern: Training budgets are small (the largest batch has about 800 optimizer steps), and the link between the curvature-to-noise mechanism and the observed crossovers is not fully established.

UOrVzUCAhw.one_liner: Allocates a fixed split-learning uplink budget across modalities using server-computed Shapley contribution scores.
UOrVzUCAhw.problem: Communication-efficient split learning gives every modality the same keep-ratio, so the budget is split by activation dimension rather than by how much each modality contributes to the fused prediction.
UOrVzUCAhw.method: Under a fixed expected payload, ModalShare sets each modality's keep-ratio from a Shapley contribution score that the server computes over coalitions of activations it has already received, adding no transmission overhead or client-side computation.
UOrVzUCAhw.key_idea: Compute Shapley contributions of modalities at the server from already-received activations, and use them to set per-modality keep-ratios within a fixed payload.
UOrVzUCAhw.evidence: Multimodal split-learning experiments at matched payload against equal keep-ratios, including MVSA and CREMA-D datasets per reviews.
UOrVzUCAhw.claimed_gains: Improves accuracy over equal keep-ratios by 15.4 and 12.4 percentage points, up to 15.4 points at matched payload, with no extra uplink.
UOrVzUCAhw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that inter-modality budget allocation is a practical, underexplored decision and that the method is simple, adds no communication cost, and gives substantial gains.
UOrVzUCAhw.main_concern: Baselines and evaluation are questioned: gains may mostly reflect dropping a weak modality against a weak equal-ratio baseline, checkpoint-selection independence is unclear, and novelty over existing Shapley-based allocation is limited.

djP0t66gCd.one_liner: Jointly trains action and bidding policies in decentralized agent swarms, with bids both allocating turns and passing training credit.
djP0t66gCd.problem: Existing multi-agent systems train agents inside fixed orchestration structures, separating the learning of individual capabilities from the organization of collective behavior.
djP0t66gCd.method: Market-based post-training (MPT) has agents express willingness to participate through bids that determine who acts and how collective outcomes provide local training credit, so action and bidding behavior are learned together without a central coordinator. Reviewers add that the bid also acts as the backward credit-transfer coefficient and is updated with counterfactual rollouts.
djP0t66gCd.key_idea: Use one learned bid both to decide which agent acts and to set how much downstream value flows back to earlier actors, updating bids by counterfactual rollouts.
djP0t66gCd.evidence: Embodied crafting, robot navigation, and deep research (one reviewer says results are shown only for embodied crafting), with ablations, transfer to related tasks, and larger-population inference scaling.
djP0t66gCd.claimed_gains: Gains over monolithic post-training, learned self-orchestration beating alternative coordination strategies with the same action policies, and better performance with larger populations at inference time; no numbers are visible in the abstract.
djP0t66gCd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that coupling turn allocation with credit assignment through a learned bid is an original, intuitive mechanism that lets participation and actions co-adapt.
djP0t66gCd.main_concern: The comparison with monolithic RL does not isolate learned orchestration from model capacity and specialization (three separately fine-tuned models and a hand-split action space), and results may cover only embodied crafting.

MulEQgmm8V.one_liner: Measures how instruct models adopt supplied solutions and strategies, including erroneous ones, using BIG-Bench-Hard generators and activation patching.
MulEQgmm8V.problem: Cheaper instruct models in agentic systems reuse reasoning produced by another model, and it is unclear whether they can benefit from inherited reasoning without propagating its errors.
MulEQgmm8V.method: Rebuilds BIG-Bench-Hard tasks as generators across twelve difficulty tiers and eight models, supplying correct or erroneous solutions and strategies either as the start of the model's own response or in a separate user message. Activation patching traces how supplied values reach the answering position.
MulEQgmm8V.key_idea: Inject correct or corrupted worked solutions and strategies into programmatically generated tasks and trace their adoption, with activation patching showing how supplied values are carried to the answer.
MulEQgmm8V.evidence: Eight models on BIG-Bench-Hard-based generators across twelve difficulty tiers and two placements, activation patching, and 200 GSM8K problems.
MulEQgmm8V.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers (the abstract says correct solutions substantially improve accuracy, models often adopt erroneous solutions even on problems they solve alone, and enabling thinking reduces but does not eliminate error adoption).
MulEQgmm8V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled, programmatically generated setup is rigorous and that the experiments, ablations, and interpretability analysis cover many models and difficulty levels.
MulEQgmm8V.main_concern: The setting is narrow: main results rely mostly on assistant-prefill placement, models are older instruct models rather than frontier or reasoning models, and no real agentic pipeline is tested.

KPyoSqDayk.one_liner: LLM proposes patches to an executable symbolic guardrail policy; a deterministic verifier and evidence-aware authority layer gate activation.
KPyoSqDayk.problem: Adaptive LLM-agent guardrails apply policies through stochastic LLM inference, while formal guardrails are deterministic but static and cannot adapt to newly observed risks.
KPyoSqDayk.method: The guardrail is a formal policy of executable symbolic rules over typed agent events. An LLM guided by deployment feedback proposes patches that repair new failures while preserving prior behavior, a deterministic verifier admits only structurally valid, conflict-free policies, and an evidence-aware authority layer activates verified rules.
KPyoSqDayk.key_idea: Evolve a symbolic rule policy through LLM-proposed patches that must pass deterministic structural and conflict checks, then activate rules according to accumulated evidence.
KPyoSqDayk.evidence: Comparisons with adaptive guardrails and symbolic rule-learning baselines over multiple seeds, sparse and noisy feedback, and component ablations per reviews, using sequential replay of benchmark streams.
KPyoSqDayk.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off before the results)
KPyoSqDayk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the separation of proposing, verifying, and authorizing rules is useful, the gap between adaptive neural and deterministic formal guardrails is well motivated, and ablations are informative.
KPyoSqDayk.main_concern: The LLM event parser that feeds the formal policy is not evaluated, and the authority-layer calibration and adaptation under real distribution shift are weakly tested.

PjsJiEaWaA.one_liner: Gaussian smoothing over Zernike aberration coefficients certifies prediction stability against physically parameterized lens distortions.
PjsJiEaWaA.problem: Empirical defenses against optical aberrations cannot guarantee that model predictions remain stable.
PjsJiEaWaA.method: CROCO adds Gaussian noise to Zernike coefficients and applies randomized smoothing to the optical renderer and model. It interprets coefficient-space radii through RMS wavefront tolerance and lens-sharpness ranges.
PjsJiEaWaA.key_idea: Apply randomized smoothing in Zernike coefficient space with the optical renderer included in the certified function.
PjsJiEaWaA.evidence: Experiments on Imagenette, ImageNet100, and ImageNet1k include classification, semantic segmentation, explanation stability, and individual aberration modes.
PjsJiEaWaA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate physically interpretable optical robustness certificates and experiments covering multiple prediction tasks.
PjsJiEaWaA.main_concern: The attack evaluation projects RGB aberrations into shared coefficients, so reported robustness may partly reflect a weakened attack.

sCiu5Miaxx.one_liner: Adaptive sensitivity-aware perturbations during reinforcement learning train language-model agents to tolerate deployment-time policy changes.
sCiu5Miaxx.problem: RL-trained language-model agents can lose task performance under hidden-state noise, pruning, and quantization.
sCiu5Miaxx.method: SPrPO introduces perturbation-robust policy analysis and conditions for stable monotonic improvement. Its training algorithm uses adaptive perturbations informed by policy sensitivity.
sCiu5Miaxx.key_idea: Adjust training perturbations according to policy sensitivity while optimizing the agent's reinforcement-learning objective.
sCiu5Miaxx.evidence: Experiments use Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct with LoRA and GiGPO on ALFWorld and WebShop, testing five perturbation types at multiple strengths.
sCiu5Miaxx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that deployment perturbations are practically relevant and that evaluation across noise, pruning, and quantization is useful.
sCiu5Miaxx.main_concern: Evaluation on one small model and one RL algorithm, without relevant compression-aware baselines, leaves the scope of the robustness gains unclear.

GRkdNsi9S0.one_liner: Gradient-coupling analysis tracks how normal-only training moves unseen representations toward or away from a one-class center.
GRkdNsi9S0.problem: Deep one-class classification does not directly train on unseen inputs, leaving their representation changes and detection failures poorly understood.
GRkdNsi9S0.method: The paper derives a finite-time first-order trajectory decomposition for unseen representations under gradient descent. It separates initial center distance from cumulative gradient-coupled displacement, gives a sufficient detection condition, and extends the analysis to anomaly supervision.
GRkdNsi9S0.key_idea: Express unseen-input displacement as accumulated normal-sample updates transferred through gradient coupling, plus approximation error.
GRkdNsi9S0.evidence: Gaussian-initialized MNIST experiments examine representation trajectories, anomaly scores, coupling geometry, and approximation limits across training time, width, and depth.
GRkdNsi9S0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the interpretable gradient-coupling account of unseen representation movement and its experimental examination.
GRkdNsi9S0.main_concern: The initialization-dependent assumptions and practical informativeness of the detection conditions need stronger validation.

WjMRYUX9Kq.one_liner: A small learned controller selects visible and remasked tokens while a frozen diffusion language model predicts token content.
WjMRYUX9Kq.problem: Hand-designed decoding rules and monotonically increasing visibility limit how masked diffusion models reconsider earlier token decisions.
WjMRYUX9Kq.method: TIPS uses visibility-aware confidence features and a shallow transformer to select token visibility under a fixed expected-visibility schedule. Supervised warmup followed by terminal-correctness reinforcement learning trains the controller while the decoder stays frozen.
WjMRYUX9Kq.key_idea: Learn binary visibility decisions that can both reveal and withdraw tokens after each denoising pass.
WjMRYUX9Kq.evidence: Experiments use LLaDA-8B-Instruct on GSM8K and MATH-500, with full-canvas and two-block variants, multiple seeds, and budget-transfer evaluations.
WjMRYUX9Kq.claimed_gains: At 32 decoder evaluations, the variants achieve 58.46% and 57.97% micro-averaged accuracy, exceeding the strongest main-comparison baseline by 12.1 and 11.6 percentage points.
WjMRYUX9Kq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a simple visibility-control formulation and substantial accuracy gains at low and moderate decoder-call budgets.
WjMRYUX9Kq.main_concern: Evaluation on one backbone and mathematical tasks leaves generalization to other domains and practical decoding configurations unclear.

p5RzOSUXH2.one_liner: Reward-free online fine-tuning adapts behavioral foundation models using causal memory and beliefs over successor ensembles.
p5RzOSUXH2.problem: Policies retrieved from pretrained behavioral foundation models can fail when test-time environment dynamics change.
p5RzOSUXH2.method: AdaBFM pretrains an adaptive prior over dynamics and continually fine-tunes it from reward-free online experience. Policies condition on causal memory and successor-ensemble beliefs, with successor-belief information gain guiding adaptation.
p5RzOSUXH2.key_idea: Update a pretrained dynamics prior from reward-free transitions while conditioning policies on causal memory and successor-ensemble beliefs.
p5RzOSUXH2.evidence: Experiments span 23 navigation, locomotion, and manipulation tasks under unseen dynamics, including exploration ablations and AntMaze layout shifts.
p5RzOSUXH2.claimed_gains: AdaBFM has the highest mean performance in 9 out of 23 zero-shot tasks and 16 out of 23 after continual training, improving by an average of 28% on harder tasks.
p5RzOSUXH2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value reward-free adaptation to unseen dynamics and experiments examining the role of exploration.
p5RzOSUXH2.main_concern: Conflicting descriptions of exploration and reward use obscure which headline results support the proposed reward-free protocol.

pHZvxtuPkK.one_liner: Low-rank behavioral projections mapped through a frozen unembedding produce prompt-dependent vocabulary corrections without model updates.
pHZvxtuPkK.problem: Language models can encode behavior-relevant information internally yet still refuse benign requests, overuse tools, or accept false claims.
pHZvxtuPkK.method: HeadEdit extracts a low-rank behavioral subspace from paired completions. It uses prompt coordinates in that subspace to produce vocabulary-wide logit corrections through the frozen unembedding, without manually selecting target tokens.
pHZvxtuPkK.key_idea: Project final hidden states onto a learned behavioral subspace and map the resulting correction through the frozen unembedding matrix.
pHZvxtuPkK.evidence: Evaluations cover three tasks and three model families, with random-subspace controls, capability checks, and analyses before and after preference tuning.
pHZvxtuPkK.claimed_gains: HeadEdit improves all nine experimental settings across three tasks and three model families.
pHZvxtuPkK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a simple, inexpensive behavioral intervention evaluated across several model-task combinations.
pHZvxtuPkK.main_concern: The projection mechanism substantially overlaps with existing output-embedding and hidden-state steering methods, which need closer comparison.

xf3A7EBait.one_liner: Curvature-paced sparsification and density-dependent optimization adjustments train highly sparse predictive representations without labels or reference runs.
xf3A7EBait.problem: Aggressive representation sparsity shrinks gradients and prevents early formation of informative JEPA features.
xf3A7EBait.method: S²-JEPA adapts sparsification timing using loss curvature and adjusts optimization strength using code density. Both controls operate during training without labels or reference runs.
xf3A7EBait.key_idea: Use loss curvature to pace sparsification and code density to correct optimization strength as sparse features develop.
xf3A7EBait.evidence: Experiments span CIFAR-100, STL-10, ImageNet-100, ImageNet-1K, five transfer datasets, ResNet and ViT backbones, and four optimizers.
xf3A7EBait.claimed_gains: At ~96% sparsity, encoder and projector gains reach 14.4 and 14.5 points; ImageNet-100 retains 97.2% of dense accuracy, ImageNet-1K gains 10.0 points at 95% sparsity, and transfer gains 8.7 points while retrieval uses 12× less storage.
xf3A7EBait.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the controlled diagnosis of sparse-training failures and the design of the experiments.
xf3A7EBait.main_concern: The contribution beyond established sparsification schedules and optimization adjustments needs clearer justification and positioning.

sxS3n9ult2.one_liner: Lightweight routing and ratio controllers jointly select pruning layers and visual-token retention for each vision-language input.
sxS3n9ult2.problem: Fixed visual-token pruning policies cannot adapt computation to input difficulty and token redundancy.
sxS3n9ult2.method: DAPrune trains a routing module for pruning-layer selection and a ratio module for token retention while freezing the base LVLM. Its policy adapts pruning decisions per input within prescribed stages.
sxS3n9ult2.key_idea: Jointly predict where to prune and how many visual tokens to retain from each input.
sxS3n9ult2.evidence: LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT, and Qwen-2.5-VL experiments and ablations accompany a representation-error comparison with fixed pruning under equal average budgets.
sxS3n9ult2.claimed_gains: DAPrune preserves over 98.5% of baseline performance under high FLOPs reduction and adapts LLaVA-1.5 within 3 hours on a single H100 GPU.
sxS3n9ult2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find joint layer-and-ratio adaptation well motivated and recognize performance-efficiency gains with modest controller training.
sxS3n9ult2.main_concern: The degree of adaptivity and distinction from existing adaptive pruning methods remain insufficiently established given predefined stages and candidate settings.

B1koChHWQJ.one_liner: Conditions image detection on deployment support sets using binary meta-learning episodes drawn from class-conditional priors.
B1koChHWQJ.problem: Static image detectors lose accuracy when new generators appear after training.
B1koChHWQJ.method: The framework constructs real-versus-generated episodes from empirical domain priors or synthetic Gaussian mixtures in embedding space. Detectors condition predictions on a small labeled deployment support set.
B1koChHWQJ.key_idea: A prior over class-conditional distributions generates binary training episodes, while labeled deployment examples condition each query prediction.
B1koChHWQJ.evidence: The study compares twelve meta-learning methods with static and support-only detectors and tests support alignment, label noise, and label inversion.
B1koChHWQJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear formulation and diagnostic comparisons across support conditions.
B1koChHWQJ.main_concern: Competitive nearest-centroid results leave the benefit of meta-training over simple support-set adaptation unclear.

O79C6XBzO8.one_liner: Selects hindsight corrections by advice-conditioned response-score differences to train small advisors for frozen language models.
O79C6XBzO8.problem: Hindsight corrections that do not change execution can still harm advisor learning through shared parameters.
O79C6XBzO8.method: AdviSD combines outcome-based reinforcement learning with self-distillation from a hindsight-conditioned advisor. It selects supervision using the magnitude of response-score differences with and without the issued advice.
O79C6XBzO8.key_idea: Score the same recorded executor response with and without advice, then use the contrast magnitude to select hindsight supervision.
O79C6XBzO8.evidence: A shared-parameter theoretical analysis and experiments with Qwen3-8B advisors for Gemini and Claude support the method on BFCL-v3 and EnvScaler.
O79C6XBzO8.claimed_gains: AdviSD outperforms advisor-GRPO by 4.2–6.4 percentage points on BFCL-v3 and by 3.9–5.1 score points on EnvScaler.
O79C6XBzO8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical API-only advising setup and theoretical distinction between correction fitting and execution improvement.
O79C6XBzO8.main_concern: Using Qwen3-8B as the sole advisor backbone limits evidence that the training method generalizes across advisors.

p3ykzmiqf9.one_liner: Retrieves prompt-relevant historical frames and selectively activates memory tokens for consistent streaming video generation.
p3ykzmiqf9.problem: Fixed historical-frame compression cannot supply the different past cues required by changing video narratives.
p3ykzmiqf9.method: MemFlow retrieves historical frames from a global memory bank using the upcoming chunk's text prompt, then selects relevant memory tokens per attention query. Training on memory-intensive scenarios teaches the model to use distant context.
p3ykzmiqf9.key_idea: Text-conditioned frame retrieval supplies historical context, and query-dependent sparse attention selects memory tokens during generation.
p3ykzmiqf9.evidence: Experiments on curated 60-second scripts evaluate character reappearance and scene switching, with ablations of semantic retrieval and memory-forced streaming tuning.
p3ykzmiqf9.claimed_gains: The abstract reports improved long-context consistency with 7.9% speed reduction compared with the LongLive baseline.
p3ykzmiqf9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find dynamic retrieval well motivated for character reappearance and scene changes.
p3ykzmiqf9.main_concern: Inconsistencies between the main text and appendix in training descriptions and baseline results undermine reproducibility.

wTdRx7vi7A.one_liner: Mixes teacher-forced embeddings with predicted soft tokens during supervised fine-tuning while leaving inference unchanged.
wTdRx7vi7A.problem: Soft-token latent reasoning requires complex training yet can underperform conventional chain-of-thought supervised fine-tuning.
wTdRx7vi7A.method: Soft-TF computes soft tokens in a parallel forward pass over the ground-truth sequence and mixes them with teacher-forced embeddings using random convex combinations. It adds no parameters or inference changes.
wTdRx7vi7A.key_idea: Random convex combinations interpolate teacher-forced token embeddings with soft embeddings computed from model predictions.
wTdRx7vi7A.evidence: Experiments cover GSM8K, MATH, MathQA, and AQuA across seven Gemma, Llama, and Mistral models, with five-seed evaluations and mixing ablations.
wTdRx7vi7A.claimed_gains: Soft-TF improves GSM8K by +2.1 to +4.1 points over SFT across seven Gemma, Llama and Mistral models.
wTdRx7vi7A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the simple training change delivers consistent gains across models without changing inference.
wTdRx7vi7A.main_concern: The unspecified model-selection split raises concern that choosing training budgets on evaluation sets inflates reported gains.

VQ8p9uhRVC.one_liner: Uses anchor genes and spatial neighbor profiles to separate native expression from contamination in spatial transcriptomics.
VQ8p9uhRVC.problem: Contamination models leave native and contaminating expression ambiguous when they lack constraints on their decomposition.
VQ8p9uhRVC.method: DeSpotX constrains a deep generative contamination model with genes not natively expressed in each cell cluster. A cluster-masked, distance-weighted neighbor average estimates local contamination.
VQ8p9uhRVC.key_idea: Cluster-specific zero-expression anchor genes constrain the mixture decomposition, while distance-weighted cross-cluster neighbors estimate contamination profiles.
VQ8p9uhRVC.evidence: Spike-in simulations cover five datasets and four spatial transcriptomics platforms; matched scRNA-seq provides an independent expression reference.
VQ8p9uhRVC.claimed_gains: DeSpotX attains the highest AUROC in 27 of 30 settings, exceeds the best baseline by up to 0.12, and retains 94% of within-type signal.
VQ8p9uhRVC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the explicit decomposition problem and spatial contamination model, with experiments supporting practical relevance.
VQ8p9uhRVC.main_concern: Reviewers question the scope and distinctiveness of the anchor-based identifiability claim relative to prior work and the learned model.

6msTAVTIHe.one_liner: Meta-learns token-position and prefix trust constraints using held-out rewards after temporary policy updates.
6msTAVTIHe.problem: Hand-set trust allocations fail to adapt policy-update constraints to how early token changes affect later reasoning.
6msTAVTIHe.method: Meta-TA differentiates query rewards through a support update to learn constraint allocation. A detached warm-up activates the constraints before differentiation, and the selected allocation remains frozen during fresh policy training.
6msTAVTIHe.key_idea: A detached warm-up activates trust constraints so a subsequent differentiable support update exposes allocation parameters to held-out reward gradients.
6msTAVTIHe.evidence: Qwen3-8B-Base experiments compare frozen allocations with CPPO on AIME, MATH-500, and OlympiadBench, including an equal-total-compute Bayesian optimization comparison.
6msTAVTIHe.claimed_gains: The frozen allocation improves three-year AIME Avg@16 over CPPO by 2.9 points, while meta-gradient selection uses 2.8 times fewer query episodes than Bayesian optimization.
6msTAVTIHe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the diagnosis of vanishing allocator gradients and the warm-up procedure that enables meta-gradient learning.
6msTAVTIHe.main_concern: Reviewers question whether meta-gradient selection justifies its added cost over simpler tuning of the same two constraint parameters.

U3q0Ag8hN4.one_liner: Quantizes softmax output heads using class-aware KL curvature and separable feature-class weighting.
U3q0Ag8hN4.problem: Weighted mean-squared error on logits does not directly capture distributional distortion from quantizing softmax output heads.
U3q0Ag8hN4.method: SoftWater derives a quantization objective from a second-order KL expansion. A separable approximation combines one feature-side factorization with class-dependent rescaling estimated in one calibration pass.
U3q0Ag8hN4.key_idea: Class-aware softmax curvature weights feature covariance, with a separable approximation implementing precision allocation through feature factorization and class rescaling.
U3q0Ag8hN4.evidence: Experiments cover five language models from 1B to 32B parameters, multiple head rates, tied and untied heads, and comparisons with WaterSIC.
U3q0Ag8hN4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the distributional objective well motivated and the simple quantizer supported by consistent experimental gains.
U3q0Ag8hN4.main_concern: The separable second-order KL approximation needs stronger validation, especially for low-bit quantization where omitted terms may matter.

dXngQ4yqjS.one_liner: Solution-adapted verification agents and grounded code-taste judges evaluate coding agents on underspecified senior engineering tasks.
dXngQ4yqjS.problem: Existing coding benchmarks test overspecified tasks solely on behavioral correctness because static test suites require pre-fixed interfaces while plain LLM judges sacrifice execution reliability.
dXngQ4yqjS.method: Senior SWE-bench curates 100 real-world feature-building and bug-fixing tasks (50 public, 50 held-out) with underspecified instructions averaging 26% of SWE-Bench Pro's median length. It grades candidate patches using a verification agent that writes executable tests adapted to each solution's design and a taste judge that scores code quality against codebase practices and human references.
dXngQ4yqjS.key_idea: Pair a verification agent that writes tests adapted to each candidate solution with a grounded taste judge on underspecified software tasks.
dXngQ4yqjS.evidence: Forty-six frontier coding agent configurations are evaluated on Senior SWE-bench alongside verifier validation and human-expert agreement studies.
dXngQ4yqjS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark addresses an important gap in evaluating underspecified software engineering work and praise the solution-adapted verification agent and multi-stage task curation.
dXngQ4yqjS.main_concern: All three reviewers question the reliability and subjectivity of the code-taste metric, citing unvalidated patch-length penalties, low inter-expert consistency (~50%), and unverified reliance on human references and inferred codebase conventions.

AGTc9IkKT5.one_liner: Measuring marginal Vendi Score diversity increases over in-distribution features detects out-of-distribution samples in linear time.
AGTc9IkKT5.problem: Post-hoc out-of-distribution detectors commonly rely on overconfident logits or feature-space density estimation under restrictive distributional assumptions.
AGTc9IkKT5.method: Vendi Score Out-Of-Distribution detection (VSOOD) measures how much a test sample increases the cosine-similarity Vendi Score diversity of in-distribution features without density modeling, combining class-conditional local and dataset-level global novelty signals in linear time via a rank-1 approximation.
AGTc9IkKT5.key_idea: Score test samples by how much they increase class-conditional and global Vendi Score similarity diversity of in-distribution features via rank-1 approximation.
AGTc9IkKT5.evidence: Experiments span multiple image classification benchmarks including ImageNet-1K, diverse network architectures, rank ablations, and low-memory subsets down to 1% of training data.
AGTc9IkKT5.claimed_gains: VSOOD retains its OOD detection performance when computed using only 1% of the training data.
AGTc9IkKT5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing post-hoc OOD detection via Vendi Score diversity with a fast linear-time rank-1 approximation is easy to follow, effective on ImageNet-1K, and data-efficient.
AGTc9IkKT5.main_concern: Reviewers note that under the rank-1 cosine approximation the local VSOOD score reduces to a monotonic transform of squared cosine similarity to the leading class principal direction, lacking comparisons to simple principal-direction or class-mean baselines.

CgJy8gpZIr.one_liner: Short-prefix training followed by high-likelihood continuation refinement balances terminal-agent recovery behavior, reliability, and supervision cost.
CgJy8gpZIr.problem: Long teacher trajectories can teach error recovery but increase training cost and encourage unproductive persistence beyond a useful supervision horizon.
CgJy8gpZIr.method: The study varies retained trajectory length and analyzes reliability through a bias–complexity bound. Selective long-horizon refinement first trains on short prefixes, then selects continuations that the warm-start model assigns high likelihood.
CgJy8gpZIr.key_idea: Warm-start on short trajectory prefixes, then refine on longer continuations selected by their likelihood under that model.
CgJy8gpZIr.evidence: Terminal-Bench evaluations compare supervision horizons, repeated-attempt reliability, behavior, training time, and two-stage all-data, random-selection, and low-likelihood controls.
CgJy8gpZIr.claimed_gains: A 12K-token horizon solves 29±0.7 tasks versus 26±0.8 at 16K with 30% less training time, while selective refinement at 16K raises successful attempts from 110±2.7 to 126±2.1 and tasks solved in at least six of eight attempts from 9±0.7 to 14±0.6.
CgJy8gpZIr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the analysis of how supervision length changes reliability, task coverage, recovery behavior, and training cost.
CgJy8gpZIr.main_concern: Much of the reported improvement comes from two-stage training, with smaller and less consistent gains attributable specifically to likelihood selection.

Kz2rjtnKgO.one_liner: Online goal extraction and probabilistic ranking maintain interpretable hypotheses about user intent during open-ended dialogue.
Kz2rjtnKgO.problem: Fixed predefined preference spaces do not capture user goals that remain underspecified or evolve during interaction.
Kz2rjtnKgO.method: Open-Universe Assistance Games represent preferences as changing distributions over natural-language goals. GOOD extracts candidate goals during dialogue and uses LLM-simulated users for probabilistic inference and ranking without large offline datasets.
Kz2rjtnKgO.key_idea: Maintain and update a probability distribution over natural-language goal hypotheses as dialogue provides new evidence.
Kz2rjtnKgO.evidence: Experiments span text-based grocery shopping, AI2-THOR household robotics, coding, and existing multi-turn preference benchmarks.
Kz2rjtnKgO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the importance of evolving user intent and the usefulness of an explicit, inspectable goal representation.
Kz2rjtnKgO.main_concern: Comparisons do not sufficiently isolate probabilistic goal tracking from structured requirement memory and additional computation.

ksA5SnB8s9.one_liner: Streaming quantile matching maps ordinal judge scores toward human rating distributions using a small labeled anchor set.
ksA5SnB8s9.problem: LLM judges exhibit rating-distribution shifts relative to human scores that pointwise calibration may not adequately address.
ksA5SnB8s9.method: SQM matches quantiles of empirical judge and human score distributions on a discrete ordinal scale. The lightweight mapping updates through score counts and accompanies an evaluation framework measuring item error and distributional fidelity.
ksA5SnB8s9.key_idea: Map judge-score quantiles to human-score quantiles while maintaining empirical rating distributions incrementally.
ksA5SnB8s9.evidence: Experiments compare multiple datasets, judge models, and calibration methods using per-item errors and distributional distances, including smaller-versus-larger judge comparisons.
ksA5SnB8s9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a simple, inexpensive way to correct judge rating-scale bias without retraining.
ksA5SnB8s9.main_concern: A deterministic mapping on discrete scores need not transport probability mass correctly and can worsen distributional distance.

MNFqHDmqU6.one_liner: Iterative Gaussian mixture estimation yields an equivalent criterion for mean, covariance, and Wasserstein consistency under synthetic-data reuse.
MNFqHDmqU6.problem: Existing collapse theory often assumes separating fresh real data from generated data, unlike training on mixed uncurated sources.
