MNFqHDmqU6.method: The analysis iteratively estimates a multivariate Gaussian from undifferentiated mixtures of real samples and samples from the previous estimate. It derives a necessary-and-sufficient consistency condition covering mean, covariance, and expected squared 2-Wasserstein error, with convergence-rate analysis.
MNFqHDmqU6.key_idea: Track mean and covariance recursions under real–synthetic mixtures to characterize when continued fresh-data injection ensures consistency.
MNFqHDmqU6.evidence: Theoretical criteria and convergence rates are supported by Gaussian simulations and supplementary CIFAR-10 diffusion-model experiments.
MNFqHDmqU6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the precise consistency criterion and the distinction between asymptotic consistency and practically slow convergence.
MNFqHDmqU6.main_concern: Short, single-seed diffusion experiments with unequal training budgets and warm-start settings do not justify broad extrapolation of the Gaussian results.

u1qufUGdCF.one_liner: Mixing local and averaged stochastic updates preserves personalized linear fixed points while exploiting low heterogeneity for faster convergence.
u1qufUGdCF.problem: Federated linear stochastic approximation needs collaboration benefits without sacrificing agent-specific solutions when heterogeneity is unknown.
u1qufUGdCF.method: PF-LSA mixes each agent's local stochastic update with the average update across agents. Its analysis decomposes error into consensus and disagreement terms to study personalization and speedup across heterogeneity regimes.
u1qufUGdCF.key_idea: Mix update vectors rather than imposing a common solution, separating rapidly decaying consensus error from heterogeneity-dependent disagreement.
u1qufUGdCF.evidence: The paper presents convergence analysis for personalized linear stochastic approximation, including linear speedup in the number of agents under sufficiently low heterogeneity.
u1qufUGdCF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple collaboration mechanism and the clear presentation of personalized federated learning analysis.
u1qufUGdCF.main_concern: Speedup guarantees emphasize low heterogeneity, leaving the practical advantage of personalization in intermediate heterogeneity regimes unclear.

vpECfsKNkT.one_liner: API proxying reconstructs token-faithful trajectories from black-box agent harnesses for asynchronous reinforcement-learning training.
vpECfsKNkT.problem: Porting complex agent harnesses into RL environment interfaces is difficult and can lose token-level training signals.
vpECfsKNkT.method: Polar intercepts model API calls and reconstructs training trajectories while rollout nodes manage runtime preparation, execution, and evaluation asynchronously. Prefix merging combines compatible requests while preserving sampled token IDs and loss masks.
vpECfsKNkT.key_idea: Use model API traffic as the training boundary, reconstructing token-faithful rollouts independently of the harness's internal orchestration.
vpECfsKNkT.evidence: GRPO experiments train Qwen3.5-4B on software-engineering tasks using Codex, Claude Code, Qwen Code, and Pi, with offline generation and reconstruction ablations.
vpECfsKNkT.claimed_gains: Polar improves Qwen3.5-4B on SWE-Bench Verified by 22.6, 4.8, 0.6 and 6.2 points with Codex, Claude Code, Qwen Code and Pi, respectively.
vpECfsKNkT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical API-boundary design for integrating complex harnesses with reinforcement-learning infrastructure.
vpECfsKNkT.main_concern: Experiments confined to a small model and coding workloads do not establish the claimed scalability and breadth across harnesses.

2bchUKjEd4.one_liner: Teacher-trajectory anchoring stabilizes on-policy recovery while repeated gradient-based channel scoring guides structural pruning of trained agents.
2bchUKjEd4.problem: One-shot pruning scores become stale during recovery, while offline or fully on-policy distillation mishandles long-horizon agent errors.
2bchUKjEd4.method: TAP anchors inter-turn context to teacher trajectories but lets the student generate each reasoning-action response under frozen-teacher supervision. After recovery, it re-scores channels with recovery-objective gradients and repeats structural pruning.
2bchUKjEd4.key_idea: Combine student-generated response prefixes with fixed teacher inter-turn contexts, then update channel importance after each recovery stage.
2bchUKjEd4.evidence: ALFWorld and WebShop experiments measure task success, pruning ratios, deployment cost per successful task, and ablations of iterative scoring and recovery context.
2bchUKjEd4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize strong task-level retention under aggressive pruning and useful ablations of pruning and recovery choices.
2bchUKjEd4.main_concern: Modified baseline allocation strategies and confounded recovery comparisons limit attribution of TAP's advantage under matched conditions.

WtFHWQ7rAd.one_liner: Video-level physical plausibility feedback trains an image-conditioning encoder and generator without explicit physical-property labels.
WtFHWQ7rAd.problem: Visually realistic video generators often violate physical laws, while explicit supervision for useful physical representations is unavailable.
WtFHWQ7rAd.method: PhysPilot extracts physics-relevant cues from the input image through PhysEncoder as additional image-to-video conditioning. A top-down reinforcement-learning strategy optimizes the encoder and generator using physical plausibility of final videos.
WtFHWQ7rAd.key_idea: Train image-derived physical conditioning through preferences over final video dynamics instead of supervising physical representations directly.
WtFHWQ7rAd.evidence: Evaluation covers controlled physical tasks, related-task transfer, broader real-world scenarios, user studies, and training-stage and encoder ablations.
WtFHWQ7rAd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize improved physical consistency and useful evaluation across controlled tasks and broader video scenarios.
WtFHWQ7rAd.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate PhysEncoder's contribution from additional DPO training or the frozen pretrained visual representation.

WzhBWnG5UD.one_liner: Distributional answer targets and co-plausibility relationships guide one-shot output-layer editing for uncertainty-aware model responses.
WzhBWnG5UD.problem: Single-answer model editors ignore uncertainty in multi-answer feedback and cannot directly preserve appropriate response distributions across related inputs.
WzhBWnG5UD.method: SoftEdit uses distributions over plausible user-provided answers as editing targets and edits the output layer. Co-plausibility relationships guide generalization to related queries while preserving genuine distributional shifts.
WzhBWnG5UD.key_idea: Edit toward multi-answer distributions and use answer co-plausibility to decide where distributional changes should generalize or remain local.
WzhBWnG5UD.evidence: Evaluation spans three language models, three vision-language models, and two datasets, including batch and sequential editing, ranked feedback, and soft-label baselines.
WzhBWnG5UD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value extending editing beyond single-answer correction and the broad multimodal experimental coverage.
WzhBWnG5UD.main_concern: First-token probabilities multiplied by a binary continuation gate do not establish calibration of complete stochastic responses.

1tuOFRWdnw.one_liner: Recurrent token-state reads train with cross-read matching, then pack into single vectors for inner-product retrieval.
1tuOFRWdnw.problem: Reasoning-intensive retrieval needs multiple query-document correspondences, but conventional late interaction adds retrieval-time cost.
1tuOFRWdnw.method: RLI uses a recurrent head to read token states and a projection shared across reads to match each query read to its best document read during training. At inference, it packs the representations into single vectors and ranks with one inner product.
1tuOFRWdnw.key_idea: Train recurrent read representations through shared-projection best-read matching, then pack them into single-vector retrieval embeddings.
1tuOFRWdnw.evidence: BRIGHT experiments cover four backbones from 0.6B to 4B across three model families, three-seed evaluation, and read-removal ablations.
1tuOFRWdnw.claimed_gains: A 4B RLI achieves 42.42 ± 0.88 nDCG@10 over three seeds, with a best score of 43.41 and a 4.1-point lead over the strongest published retriever-only baseline, while removing reads costs 3.9 to 5.2 nDCG@10.
1tuOFRWdnw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value using late-interaction training signals while retaining a single-vector retrieval interface.
1tuOFRWdnw.main_concern: A single learned read performs nearly as well as multiple reads, leaving the independent benefit of recurrent multi-read structure unclear.

9Hz7XIj7uq.one_liner: A shared diffusion world model supplies imagined training trajectories and local observation predictions for decentralized adversarial defense.
9Hz7XIj7uq.problem: Robust multi-agent policies require costly environment interaction, while globally conditioned world models cannot directly support decentralized test-time defense.
9Hz7XIj7uq.method: MATRIX uses classifier-free guidance to predict observations with either local information or combined local and global information. The same diffusion world model generates trajectories for policy learning and robustification and predicts local observations for test-time detection and correction.
9Hz7XIj7uq.key_idea: Switch one diffusion world model between global conditioning for policy training and local conditioning for decentralized observation correction.
9Hz7XIj7uq.evidence: Experiments cover discrete and continuous control tasks with ablations of policy robustification and test-time defense.
9Hz7XIj7uq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value sharing one world model across sample-efficient policy learning and decentralized observation defense.
9Hz7XIj7uq.main_concern: Unmatched clean baseline performance and insufficient detector evaluation weaken the evidence for adversarial robustness.

DEo5cLf1K3.one_liner: Preference-adjusted null hypotheses and aggregated e-values test multiple-choice benchmarks for model contamination signals.
DEo5cLf1K3.problem: Ordinary answer preferences can mimic benchmark contamination and undermine the reliability of detection scores.
DEo5cLf1K3.method: The paper introduces three detectors with explicit null hypotheses that account for specified response preferences and combines detector e-values to rank evidence against a global null. Controlled testbeds induce known exposure through original, shuffled-choice, and paraphrased questions.
DEo5cLf1K3.key_idea: Adjust contamination tests for response preferences and combine detector-specific e-values across benchmarks.
DEo5cLf1K3.evidence: The abstract reports an audit of 35 models on MMLU, MMLU-Pro, GPQA Diamond, and multiple-choice HLE, plus WikiCutoffQA and SyntheticSourcesQA comparisons with 19 published detectors.
DEo5cLf1K3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the broad audit and controlled testbeds with known benchmark exposure.
DEo5cLf1K3.main_concern: Calibration and transfer beyond one controlled-exposure model remain uncertain, particularly for real human-written benchmarks.

Ep9SLKkvQF.one_liner: Quantifies functional similarity between neural networks directly from weights without probing data using the wARV coefficient.
Ep9SLKkvQF.problem: Standard neural network similarity metrics compare outputs or activations on a finite set of probing inputs, which requires data access and cannot guarantee similarity outside the probe set.
Ep9SLKkvQF.method: The authors introduce the weight-based Ahmad RV coefficient (wARV), a data-free metric that compares neural networks directly through chain weight representations extended across MLPs, convolutions, residual connections, and attention layers. The metric is invariant to parameter-space permutation symmetries and quantifies cross-model variation across architectures and training regimes.
Ep9SLKkvQF.key_idea: Computes a permutation-invariant Ahmad RV coefficient over structural chain-weight representations to estimate neural network similarity without input probing data.
Ep9SLKkvQF.evidence: Evaluated in factorial experiments varying training tasks, architectures, class replacements, and training dynamics, as well as on pretrained ImageNet models.
Ep9SLKkvQF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the goal of a data-free, permutation-invariant weight-space similarity metric applicable across diverse neural architectures interesting and well-explored in factorial task experiments.
Ep9SLKkvQF.main_concern: Within the same training task, wARV correlates weakly with actual output logit similarity (Spearman 0.18), prior data-free similarity literature is omitted, and parts of the experimental setup lack clarity.

5aH1G4WwDg.one_liner: Corrects straight-through activation gradients in binarized neural networks using an empirical-Fisher diagonal curvature approximation.
5aH1G4WwDg.problem: Training binarized neural networks with the straight-through estimator (STE) produces biased activation gradients because applying the chain rule through a discontinuous quantizer ignores finite loss jumps between quantization levels.
5aH1G4WwDg.method: The authors derive a second-order expansion of the population loss jump across adjacent quantization levels, yielding an activation-gradient correction term proportional to the quantization residual and the diagonal curvature of the downstream loss. They approximate this diagonal curvature using a moving-average empirical-Fisher proxy and apply the corrected backward rule during the final 10% of training.
5aH1G4WwDg.key_idea: Adds a second-order activation gradient correction proportional to the quantization residual and an empirical-Fisher diagonal curvature proxy during late-stage binarized network training.
5aH1G4WwDg.evidence: Evaluated on binarized Llama-style language models up to 1.6B parameters trained with QuEST and CAGE.
5aH1G4WwDg.claimed_gains: Reduces perplexity by 1.0–3.1% across binarized Llama-style language models up to 1.6B parameters.
5aH1G4WwDg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the second-order distributional analysis of activation quantization jumps is clearly presented and yields a consistent perplexity reduction when applied at the end of training.
5aH1G4WwDg.main_concern: Perplexity gains are modest and evaluated on a single random seed, training memory and runtime overheads from tracking activation second moments are not reported, and distinctions from prior weight-curvature methods need expansion.

cL8CBkgsKQ.one_liner: Preserves exact sample realizability across sequential differentially private component learners using LabelBoost and two alternating sample reservoirs.
cL8CBkgsKQ.problem: In realizable differentially private learning of k-component hypotheses, an approximate private choice of one component can destroy exact realizability of the labeled sample for subsequent components.
cL8CBkgsKQ.method: The framework restores exact realizability after each private component learning step using the LabelBoost procedure and recycles data through two alternating reservoirs with macro-block privacy analysis. Instantiating this framework with IPConcave and a private quasi-concave optimizer yields improved sample complexity bounds for learning d-dimensional halfspaces over a finite grid.
cL8CBkgsKQ.key_idea: Combines LabelBoost relabeling with two alternating data reservoirs to guarantee exact realizability for each sequential component learner at O-tilde(sqrt(k)/epsilon) privacy overhead.
cL8CBkgsKQ.evidence: Supported by theoretical sample-complexity and privacy proofs for k-component realizable PAC learning, boolean compositions, and d-dimensional halfspaces over a finite grid of size L.
cL8CBkgsKQ.claimed_gains: Achieves a realizable privacy overhead of O-tilde(sqrt(k)/epsilon) and improves d-dimensional halfspace sample complexity over a finite grid of size L to O-tilde((1/(epsilon * alpha)) * min{d^2.5 log* L, d^2.5 + d^1.5 2^{log* L}}).
cL8CBkgsKQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the sequential realizability-preserving framework and the improved dimensional sample-complexity bounds for privately learning halfspaces.
cL8CBkgsKQ.main_concern: A simpler modified-score LabelBoost variant from recent literature may achieve the same rate via standard advanced composition without the two-reservoir construction, and proof details linking internal grid size N to L need clarification.

oNxLR0Q6JI.one_liner: Measures how much activation monitors rely on native behavior-generating model states versus altered or re-encoded transcript states.
oNxLR0Q6JI.problem: It is unclear how much the predictive accuracy of internal activation monitors depends on privileged access to the exact behavior-generating forward pass rather than information recoverable from altered or re-encoded transcripts.
oNxLR0Q6JI.method: Holding target model, monitor architecture, and training labels fixed, the authors compare activation monitors trained and evaluated on native execution states against monitors running on controlled counterfactual transcripts (such as paraphrased text, altered chat formatting, or system-prompted reconstructions). They also analyze performance on examples whose behavioral labels flip under paraphrasing and compare against answer logit margins.
oNxLR0Q6JI.key_idea: Compares activation monitors on native execution traces against controlled transcript re-encodings to isolate the value of privileged access to original model computations.
oNxLR0Q6JI.evidence: Evaluated across up to four language models and two counterfactual monitoring tasks, including paraphrase-disagreement subsets and logit-margin baselines.
oNxLR0Q6JI.claimed_gains: Native-trained monitors outperform the strongest counterfactual controls by up to 0.014 AUROC overall, while most monitoring performance is recovered without the original trace.
oNxLR0Q6JI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled experimental design isolating original computational states from transcript re-encodings and find the larger native advantage on paraphrase-sensitive examples insightful.
oNxLR0Q6JI.main_concern: Experiments are restricted to single-token responses with thinking disabled, and combining altered-state monitors with simple output confidence margins is not tested to see if the small 0.014 AUROC native gap disappears.

tVIzJu9F3L.one_liner: Accelerates exact top-k sparse attention routing by caching persistent per-head temporal working sets and page upper bounds.
tVIzJu9F3L.problem: Sparse attention reduces value aggregation to top-k tokens, but finding those tokens still requires scanning the entire key cache at every decoding step.
tVIzJu9F3L.method: Recurrent Attention Routing (RAR) exploits temporal working sets by having each attention head retain candidate keys and page-level score maxima from earlier cache visits. At each step, incoming queries score the retained working-set candidates and newly appended keys, revisiting only cache pages whose certified upper bounds allow them to enter the top-k selection.
tVIzJu9F3L.key_idea: Caches per-head candidate keys and page score upper bounds across decoding steps to skip scanning KV cache pages that provably cannot enter the top-k.
tVIzJu9F3L.evidence: Supported by an exact top-k recovery proof, agreement checks over 65 million head routes, and 128K-context latency benchmarks on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B.
tVIzJu9F3L.claimed_gains: At 128K context, RAR speeds up attention routing by 3.9x on Llama-3.1-8B and 3.6x on Qwen3-8B, yielding a 1.4x token-decoding speedup on both models while recovering the exact exhaustive top-k.
tVIzJu9F3L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the identification of persistent temporal working sets and the certified upper-bound mechanism that accelerates routing while preserving exact exhaustive top-k selections.
tVIzJu9F3L.main_concern: The paper omits empirical comparisons and discussion of closely related candidate-reuse methods (such as TidalDecode, LServe, and ReTopK), and timing evaluations rely on only four PG-19 books with two repetitions on 8B models.

LOY4KMF2SC.one_liner: Adapts PCA for time-series anomaly detection using multi-resolution Toeplitz covariance, cross-resolution consensus, and FFT-aligned shape residuals.
LOY4KMF2SC.problem: Standard PCA treats time-series windows as static vectors without modeling multi-scale temporal durations or phase-shifted recurrent patterns, while deep anomaly detectors are computationally heavy.
LOY4KMF2SC.method: Time-series Adaptive PCA (TAP) combines three components: Multi-Resolution PCA using Toeplitz covariance compression to capture anomalies across window scales, Cross-Resolution Evidence Consensus to fuse multi-scale anomaly scores, and Shape-Residual PCA using batched FFT alignment to detect deviations from recurrent normal patterns.
LOY4KMF2SC.key_idea: Combines Toeplitz-compressed multi-resolution window PCA and FFT-aligned shape-residual PCA with cross-resolution score consensus for CPU-fast time-series anomaly detection.
LOY4KMF2SC.evidence: Evaluated across 23 public time-series anomaly detection dataset collections (including TSB-AD-U under VUS-PR) on a single CPU core.
LOY4KMF2SC.claimed_gains: Improves overall detection performance over the second-best method by 17.9% while running 10 times faster, averaging 2.5 seconds per benchmark series and processing approximately 28,000 points per second on a single CPU core.
LOY4KMF2SC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the strong VUS-PR accuracy and fast single-core CPU throughput achieved by extending PCA with multi-resolution Toeplitz and FFT-aligned shape-residual branches.
LOY4KMF2SC.main_concern: The paper omits discussion and comparison with classical time-series PCA variants (such as SSA), lacks timestamp-level analysis showing where multi-scale gains occur, and introduces multiple heuristic fusion hyperparameters.

KdCdB5V6ku.one_liner: Adds a linear injection term to predictive coding energy so physical relaxation computes generative velocity gradients and trains via Equilibrium Propagation.
KdCdB5V6ku.problem: Sampling and training energy-based or flow generative models normally require backpropagation through network layers at every integration step, which is incompatible with local analog neuromorphic hardware.
KdCdB5V6ku.method: PotentialEP modifies a predictive coding network's energy function with a single linear injection term so that its physical equilibrium relaxation inherently yields the spatial gradient of an Energy Matching potential at the visible layer. This allows pretrained Energy Matching models to be sampled purely by relaxation and enables end-to-end backpropagation-free generative training via Equilibrium Propagation.
KdCdB5V6ku.key_idea: Augments a predictive coding energy with a linear injection term so equilibrium relaxation directly outputs the Energy Matching velocity gradient for backprop-free sampling and Equilibrium Propagation training.
KdCdB5V6ku.evidence: Evaluated via theoretical O(gamma) equilibrium-gradient correspondence proofs and image generation experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-32.
KdCdB5V6ku.claimed_gains: Matches a backprop-trained Energy Matching model's FID to within 0.04 via relaxation sampling on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-32, reproduces backpropagation parameter updates with 0.9998 cosine similarity, and reaches 3.33 FID on unconditional CIFAR-10 when trained end-to-end.
KdCdB5V6ku.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theoretical link showing that predictive coding relaxation with a linear injection computes the Energy Matching gradient clever and well-suited to neuromorphic substrates.
KdCdB5V6ku.main_concern: The software implementation still uses autograd in error coordinates during single-sweep equilibrium finding and negative-sample generation, prior CelebA Equilibrium Propagation generative work is under-discussed, and the prose is overly dense.

IG8fw7MujT.one_liner: Indexes single-artifact summaries and artifact-pair structural links from past reasoning traces to guide agent corpus retrieval.
IG8fw7MujT.problem: Agents solving repeated tasks over a shared document or code corpus lack persistent memory anchored to specific corpus artifacts, leading to incomplete evidence retrieval and redundant search.
IG8fw7MujT.method: ExperienceIndex is a framework-agnostic middleware layer that extracts and indexes two types of artifact-grounded memory from prior task-solving traces: single-artifact experiences summarizing an item's task utility and artifact-pair experiences capturing relational links between items. At inference time, it retrieves these artifact experiences to guide the agent toward complete relevant artifact sets.
IG8fw7MujT.key_idea: Extracts and indexes single-artifact utility summaries and pairwise artifact relationships from past reasoning traces to guide evidence retrieval on future corpus queries.
IG8fw7MujT.evidence: Evaluated across seven datasets spanning conversations, code (SWE-bench), scientific literature (ScholarQA), and relational tables (Spider, MMQA).
IG8fw7MujT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that anchoring agent memory directly to corpus artifacts and incremental trace extraction is a practical, lightweight alternative to full-corpus offline enrichment.
IG8fw7MujT.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate single-artifact versus artifact-pair links, small 100-task test splits with random 80/20 partitioning risk near-duplicate leakage without confidence intervals, and classic case-based reasoning literature is overlooked.

OWX14VkewV.one_liner: Encodes reusable text chunks behind a fixed offline surrogate prefix and discards the prefix before storing KV caches.
OWX14VkewV.problem: Encoding reusable text chunks in isolation for non-prefix KV cache composition creates severe attention-routing mismatch when chunks are later composed under non-empty contexts.
OWX14VkewV.method: SurroKV is a training-free offline cache construction method that prepends a fixed, request-independent surrogate text context before encoding each reusable chunk and then discards the surrogate's KV entries, storing only the chunk's KV cache. This pre-conditions the chunk's keys and values to reduce attention-routing mismatch during online composition and selective recomputation without increasing cache size or online latency.
OWX14VkewV.key_idea: Conditions offline chunk KV cache construction on a fixed surrogate prefix that is discarded before storage to mitigate attention-routing mismatch during non-prefix reuse.
OWX14VkewV.evidence: Evaluated across RULER, LongBench, and HELMET on multiple LLMs and integrated with four existing selective KV recomputation methods.
OWX14VkewV.claimed_gains: Improves accuracy by 2.1%–12.7% relative to existing non-prefix KV cache reuse methods across RULER, LongBench, and HELMET with no additional online latency.
OWX14VkewV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the training-free, zero-overhead offline modification that reduces attention-routing error and consistently improves accuracy across multiple models and recomputation budgets.
OWX14VkewV.main_concern: The paper lacks direct experimental comparisons and conceptual differentiation against closely related shared-prefix KV caching methods (APE and CacheClip) and does not justify why a fixed Wikipedia surrogate satisfies the theoretical conditions across domains.

EOPBKceYco.one_liner: Diagnoses the search-priority gap in multi-hop RAG when unselective bridge-entity facts distract planners from selective anchor queries.
EOPBKceYco.problem: Multi-hop RAG planners decompose questions along logical dependencies without prioritizing how selectively each candidate query narrows the search space.
EOPBKceYco.method: The authors construct 2,541 controlled question pairs from 2WikiMultiHopQA by adding true but low-selectivity Wikidata facts about the bridge entity while keeping the selective anchor relation and answer unchanged. They analyze retrieval trajectories across decomposition, iterative, and agentic RAG systems and evaluate a few-shot prompt that instructs planners to prioritize high-selectivity anchor constraints.
EOPBKceYco.key_idea: Adds true but low-selectivity bridge-entity facts to multi-hop questions to expose and measure how retrieval planners fail to prioritize the most selective anchor query.
EOPBKceYco.evidence: Evaluated on 2,541 controlled 2WikiMultiHopQA question pairs across decomposition-based, iterative, and agentic RAG systems including PlanRAG and AceSearcher-14B.
EOPBKceYco.claimed_gains: Adding true but less selective bridge facts drops PlanRAG accuracy from 67.1% to 31.0%, while a few-shot anchor-prioritizing prompt raises AceSearcher-14B accuracy from 50.8% to 66.7%.
EOPBKceYco.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating logical validity from retrieval selectivity via controlled fact-injection question pairs reveals a clear and underexplored failure mode in multi-hop RAG planners.
EOPBKceYco.main_concern: Trajectory evidence leaves some ambiguity between query formulation failures and entity extraction errors from retrieved passages, evaluation is limited to two-hop questions, and the proposed fix is only a prompt heuristic.

AEAYnCoWt6.one_liner: Probes per-head CFG activation differences in unified VLMs to selectively tune attention-head guidance scales at inference time.
AEAYnCoWt6.problem: Unified vision-language models use a single shared Transformer backbone for both text-to-image and image-to-text generation, but standard classifier-free guidance applies a uniform scale across all attention heads regardless of their sensitivity to conditioning.
AEAYnCoWt6.method: The authors probe attention heads across autoregressive and masked-diffusion unified VLMs by measuring activation differences between positive and negative CFG branches, uncovering a stable subset of condition-sensitive heads in both generation directions. Based on this probe, HeadTuned-CFG selectively adjusts conditional guidance scales at the individual attention-head level during inference without retraining.
AEAYnCoWt6.key_idea: Measures per-head activation differences between conditional and unconditional CFG branches to selectively modulate guidance strength across attention heads at inference time.
AEAYnCoWt6.evidence: Evaluated on two unified VLMs spanning autoregressive and masked-diffusion paradigms across both text-to-image and image-to-text generation benchmarks (including MJHQ).
AEAYnCoWt6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate connecting mechanistic probing of bi-directional unified VLM attention heads to a practical, training-free head-level CFG intervention.
AEAYnCoWt6.main_concern: The unnormalized activation-difference probe may reflect raw head activation magnitude or layer depth rather than semantic specialization, and distinctions from prior head-level guidance methods (HeadHunter, NAG) are under-articulated.

G1NMTIej4w.one_liner: Evaluates multinomial concept localization and steering representations across geometries by sampling steering vectors and measuring concept coverage diversity.
G1NMTIej4w.problem: Concept localization and activation steering benchmarks primarily assume binary or one-dimensional concepts, leaving multi-valued concepts with affine, subspace, or manifold geometries poorly evaluated.
G1NMTIej4w.method: MAxBench extends concept steering evaluation to multinomial concepts by sampling vectors from a recovered concept representation (such as directions, linear subspaces, or affine subspaces) and steering language model generations. It evaluates representations by combining concept injection success, fluency, and instruction following with a Diversity score measuring coverage across the concept's multiple values.
G1NMTIej4w.key_idea: Benchmarks multi-valued concept representations of arbitrary geometry by sampling steering interventions from the representation and scoring output concept coverage diversity alongside steering success.
G1NMTIej4w.evidence: Evaluated across multiple representation geometry families (directions, linear subspaces, affine subspaces), models, and six multinomial concepts against prompting baselines.
G1NMTIej4w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending steering evaluation beyond binary directions to multinomial concepts and testing the role of affine offsets and coverage diversity is a useful research direction.
G1NMTIej4w.main_concern: The benchmark only evaluates six concepts, represents an incremental extension of AxBench, and uses an entropy-based diversity normalization that can exceed its theoretical upper bound when outputs contain multiple entities.

OTjt9xm28s.one_liner: Characterizes which downstream tasks survive two-view self-supervised learning via spectral alignment of task posteriors with cross-view stable modes.
OTjt9xm28s.problem: Enforcing representation consistency across two augmented views of an instance in self-supervised learning does not specify which downstream semantic tasks will remain linearly recoverable.
OTjt9xm28s.method: The authors define semantic recoverability as the fraction of a task's posterior score captured by the representation's function space and prove that for centered, whitened representations it determines directional class-distance normalized variance (CDNV) and few-shot nearest-centroid accuracy. Analyzing a canonical two-view SSL objective, they derive a closed-form spectral characterization showing that a task survives to the extent its posterior lies in the leading cross-view stable modes of the two-view operator.
OTjt9xm28s.key_idea: Links downstream few-shot and linear-probe recoverability in centered, whitened SSL representations to the projection of the task posterior onto the leading eigenmodes of the two-view augmentation operator.
OTjt9xm28s.evidence: Validated via theoretical proofs on directional CDNV, factorial centroid geometry, and spectral subspaces alongside experiments on synthetic and real datasets across multiple SSL methods.
OTjt9xm28s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theoretical synthesis connecting spectral two-view augmentation operators, posterior energy capture, directional CDNV, and multitask centroid geometry clear and meaningful.
OTjt9xm28s.main_concern: The linear posterior-capture metric misses nonlinearly separable tasks, and the paper needs clearer differentiation from prior spectral SSL and directional CDNV analyses.

qQdbDVtyDg.one_liner: Fine-tunes an LLM on over 100,000 Bayesian optimization trajectories to jointly propose candidates and predict calibrated surrogate statistics.
qQdbDVtyDg.problem: Bayesian optimization excels at numerical refinement but ignores natural-language domain context, whereas prompting LLMs gives strong warm starts that quickly plateau as numerical observations accumulate.
qQdbDVtyDg.method: SemanticOpt constructs over 100,000 optimization trajectories combining context-informed LLM initializations with multiple Bayesian optimization solvers across synthetic and real-world-like function spaces. An LLM is supervised fine-tuned on these trajectories to jointly output candidate configurations and predict objective values, uncertainty, and failure probabilities without fitting a separate Gaussian process surrogate.
qQdbDVtyDg.key_idea: Fine-tunes a language model on Bayesian optimization trajectories with semantic metadata to jointly generate candidate points and predict objective mean, uncertainty, and failure probability.
qQdbDVtyDg.evidence: Evaluated across 42 scientific and engineering black-box optimization problems under full-context, counterfactual, mismatched, and shared-initialization settings.
qQdbDVtyDg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the systematic pipeline unifying semantic warm-starts with BO trajectory imitation and the shared-initialization experiments separating warm-start gains from iterative refinement.
qQdbDVtyDg.main_concern: The paper does not experimentally compare against existing LLM-assisted BO baselines (such as LLAMBO, LGBO, or GOLLuM) or ablate the individual contributions of multi-teacher selection and auxiliary surrogate prediction targets.

sEQg5ZmRL4.one_liner: Trains a single preference-conditioned LLM for multi-objective alignment against an adversarial Dirichlet preference distribution updated via mirror descent.
sEQg5ZmRL4.problem: Training a single preference-conditioned LLM on a fixed preference distribution leaves difficult trade-off regions of the preference simplex under-trained.
sEQg5ZmRL4.method: MAESTRO trains a single prompt-conditioned policy end-to-end with reinforcement learning against an adaptive adversarial preference distribution parameterized as a Dirichlet distribution. During training, online mirror descent updates the Dirichlet concentration parameters toward preference weight vectors where the current policy achieves the worst scalarized performance.
sEQg5ZmRL4.key_idea: Updates a Dirichlet preference-sampling distribution via online mirror descent toward worst-performing trade-off weights during single-model preference-conditioned RL alignment.
sEQg5ZmRL4.evidence: Evaluated on HH-RLHF, BeaverTails, and a summarization task with up to three objectives over five random seeds, including held-out reward model re-scoring and fixed-Dirichlet ablations.
sEQg5ZmRL4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adaptively shifting the preference-sampling distribution during single-model multi-objective RL is simple, low-overhead, and well-supported by fixed-Dirichlet ablations across three datasets.
sEQg5ZmRL4.main_concern: The implemented algorithm replaces the theoretical scalarized-return gradient with a biased batch-relative rank heuristic, lacks visualizations tracking how the Dirichlet distribution shifts during training, and offers incremental novelty over existing preference-conditioned MOA methods.

Sdxjs9k4iP.one_liner: Uses a lightweight auxiliary adapter to bound sequential-parallel decoding inconsistency when unmasking tokens in diffusion language models.
Sdxjs9k4iP.problem: Parallel decoding in masked diffusion language models loses accuracy when simultaneously unmasked tokens deviate from the joint distribution followed by sequential one-by-one unmasking.
Sdxjs9k4iP.method: Parallel Inconsistency Guidance (PIG) trains a lightweight ~2M-parameter auxiliary adapter to predict the divergence between parallel and sequential decoding from a single backbone forward pass. At inference, candidate masked positions are traversed in order of decreasing confidence and added to the parallel unmasking set until the cumulative predicted inconsistency exceeds a threshold.
Sdxjs9k4iP.key_idea: Estimates cumulative parallel-versus-sequential unmasking divergence with a 2M-parameter single-pass adapter to greedily admit high-confidence tokens up to an inconsistency budget.
Sdxjs9k4iP.evidence: Evaluated on LLaDA-8B Instruct and NemotronDiffusion-3B Instruct across GSM8K, MATH500, MBPP, HumanEval, and MMLU against Fast-dLLM, DAPD, KLASS, and EB-sampler.
Sdxjs9k4iP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the formulation of directly predicting parallel-versus-sequential decoding inconsistency via a tiny ~2M-parameter adapter and note substantial accuracy gains at high tokens-per-forward-pass.
Sdxjs9k4iP.main_concern: The adapter and calibration tables require offline per-backbone trajectory harvesting, and ablations do not test a confidence-only cumulative budget rule to prove gains come from the learned predictor rather than the cumulative stopping rule.

mo7xkP5u5M.one_liner: Generates block-level predictive states via a rectified-flow prior and decodes token blocks in parallel with a block-causal decoder.
mo7xkP5u5M.problem: Continuous diffusion language models struggle to model fine-grained discrete token choices directly within the joint continuous latent distribution.
mo7xkP5u5M.method: Predictive-State Flows (PSF) partitions a sequence into K blocks and associates each block with a predictive state computed solely from preceding context. A rectified-flow prior generates the sequence of predictive states, and a block-causal decoder generates all blocks in parallel while decoding autoregressively within each block.
mo7xkP5u5M.key_idea: Divides generation between a rectified-flow prior producing K block-level predictive states and a block-causal decoder resolving tokens in parallel across blocks.
mo7xkP5u5M.evidence: Evaluated on unconditional OpenWebText generation with a 197M-parameter model against ELF-B, BD3-LM, and a same-data autoregressive baseline, with ablations on block length, landing targets, and realization codes.
mo7xkP5u5M.claimed_gains: On unconditional OpenWebText generation, a 197M-parameter model with K=8 achieves a generative perplexity of 22.8 at entropy 5.16 using 0.31 TFLOPs per 1024-token document, compared with 24.0 and 7.2 TFLOPs for ELF-B with 32 sampling steps.
mo7xkP5u5M.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the division of labor between the flow prior and parallel block-causal decoder, noting substantial FLOP reductions and useful ablations.
mo7xkP5u5M.main_concern: The content-state control reuses components trained under predictive states and the gap persists when bypassing the prior, leaving the cause of the predictive-state advantage unclear alongside a complex multi-stage training procedure.

xKHNlGXJzj.one_liner: Estimates causal importance among chain-of-thought reasoning units by fitting a structural causal model over log-probability perturbations.
xKHNlGXJzj.problem: Existing methods lack faithful local and causal explanations of how individual steps in a specific chain-of-thought trace depend on prior steps.
xKHNlGXJzj.method: AttriCoT constructs a structural causal model over units in a chain-of-thought trace and relates each unit to the log probability of generating subsequent output units. It estimates importance parameters in this model using O(U) non-generative forward passes over U units.
xKHNlGXJzj.key_idea: Fits a linear structural causal model to log-probability changes of subsequent reasoning units under O(U) unit-removal interventions.
xKHNlGXJzj.evidence: Evaluated via perturbation curves across 5 datasets and 4 reasoning models, plus a regenerative evaluation on GSM8K.
xKHNlGXJzj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the method is conceptually clear, computationally efficient with O(U) forward passes, and evaluated across multiple reasoning models and datasets.
xKHNlGXJzj.main_concern: The primary evaluation metric closely mirrors the log-probability objective optimized by AttriCoT, potentially favoring it over distribution-based baselines, while the linear perturbation approach is incremental over existing attribution methods.

vfj1rb7yk1.one_liner: Trains a sequence-to-sequence retokenizer with task rewards to re-segment inputs using a frozen language model's existing vocabulary.
vfj1rb7yk1.problem: Predefined generic tokenizers are often poorly suited to specific downstream tasks, while retraining a tokenizer changes the vocabulary and is infeasible for frozen or closed-weight language models.
vfj1rb7yk1.method: The authors propose a sequence-to-sequence retokenizer that maps an input token sequence to an alternative valid token sequence within the original vocabulary while preserving the exact string content. The retokenizer is trained using reinforcement learning from task-specific rewards requiring only black-box access to the frozen LLM.
vfj1rb7yk1.key_idea: Learns a string-preserving sequence-to-sequence retokenizer via reinforcement learning to remap tokens within a frozen model's fixed vocabulary.
vfj1rb7yk1.evidence: Evaluated on arithmetic, character manipulation, and code understanding tasks against canonical, hand-designed, and compute-matched tokenization baselines.
vfj1rb7yk1.claimed_gains: Across arithmetic, character manipulation, and code understanding tasks, learned retokenization improves accuracy over default tokenization by 10% on average.
vfj1rb7yk1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the black-box retokenization approach intuitive and effective at improving performance on tokenization-sensitive tasks without modifying the underlying LLM.
vfj1rb7yk1.main_concern: The evaluation is restricted to a narrow set of tasks known to suffer from default tokenization, requires retraining per task and model, and adds transformer inference overhead.

Gz6H1YZtjC.one_liner: Eliminates word-duration timing leakage in non-invasive brain-to-text decoding by processing word-aligned signal windows independently rather than jointly.
Gz6H1YZtjC.problem: Jointly encoding overlapping word-aligned brain-recording windows leaks inter-word timing durations, allowing decoders to predict words without using actual brain activity.
Gz6H1YZtjC.method: The authors show that synthetic signals without brain information reproduce reported joint-decoding accuracy due to window overlap, and modify the pipeline to encode each word window independently. Removing this timing shortcut allows the decoder to learn word-specific neural representations that benefit from repetition aggregation and LLM rescoring.
Gz6H1YZtjC.key_idea: Processes word-aligned brain-recording windows independently instead of jointly across a sentence to prevent the network from exploiting inter-word interval durations.
Gz6H1YZtjC.evidence: Evaluated on non-invasive MEG brain recordings and synthetic timing-only control signals across word classification and sentence reconstruction tasks.
Gz6H1YZtjC.claimed_gains: The prior joint method reaches 22.0% balanced accuracy on synthetic signals containing no brain information compared with 22.3% on real brain recordings, whereas independent decoding with repetition and an LLM reaches 36.6% WER.
Gz6H1YZtjC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers strongly value the discovery and clear synthetic demonstration of timing-shortcut leakage in word-aligned non-invasive brain decoding.
Gz6H1YZtjC.main_concern: The positive sentence-reconstruction results rely on pseudo-sentences assembled from repeated word occurrences using known reference word identities and domain-prompted LLM rescoring rather than true continuous sentence decoding.

mya2uCt7Xs.one_liner: Formulates LLM-driven program evolution as Sequential Monte Carlo sampling from a reward-tilted target distribution.
mya2uCt7Xs.problem: Existing LLM-driven program evolution frameworks rely on heuristic component designs and lack theoretical convergence guarantees.
mya2uCt7Xs.method: SMCEvolve casts program search as sampling from a reward-tilted target distribution approximated via a Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) sampler. This formulation yields adaptive parent resampling, a mixture of mutation with acceptance, and automatic convergence control with finite-sample guarantees.
mya2uCt7Xs.key_idea: Approximates a reward-tilted program distribution using Sequential Monte Carlo with adaptive parent resampling, mutation-acceptance kernels, and automatic termination.
mya2uCt7Xs.evidence: Supported by finite-sample theoretical guarantees and experiments across math, algorithm efficiency, symbolic regression, and end-to-end ML research benchmarks.
mya2uCt7Xs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the coherent probabilistic framing that unifies parent selection, mutation acceptance, and stopping rules under Sequential Monte Carlo alongside strong empirical results.
mya2uCt7Xs.main_concern: The theoretical convergence guarantee holds for an intermediate distribution rather than the true reward-tilted target because black-box LLM mutation kernels do not preserve invariance, and baselines use fixed budgets against SMCEvolve's adaptive stopping.

gwk3EQeQte.one_liner: Stabilizes GRPO alignment for flow-matching generators by calibrating per-step policy importance ratios using transition-kernel path variance.
gwk3EQeQte.problem: In multi-step flow-matching reinforcement learning, policy importance ratios drift below one, disperse across denoising steps, and clip asymmetrically, causing late-stage training instability.
gwk3EQeQte.method: The authors show that importance-ratio drift and spread are governed by a per-step path variance determined by the sampler's Gaussian transition kernel and split by mean-reduced log-probabilities into centering and variance scales. Their method, lambda-Controlled GRPO, estimates this quantity during training to calibrate and budget variance across denoising steps without hand-tuned clip schedules.
gwk3EQeQte.key_idea: Computes per-step path variance from the Gaussian transition kernel to analytically center and calibrate importance-ratio variance across flow-matching denoising steps.
gwk3EQeQte.evidence: Supported by theoretical Gaussian moment derivations and image generation alignment experiments on the FLUX backbone including GenEval and Hard-OCR.
gwk3EQeQte.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the theoretical connection between the Gaussian transition kernel and timestep-dependent importance-ratio instability in Flow-GRPO.
gwk3EQeQte.main_concern: Empirical gains over baselines on tasks like GenEval and Hard-OCR are inconsistent or statistically inconclusive, and ablations do not cleanly separate the effects of calibration and damping from prior analytic centering.

IOadi6LJPR.one_liner: MemOIR conditions driving diffusion on instance-labeled 3D blocks and repositions cached object tokens when instances reappear.
IOadi6LJPR.problem: Driving generators underspecify the static world and ego motion, while frame-level memory is costly and cannot identify individual instances.
IOadi6LJPR.method: MemOIR renders dynamic and static instances as view-space 3D blocks encoding class, identity, and occlusion. Object-level KV memory caches tokens from complete observations and re-embeds them at the current projected block locations when objects return.
IOadi6LJPR.key_idea: Use persistent instance identities to retrieve object-specific KV tokens and projected 3D geometry to place them in new frames.
IOadi6LJPR.evidence: Driving-generation experiments assess instance placement, ego-motion control, unseen maneuvers, and returning-vehicle identity, with memory ablations reported in reviews.
IOadi6LJPR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find structured scene conditioning and instance-addressable memory a coherent approach to controllable, consistent driving videos.
IOadi6LJPR.main_concern: Different inputs, conditioning resources, and training settings across methods confound attribution of the reported control and quality gains.

504XPhQiFT.one_liner: A generative weight model adapts robot policies from short target-domain trajectories without target rewards or domain parameters.
504XPhQiFT.problem: Robot policies need rapid adaptation to unknown dynamics when target rewards and domain parameters are unavailable.
504XPhQiFT.method: Generative On-Policy Learners condition on an initial policy and a few interaction episodes to generate updated policy parameters. Training imitates on-policy reinforcement-learning trajectories in a behavior-aligned latent space.
504XPhQiFT.key_idea: Generate policy updates in a behavior-aligned latent space conditioned on the current policy and recent target-domain interactions.
504XPhQiFT.evidence: Continuous-control evaluations include out-of-distribution quadruped locomotion, drone racing, and real-drone sim-to-real adaptation.
504XPhQiFT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value adaptation without target rewards or privileged dynamics information and the real-world drone demonstration.
504XPhQiFT.main_concern: Unequal source-training budgets make it difficult to separate the method's contribution from its greater training resources.

w3WrJ9IVVL.one_liner: Chronological versus shuffled fact training tests how temporal data order shapes representation sharing and later knowledge updates.
w3WrJ9IVVL.problem: How temporal changes in pretraining facts influence knowledge storage and future updates remains unclear.
w3WrJ9IVVL.method: The study trains models on changing facts presented chronologically or shuffled across periods, then measures update behavior and representation structure. It also examines evidence of coupled updates in OLMo-2-7B.
w3WrJ9IVVL.key_idea: Vary temporal fact ordering while holding facts fixed to test whether updates remain local or propagate through shared representations.
w3WrJ9IVVL.evidence: Controlled synthetic knowledge experiments examine update coupling, gradient similarity, temporal noise, and model size, with a correlational study in OLMo-2-7B.
w3WrJ9IVVL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the controlled data-order comparisons and their evidence that training order affects knowledge storage and updating.
w3WrJ9IVVL.main_concern: Generalization beyond structured synthetic settings remains uncertain because the real-model evidence is correlational and limited to one model.

hPO7EzwyGt.one_liner: Backward dependency-graph credit and gold-answer likelihood changes reshape GRPO advantages into step-specific reasoning updates.
hPO7EzwyGt.problem: Trajectory rewards and local importance scores do not distinguish redundant reasoning steps from steps supporting later deductions.
hPO7EzwyGt.method: RECAP propagates credit backward from the final answer through an LLM-annotated semantic dependency graph to measure structural responsibility. It combines this with changes in gold-answer log-likelihood to reweight GRPO advantages for individual steps.
hPO7EzwyGt.key_idea: Combine backward-propagated dependency credit with incremental gold-answer likelihood changes to assign step-specific GRPO advantages.
hPO7EzwyGt.evidence: Experiments include Qwen2.5-Math-7B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, with analyses of dead-end reasoning steps, token savings, and annotator choice.
hPO7EzwyGt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers consider dependency-aware step credit a useful approach to distinguishing necessary reasoning from redundancy.
hPO7EzwyGt.main_concern: Dependence on a strong external graph annotator and extra forward computations substantially increases training cost.

GO1rHtz3IX.one_liner: Tangent and normal projections separate activation geometry and expose off-manifold dependence in Jacobian-based interpretability.
GO1rHtz3IX.problem: Jacobian-based explanations can depend on network behavior away from the activation manifold rather than observed model behavior.
GO1rHtz3IX.method: The paper projects activations and J-lens readouts onto tangent and normal spaces, deriving an analytic tangent-native J-lens. It analyzes how off-manifold extensions can alter normal readouts while testing the resulting decomposition empirically.
GO1rHtz3IX.key_idea: Decompose activations and Jacobian readouts into tangent and normal components to identify dependence on off-manifold network extensions.
GO1rHtz3IX.evidence: Analytic results and synthetic lens evaluations across multiple language models examine tangent approximations, on-manifold cancellation, and J-lens reliance on normal components.
GO1rHtz3IX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the tangent-normal decomposition and the warning about J-lens off-manifold dependence informative.
GO1rHtz3IX.main_concern: The relationship between empirical tangent-space approximations and the smooth manifolds assumed by the theory needs stronger validation.

ihu5pgx8hj.one_liner: Deletion-hazard estimates allocate federated training gradients between shared and private adapters under a common utility budget.
ihu5pgx8hj.problem: Uniform unlearning preparation spends limited model utility on clients with very different withdrawal probabilities.
ihu5pgx8hj.method: PREMIUM estimates client deletion hazards with a discrete-time survival model and allocates readiness through water-filling with one dual price. Training splits gradients between shared and private adapters so deletion detaches private contributions and removes shared contributions.
ihu5pgx8hj.key_idea: Allocate preparation by predicted deletion hazard, then route client gradients between shared and private adapters in the assigned proportions.
ihu5pgx8hj.evidence: Experiments compare six published baselines at a common utility budget across three hazard profiles on Reddit, with ablations and scalability studies.
ihu5pgx8hj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value treating client-specific deletion likelihood as a basis for allocating federated-unlearning preparation.
ihu5pgx8hj.main_concern: The framework relies on strong assumptions about predictable deletion hazards and their relationship to unlearning cost.

wpW0S1A50x.one_liner: Staged sketch composition exploits full offline inputs to achieve linear application time with high success probability.
wpW0S1A50x.problem: Simulating streaming updates on a fixed vector or matrix adds update and repetition overhead that offline access may avoid.
wpW0S1A50x.method: The paper composes existing sketching primitives through staged dimensionality reduction and probability amplification. It combines the construction with ExpanderSketch for decoding and extends it to tensor sketches, sampling, and moment estimation.
wpW0S1A50x.key_idea: Use staged dimensionality reduction and probability amplification on fully available inputs instead of simulating streaming coordinate updates.
wpW0S1A50x.evidence: Theoretical guarantees cover norm estimation, heavy hitters, rank-one tensor sketches, and sampling; experiments primarily examine synthetic norm estimation.
wpW0S1A50x.claimed_gains: For ℓ2 estimation and heavy hitters, the paper claims optimal sketching dimension, success probability at least 1-1/d, and truly linear application time.
wpW0S1A50x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize useful theoretical guarantees across several basic sketching problems under the stated offline assumptions.
wpW0S1A50x.main_concern: Limited experiments and narrow baseline coverage leave the practical advantage over other offline approaches insufficiently established.

Iiw1WtkMkZ.one_liner: A shared policy learns across executable harness populations while a proposer revises harness code from execution traces.
Iiw1WtkMkZ.problem: Optimizing a fixed harness or a policy under a fixed interface overlooks their changing interaction during training.
Iiw1WtkMkZ.method: CoHARL co-evolves a shared agent policy and a population of executable harnesses through reinforcement learning. The policy trains on population rollouts while a proposer uses execution traces to revise and validate harness code.
Iiw1WtkMkZ.key_idea: Train one policy across multiple executable harnesses while iteratively proposing harness-code revisions from its execution traces.
Iiw1WtkMkZ.evidence: Evaluations on SWE-rebench, SWE-bench Verified, and Terminal-Bench 2.0 include matched-budget controls for harness-only, fixed-harness, and single-harness adaptation.
Iiw1WtkMkZ.claimed_gains: CoHARL achieves a 27.6% mean resolved rate on SWE-rebench, improving over harness-only search by 6.4 percentage points.
Iiw1WtkMkZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find joint adaptation of policy parameters and executable harnesses useful and the code-revision mechanism sensible.
Iiw1WtkMkZ.main_concern: Limited repeated-run and configuration coverage leaves the benefit of maintaining a harness population insufficiently established.

N46h88pjTd.one_liner: Dual-space audio diffusion synchronization couples reconstructed moving sound sources with explorable 4D visual scenes.
N46h88pjTd.problem: Existing dynamic scene generation largely omits sound and its dependence on moving objects and listener position.
N46h88pjTd.method: SonicVista builds a 360-degree static background, reconstructs dynamic foreground trajectories, and synthesizes a multi-source sound field using dual-space audio diffusion synchronization. The resulting scene supports novel-view visual and spatial-audio rendering.
N46h88pjTd.key_idea: Synchronize audio diffusion across spatial representations using explicit scene geometry and moving sound-source trajectories.
N46h88pjTd.evidence: Real-world dataset evaluations assess spatial audio rendering and geometry-grounded audio-visual consistency, including ground-truth audio at a novel listener pose.
N46h88pjTd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that generating explorable scenes with moving sound sources is a useful task with a coherent geometric formulation.
N46h88pjTd.main_concern: The pipeline needs stronger analysis of how visual reconstruction and alignment errors affect the final audio-visual scene.

Dq9aQxMRaL.one_liner: Streaming fixed-policy gradients overlaps agent rollouts and learning while preserving batch-synchronous GRPO and distillation updates.
Dq9aQxMRaL.problem: Synchronous agent training leaves learners idle during long rollouts, while asynchronous overlap introduces policy staleness.
Dq9aQxMRaL.method: ThunderSyncRL starts trajectory-local GRPO score gradients when rewards arrive and OPD gradients when teacher-scored turns finish. It combines these computations into the same update as batch-synchronous training while keeping policy parameters fixed.
Dq9aQxMRaL.key_idea: Compute trajectory-local or turn-local gradients as their inputs become available, then assemble the unchanged synchronous policy update.
Dq9aQxMRaL.evidence: Update-equivalence proofs and training experiments on SWE-bench Verified and Terminal Bench 4.0 compare synchronous and asynchronous schedules.
Dq9aQxMRaL.claimed_gains: ThunderSyncRL reaches the same performance up to 1.9 × faster than synchronous training and exceeds asynchronous training at fixed budget by up to 2.47 percentage points.
Dq9aQxMRaL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate reducing learner idle time through a simple gradient decomposition that preserves synchronous updates.
Dq9aQxMRaL.main_concern: Comparisons do not establish the advantage over asynchronous methods that explicitly correct for stale-policy trajectories.

urjXCbKVzH.one_liner: Lineage-based data stratification prioritizes informative examples for prompt mutations and candidate comparisons.
urjXCbKVzH.problem: Prompt-search methods waste evaluation budgets by repeatedly treating all development examples as equally informative.
urjXCbKVzH.method: APEX-Data stratifies examples into Easy, Hard, and Mixed tiers using prompt optimization history. It prioritizes Mixed examples through separate frontiers for generating useful mutations and distinguishing candidate quality.
urjXCbKVzH.key_idea: Track pass/fail histories across prompt lineages to select mixed-performance examples for mutation and candidate ranking.
urjXCbKVzH.evidence: Experiments on IFBench, SimpleQA Verified, and FACTS Grounding evaluate Gemini 2.5 Flash and Gemma 3 27B under a fixed evaluation-call budget.
urjXCbKVzH.claimed_gains: Under 5,000 evaluation calls, APEX improves over the initial prompt by an average of 11.2% on Gemini 2.5 Flash and 6.8% on Gemma 3 27B.
urjXCbKVzH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find selecting informative evaluation data a practical and effective direction for automatic prompt optimization.
urjXCbKVzH.main_concern: Budget accounting and unequal caching could obscure total costs and make baseline efficiency comparisons unfair.

Uq5QO6LwrH.one_liner: Auction and matching interface interventions test whether economically simple decision procedures steer LLM agents toward optimal strategies.
Uq5QO6LwrH.problem: Reasoning prompts and verbal explanations may not reliably indicate or improve agents' actual strategic decisions.
Uq5QO6LwrH.method: The study varies action interfaces, payoff descriptions, and reasoning scaffolds in auctions and matching across four model families. It compares departures from theoretically optimal strategies with verbal indicators in agents' stated plans.
Uq5QO6LwrH.key_idea: Vary mechanism interfaces and payoff explanations while scoring realized decisions against known optimal strategies and comparing them with stated plans.
Uq5QO6LwrH.evidence: Auction and matching experiments across four model families compare truthful behavior, bid errors, and measured verbal understanding under interface and prompt interventions.
Uq5QO6LwrH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that economic mechanisms supply clear normative benchmarks for evaluating decisions independently of explanations.
Uq5QO6LwrH.main_concern: The matching-interface comparisons use incompatible error measures that can overstate improvements when rankings contain little information.

S5kRMV7ro6.one_liner: Progressively increasing lookahead and attribute vocabulary trains deeper implicit reasoning within a single forward pass.
S5kRMV7ro6.problem: Direct training struggles to teach models the long lookahead needed to select correct reasoning moves without explicit search.
S5kRMV7ro6.method: The curriculum increases both reasoning lookahead and attribute vocabulary size during fine-tuning. Compute-matched comparisons test depth gains, while saturation fits estimate how achieved lookahead changes with further training.
S5kRMV7ro6.key_idea: Gradually increase task lookahead and attribute vocabulary during fine-tuning to train implicit next-move selection.
S5kRMV7ro6.evidence: Compute-matched curriculum comparisons, curriculum-design ablations, and training-curve fits examine synthetic long-horizon reasoning, including Qwen3-0.6B.
S5kRMV7ro6.claimed_gains: Qwen3-0.6B reaches 98% accuracy on problems with lookahead up to 256 with curriculum, compared to 49% without.
S5kRMV7ro6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that curriculum learning yields substantial gains over compute-matched direct training on the tested reasoning tasks.
S5kRMV7ro6.main_concern: Single-seed training leaves the stability of accuracy gains, convergence times, and fitted saturation curves uncertain.

cn6CNMVBw6.one_liner: Residual-stream edits match counterfactual next-token distributions along fixed responses to localize prompt-intervention effects.
cn6CNMVBw6.problem: Variation across sampled reasoning traces makes prompt-intervention effects difficult to isolate and compare.
cn6CNMVBw6.method: A trained module edits residual activations to minimize KL divergence between source-prompt and counterfactual-target output distributions on a fixed response. Attribution maps suggest important locations and hypotheses for activation-patching tests.
cn6CNMVBw6.key_idea: Hold the response fixed and train residual edits to match counterfactual token distributions, then attribute the edits to candidate causal locations.
cn6CNMVBw6.evidence: Distribution-reconstruction comparisons, attribution analyses, and activation patching include case studies on Gemma-4-E4B-it and DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B using Scruple.
cn6CNMVBw6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find fixed-response behavioral comparisons useful and appreciate distinguishing behavioral recovery from activation reconstruction.
cn6CNMVBw6.main_concern: Missing localization and resampling baselines leave the method's advantage and connection to freely generated behavior unclear.

qmsNFwrvbR.one_liner: Answer confidence and stability across chunks trigger training-free stopping in a frozen long-context reader.
qmsNFwrvbR.problem: Sequential readers waste computation after acquiring sufficient evidence, while existing learned stopping gates require training.
qmsNFwrvbR.method: Answer-Convergence Stopping probes the model's answer state after each chunk using generated outputs and token log probabilities. It stops when answers are confident and stable under one shared configuration.
qmsNFwrvbR.key_idea: Stop chunked reading when the frozen model's answer distribution remains both confident and stable across successive probes.
qmsNFwrvbR.evidence: Evaluations include full LongBench-v2 with two frontier models and evidence-position analysis on 250 S-NIAH questions across five models from two families.
qmsNFwrvbR.claimed_gains: Across 250 S-NIAH questions, ACS premature stopping ranges from 0% to 12%, compared to 8.4% to 45.6% for the verbalized gate.
qmsNFwrvbR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple training-free combination of answer confidence and stability and the explicit premature-stopping evaluation.
qmsNFwrvbR.main_concern: Missing direct comparisons with DCC and GRU-Mem leave the accuracy-efficiency trade-off against established methods unresolved.

WY59SKCODP.one_liner: Discrete Morse critical events weight teacher supervision when distilling a wildfire forecaster into an MLP.
WY59SKCODP.problem: Uniform distillation ignores the differing structural roles of wildfire events while large diffusion forecasters are computationally expensive.
WY59SKCODP.method: MorseDistil builds a graph representation of spatio-temporal events and identifies critical events through discrete Morse functions and gradient pairings. These events weight the distillation loss from a Transformer teacher to an MLP student.
WY59SKCODP.key_idea: Use discrete Morse critical events on a spatio-temporal graph to concentrate distillation supervision on selected event structures.
WY59SKCODP.evidence: Review text describes experiments across ten datasets using sources including FIRMS hotspots and NOAA NCEI records.
WY59SKCODP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the motivation for reducing the computational cost of spatio-temporal wildfire forecasting.
WY59SKCODP.main_concern: Missing data-construction, split, and forecasting-protocol details undermine confidence in the evaluation.

bEYxPWtTNk.one_liner: Base/post-training coverage comparisons diagnose how post-training concentrates success and reduces gains from repeated sampling.
bEYxPWtTNk.problem: Single-shot accuracy can conceal reduced solution coverage and test-time scalability after agent post-training.
bEYxPWtTNk.method: The study compares base and post-trained agents under repeated sampling and introduces Sharpening Tax to quantify lost test-time scalability. It also evaluates posterior-tempered group sampling as a post-training intervention.
bEYxPWtTNk.key_idea: Compare success under repeated sampling before and after post-training to measure concentration toward always-solved and never-solved tasks.
bEYxPWtTNk.evidence: The observational study covers 14 base/post-trained model pairs from four families on three agentic benchmarks, with harness ablations and PTGS experiments.
bEYxPWtTNk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value extending the study of post-training coverage loss to agentic tasks and find PTGS empirically promising.
bEYxPWtTNk.main_concern: A positive Sharpening Tax can reflect improved sampling efficiency rather than lost coverage, limiting its standalone interpretation.

IhkeuN9dEd.one_liner: Local mixing induces residual-stream recency bias that global attention without explicit position encoding can read.
IhkeuN9dEd.problem: Hybrid language models use global attention without explicit position encoding, but the source of their positional information remains unclear.
IhkeuN9dEd.method: The paper analyzes how sliding-window and gated linear attention induce residual-stream recency bias. Theory and experiments examine how this bias propagates into global NoPE attention logits.
IhkeuN9dEd.key_idea: Local mixing creates recency-dependent residual similarities that global NoPE attention selects through its logits.
IhkeuN9dEd.evidence: Theoretical derivations and empirical analyses of hybrid models examine recency bias and its propagation into global attention.
IhkeuN9dEd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the analysis relevant to increasingly used hybrid architectures and appreciate the theoretical and empirical support.
IhkeuN9dEd.main_concern: Showing recency bias does not establish that it supplies sufficient relative-position information or supports length extrapolation.

6iDOH92jna.one_liner: Trains an inertia-scaled RL policy to output time-varying per-joint stiffness, damping, and setpoints for force-accurate motion imitation.
6iDOH92jna.problem: Physics-based motion imitation with fixed-gain proportional-derivative controllers faces conflicting stiffness and damping demands between swing and contact phases, degrading contact-force accuracy.
6iDOH92jna.method: ImpedanceMimic trains a reinforcement-learning policy using motion capture and force-plate ground-reaction-force rewards to output per-joint stiffness, damping, and target position offsets scaled by joint inertia priors, while requiring only motion input at inference time. Scaling gains by inertia enables a single policy to control subject-specific biomechanical models and transfer zero-shot across body morphologies and simulated humanoids.
6iDOH92jna.key_idea: Use inertia-scaled per-joint stiffness, damping, and position setpoints as an RL action space trained with kinematic and contact-force supervision.
6iDOH92jna.evidence: Evaluated across biomechanical models of 129 human participants and six activities with force-plate measurements, plus zero-shot transfer to unseen subjects, held-out activities, and a simulated humanoid against fixed-gain PD, torque, muscle, and regression baselines.
6iDOH92jna.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that scaling physics-based motion imitation to 129 participants with detailed ground-reaction-force evaluation and adaptive impedance control improves tracking on dynamic tasks over fixed-gain explicit PD.
6iDOH92jna.main_concern: Reviewers question physiological interpretations of learned gains (noting position offsets dominate reconstructed push-off torque), point out that standard implicit or stable PD avoids the theoretical explicit-PD bounds, and note reliance on ground-truth subject inertia and mass priors.

QRmvAEdAw4.one_liner: Extends Ho-Kalman realization via Markov-parameter estimation to prove single-trajectory PAC learnability for affine selective state-space models.
QRmvAEdAw4.problem: Finite-sample PAC learnability from a single temporally correlated trajectory remained unestablished for input-dependent selective state-space models such as affine Linear Parameter-Varying systems.
QRmvAEdAw4.method: Focusing on stable selective state-space models whose state-transition, input, and readout matrices are affine functions of input features, the authors estimate generalized Markov parameters from a single stationary trajectory and apply an extended Ho-Kalman realization algorithm. They derive finite-sample high-probability bounds on system parameter recovery and prediction error without requiring i.i.d. inputs or zero initial state.
QRmvAEdAw4.key_idea: Estimate generalized Markov parameters from a single correlated trajectory and apply Ho-Kalman realization to recover affine input-dependent state-space matrices.
QRmvAEdAw4.evidence: Purely theoretical finite-sample probabilistic PAC bounds on parameter estimation and prediction error for quadratically stable, minimal affine selective SSMs under stationary non-i.i.d. inputs, with no numerical experiments.
QRmvAEdAw4.claimed_gains: Establishes a single-trajectory finite-sample probabilistic PAC bound of O-tilde(1/N^zeta) with zeta <= 1/2 on parameter-estimation and prediction error over trajectory length N.
QRmvAEdAw4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending single-trajectory Ho-Kalman system identification to affine input-dependent selective SSMs under correlated inputs and stationary initialization broadens classical realization theory.
QRmvAEdAw4.main_concern: Reviewers emphasize that the algorithm assumes exact knowledge of an unestimated population Gram matrix G_L—undermining purely data-driven single-trajectory identification—alongside heavy notation and the absence of numerical experiments.

9vT48Lms48.one_liner: Diagnoses early irreversible lock-in and vanishing marginal utility signals that prevent task-loss training of hybrid attention routers.
9vT48Lms48.problem: Learned token-level routers that allocate sparse attention budgets in hybrid recurrent-attention models consistently collapse to chance accuracy, even when REINFORCE supplies gradients to unselected tokens.
9vT48Lms48.method: Using controlled routing-schedule interventions on multi-query associative recall—holding total correctly routed steps fixed while shifting when misrouting begins and how long it lasts—the authors isolate an early irreversible lock-in window alongside an analysis of vanishing marginal attention utility under initial misrouting.
9vT48Lms48.key_idea: Shift fixed-duration misrouting windows across training steps in hybrid state-space-attention models to isolate early irreversible parameter lock-in and vanishing router signals.
9vT48Lms48.evidence: Multi-seed timing-onset and deficit-duration sweeps (10 seeds across 9 onsets), learning-rate warmup and multi-block tests on synthetic multi-query associative recall, theoretical gradient analysis, and WikiText-103 language-modeling checks.
9vT48Lms48.claimed_gains: At a 6.25% attention budget on multi-query associative recall, routing the right tokens achieves 0.997 accuracy versus 0.0002 for a tuned static schedule, while early misrouting causes lock-in with a midpoint onset at 23 steps and deficit-length threshold at 48 steps.
9vT48Lms48.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the fixed-budget timing-window experiments are carefully controlled across seeds and clearly demonstrate that early routing history critically affects hybrid model training on associative recall.
9vT48Lms48.main_concern: Reviewers point out that lock-in is demonstrated only in tiny models on one synthetic task (with no attention headroom found on WikiText-103), depends strongly on aggressive learning rates, and contains errors in Proposition 1's gradient derivation.

OQGqBJhAWb.one_liner: Shows lightweight retrieval previews so LLM search agents selectively admit arbitrary subsets of full documents into context.
OQGqBJhAWb.problem: Multi-round LLM search agents admit retrieved documents via fixed or rank-prefix rules, injecting redundant or misleading high-ranked passages while missing relevant lower-ranked ones.
OQGqBJhAWb.method: Selective Evidence Entry During Search (SEEDS) decouples retrieval from context admission by first presenting compact previews of all retrieved candidates to the reasoning agent. Conditioned on its evolving reasoning trace, the agent selects an arbitrary non-prefix subset and number of candidates to expand into full documents, operating either training-free or with further policy learning.
OQGqBJhAWb.key_idea: Insert a preview-inspection step before document expansion so search agents admit arbitrary reasoning-conditioned subsets of retrieved candidates rather than top-k prefixes.
OQGqBJhAWb.evidence: Evaluated across nine knowledge-intensive QA benchmarks in both local-corpus and live-web search settings on ReAct and o1-style reasoning agents against fixed-k and dynamic-prefix baselines.
OQGqBJhAWb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling candidate retrieval from full-document context admission via a plug-and-play preview loop is intuitive and substantially reduces full-document reads while improving QA exact match.
OQGqBJhAWb.main_concern: Reviewers note that efficiency metrics omit preview tokens and extra generation turns (which can exceed baseline token counts), confound wider candidate visibility with reasoning-conditioned selection, and overlook existing search agents that already browse snippets before opening pages.

Ee6uFcDt46.one_liner: Certifies policy sets under dependent data streams using martingale concentration tests on conditionally centered average predictable risk.
Ee6uFcDt46.problem: Standard Learn-then-Test policy certification assumes stationary, independent calibration losses and fails when sequential deployment losses are temporally dependent and history-evolving.
