Ee6uFcDt46.method: StreamLTT replaces fixed population risk with average predictable risk—the mean conditional expected loss given past stream history—so conditionally centered empirical deviations form a martingale difference sequence. Applying finite-sample Hoeffding or predictable-variance-adaptive martingale tests with family-wise error rate control produces a simultaneously certified safe policy set for deployment selection.
Ee6uFcDt46.key_idea: Center sequential losses on their history-conditioned expectations to form martingales and apply multiple-testing FWER control to certify average predictable risk.
Ee6uFcDt46.evidence: Finite-sample and asymptotic martingale risk-control theorems plus experiments across seven forecasting datasets and seven deployment risk metrics against IID, robust-variance, block-bootstrap, and concentration baselines.
Ee6uFcDt46.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that certifying decision policies under nonstationary dependent streams via conditionally centered predictable risk and martingale bounds addresses a practically relevant deployment problem.
Ee6uFcDt46.main_concern: Reviewers question the validity of standard Holm FWER proofs when the set of unsafe null hypotheses is history-dependent and random, note that guarantees cover only the observed past horizon rather than future deployment rounds, and find the presentation dense and narrow in experimental clarity.

Litd4TYnJU.one_liner: Summarizes clustered AI error histories with Hawkes exponential memory filters inside PPO to optimize continuous-time human-AI delegation.
Litd4TYnJU.problem: Static human-AI delegation policies ignore temporal clustering of AI failures, making it unclear when to increase human verification, hand back control, or resume autonomy after recent incidents.
Litd4TYnJU.method: Motivated by Hawkes-process fits showing self-exciting incident clustering on AgentLogs and ODCV-Bench traces, the authors formulate a continuous-time stochastic control problem jointly selecting productive actions, verification effort that dampens error propagation, and regime-switching rates across autonomous, AI-assisted, and human-directed modes. Hawkes-PPO encodes observed incident histories via exponential memory filters and optimizes delegation policies with reinforcement learning.
Litd4TYnJU.key_idea: Feed exponential Hawkes memory filters of past AI incidents into PPO to learn continuous-time verification effort and human-AI regime switching.
Litd4TYnJU.evidence: Held-out log-likelihood fits of Hawkes incident models on AgentLogs coding traces and ODCV-Bench runs, plus synthetic stochastic-control simulations comparing Hawkes-PPO against fixed regimes, history-free PPO, and an approximate full-information benchmark.
Litd4TYnJU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling self-exciting AI error clustering via Hawkes processes to guide dynamic human supervision and regime switching is an interesting formulation of human-AI delegation.
Litd4TYnJU.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the dense, hard-to-follow mathematical writeup and lack of real-system closed-loop validation, noting that Hawkes-PPO is tested only in synthetic simulations with unvalidated modeling assumptions such as zero detection lag.

Lxy0zAb3jK.one_liner: Bidirectional Transformer iteratively unmasks high-confidence missing labels as discrete latent variables for in-context semi-supervised learning
Lxy0zAb3jK.problem: In-context learning typically relies on scarce labeled demonstrations while failing to exploit abundant unlabeled examples within the context.
Lxy0zAb3jK.method: Diffusion In-Context Learner (DICL) treats unknown query labels as discrete latent variables and trains a conditional discrete diffusion process over a bidirectional Transformer. At inference, the frozen model iteratively denoises missing labels while fixing input features and observed labels, progressively committing high-confidence predictions as pseudo-labeled context under a controllable step budget.
Lxy0zAb3jK.key_idea: Treat missing context labels as discrete latent variables and iteratively commit the highest-confidence predictions across bidirectional denoising passes while holding inputs and observed labels fixed.
Lxy0zAb3jK.evidence: Evaluated on controlled synthetic in-context classification of Gaussian mixtures (GMM and SubGMM) and two wireless MIMO symbol detection settings against one-shot and classical statistical baselines.
Lxy0zAb3jK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the iterative unmasking formulation is simple, offers a retraining-free inference compute knob on a frozen model, and lowers error across Gaussian-mixture and MIMO benchmarks.
Lxy0zAb3jK.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate the contribution of discrete diffusion from deterministic confidence-ordered decoding and generic iterative pseudo-labeling at matched compute.

2j8WEYnJOt.one_liner: Jointly optimizes articulated robot morphology distributions and a shared controller using short-horizon gradients through differentiable rigid-body simulation
2j8WEYnJOt.problem: Computing design gradients for articulated rigid-body robots with discrete joints and contacts is difficult, leaving prior differentiable co-design methods restricted mainly to slower soft bodies.
2j8WEYnJOt.method: The method (FORM) continuously relaxes appendage presence within a candidate kinematic supergraph, sampling a population of articulated designs controlled by a shared universal policy. Differentiable rigid-body contact simulation computes fitness gradients averaged over the population and truncated simulation windows to concurrently update the design distribution and controller.
2j8WEYnJOt.key_idea: Continuously relax rigid-body appendage parameters in a candidate supergraph and average short-horizon differentiable physics gradients across a sampled design population sharing one universal policy.
2j8WEYnJOt.evidence: Demonstrated in differentiable rigid-body contact simulation starting from a capsule morphology on flat-ground legged locomotion, with ablations and comparisons against a CMA-ES baseline.
2j8WEYnJOt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value extending end-to-end differentiable morphology-control co-design from soft bodies to articulated rigid-body locomotion via continuous appendage relaxation and differentiable contact physics.
2j8WEYnJOt.main_concern: Topology changes are confined to a single predefined kinematic supergraph, and baseline comparisons do not cleanly isolate first-order morphology gradients due to confounded schedules and missing RL co-design baselines.

itJU9MsEBW.one_liner: CompleteP scaling transfers GRPO learning rates from small language models to wider and deeper models.
itJU9MsEBW.problem: RL post-training requires costly learning-rate tuning that becomes especially burdensome for larger language models.
itJU9MsEBW.method: The authors show GRPO is compatible with CompleteP feature-learning scaling and compare scaled and standard parameterizations during learning-rate sweeps across model sizes.
itJU9MsEBW.key_idea: CompleteP parameter scaling widens the shared high-performing GRPO learning-rate range across widths and depths.
itJU9MsEBW.evidence: Experiments cover five verifiable-reward tasks and models up to approximately one billion parameters after pretraining and task-specific SFT.
itJU9MsEBW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that small-model tuning for RL post-training is practically useful and that the multistage, five-task evaluation is informative.
itJU9MsEBW.main_concern: Reviewers most often question support for larger models because experiments stop near one billion parameters and the analyzed and implemented model families differ.

F3XzeZEOFM.one_liner: Finite-time bounds separate Adam's momentum tracking and preconditioner errors under nonstationary objectives.
F3XzeZEOFM.problem: Adam's noise reduction and responsiveness to objective drift can favor either Adam or SGD, but existing theory does not explain the tradeoff.
F3XzeZEOFM.method: The analysis derives expected and high-probability tracking bounds under adaptive strong monotonicity and projected stationarity bounds under smooth objectives with distribution shift.
F3XzeZEOFM.key_idea: Explicit β1, β2, and ε-dependent terms separate first-moment lag from preconditioner perturbation in Adam's tracking error.
F3XzeZEOFM.evidence: The paper provides finite-time and high-probability theory, burn-in analyses, and experiments on convex and nonconvex problems consistent with the predicted noise–drift tradeoff.
F3XzeZEOFM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating momentum and preconditioner effects clarifies Adam's noise–drift tradeoff and matches the experiments.
F3XzeZEOFM.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the tracking bound insufficiently informative because domain-diameter terms can exceed trivial feasible-set guarantees and drift enters indirectly.

jk5GLnlVRg.one_liner: ActiveLang adapts dual-Gaussian language features online and explores viewpoints using semantic uncertainty.
jk5GLnlVRg.problem: Robots need efficient open-vocabulary 3D maps in unfamiliar environments rather than passive reconstruction along prerecorded trajectories.
jk5GLnlVRg.method: ActiveLang jointly reconstructs geometry, appearance, and language features on a compact dual-Gaussian representation while a semantic-uncertainty planner selects informative viewpoints.
jk5GLnlVRg.key_idea: Semantic uncertainty guides active observations for online adaptation of compact open-vocabulary Gaussian maps.
jk5GLnlVRg.evidence: Replica and ScanNet++ experiments evaluate 2D and 3D open-vocabulary segmentation and 3D reconstruction against online and offline baselines.
jk5GLnlVRg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that joining active exploration with open-vocabulary mapping addresses a useful embodied-AI setting and improves several metrics.
jk5GLnlVRg.main_concern: Reviewers most often describe the system as an integration of existing mapping and compression techniques with limited methodological novelty.

kzrqRwW8QW.one_liner: Exponential likelihood tilting rescales pretrained diffusion scores to sample controllable outliers without retraining.
kzrqRwW8QW.problem: Outlier generation usually requires specialized architectures or training objectives rather than reusing models trained on regular data.
kzrqRwW8QW.method: The method exponentially tilts the pretrained model's induced log-likelihood distribution, producing an explicit scalar score modification that steers sampling toward lower-likelihood regions.
kzrqRwW8QW.key_idea: A time-dependent scalar score rescaling approximates exponential tilting of the log-likelihood distribution for controlled outlier strength.
kzrqRwW8QW.evidence: The paper derives stochastic-ordering and convergence results and evaluates nine real-world multivariate time-series datasets against specialized outlier generators.
kzrqRwW8QW.claimed_gains: Across nine real-world multivariate time-series datasets, the method ranks first or second in all main benchmark comparisons against specialized outlier-generation methods.
kzrqRwW8QW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that scalar score control is simple and inexpensive, with interpretable theory and broad time-series evaluation.
kzrqRwW8QW.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite missing comparisons with score-rescaling controls and same-data evaluation that measures fitting rather than generalization.

Pz7PpCK6Py.one_liner: Low-dimensional curvature explains small-population ES scaling and non-monotonic fine-tuning reward dynamics.
Pz7PpCK6Py.problem: Classical zeroth-order intuition cannot explain why tiny ES populations fine-tune billion-parameter models or why rewards later decline.
Pz7PpCK6Py.method: A quadratic stochastic-ascent model and curvature measurements connect stiff directions with heterogeneous timescales and dimension-independent access to improving isotropic perturbations.
Pz7PpCK6Py.key_idea: Curvature concentrates in a few stiff directions, leaving flat ambient dimensions irrelevant to perturbation improvement probability.
Pz7PpCK6Py.evidence: GSM8K, ARC-C, and WinoGrande reward surfaces are probed with ES on Qwen2.5-Instruct models from 0.5B to 7B, alongside analytical and perturbation studies.
Pz7PpCK6Py.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that a shared geometric account of scalability and non-monotonic rewards is testable and supported by analysis and measurements.
Pz7PpCK6Py.main_concern: Reviewers most often argue that matching quadratic-model curve shapes does not establish curvature and noise as the causes of actual ES or GRPO declines.

nfOKEHU9sm.one_liner: InterEvolve edits staged reward programs from execution feedback to reuse frozen humanoid controller skills.
nfOKEHU9sm.problem: Humanoids need to solve unseen loco-manipulation tasks by repurposing existing skills without controller retraining.
nfOKEHU9sm.method: An object-aware forward-backward model adds object residuals to a frozen body prior, while an LLM edits staged reward programs and a numerical optimizer tunes constants using verified simulation rollouts.
nfOKEHU9sm.key_idea: Execution-verified reward programs provide an editable interface that induces and composes latent skills in a frozen controller.
nfOKEHU9sm.evidence: Parallel simulation scenarios verify candidate programs across contact-rich, multi-stage tasks, with component ablations, a verified skill library, and hardware replay demonstrations.
nfOKEHU9sm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that object-aware residual control and execution-guided reward editing enable useful test-time adaptation without retraining.
nfOKEHU9sm.main_concern: Reviewers most often note that hardware tests replay simulation-generated latent prompts rather than executing the full reward mechanism live.

giQvIQ6jss.one_liner: Linearized deep cross-attention provably recovers Bayes-optimal multimodal in-context prediction under latent factors.
giQvIQ6jss.problem: In-context-learning theory addresses unimodal data, leaving multimodal prediction and the role of cross-attention poorly understood.
giQvIQ6jss.method: A latent-factor framework proves single-layer self-attention cannot uniformly recover the Bayes predictor, then analyzes multi-layer linearized cross-attention trained by gradient flow at large depth and context length.
giQvIQ6jss.key_idea: Deep cross-attention implements iterative covariance correction needed for Bayes-optimal prediction in the multimodal latent-factor model.
giQvIQ6jss.evidence: The paper provides negative and positive training theorems, synthetic experiments, and corrupted avMNIST results.
giQvIQ6jss.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the separation between single-layer attention and deep cross-attention is clear and supported by synthetic experiments.
giQvIQ6jss.main_concern: Reviewers most often argue that fixed matrices and one or two trained scalars limit implications for standard Transformers beyond the constrained regression setting.

NH8Eqmd9je.one_liner: Jointly learns disease subtypes, continuous stages, and monotonic biomarker trajectories from sparse cross-sectional and longitudinal data.
NH8Eqmd9je.problem: Existing disease-progression models confound stage with subtype, scale poorly with biomarker count, or struggle to combine cross-sectional and sparse longitudinal data.
NH8Eqmd9je.method: TRACE models subtype-specific biomarker trajectories using monotonic neural networks, jointly optimizing continuous individual stages, subtype mixture assignments, and a longitudinal temporal-change loss end-to-end with SGD.
NH8Eqmd9je.key_idea: Jointly optimizes monotonic neural biomarker trajectories, continuous disease stages, and subtype mixtures with longitudinal change regularization via SGD.
NH8Eqmd9je.evidence: Evaluates on semi-simulated MRI biomarker data with known subtypes and stages using five-fold validation and trajectory-family ablations.
NH8Eqmd9je.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the joint continuous-stage and subtype formulation well suited to sparse mixed longitudinal-cross-sectional medical data.
NH8Eqmd9je.main_concern: Validation relies on a single semi-simulated MRI dataset, omits recent Bayesian EBM baselines, and does not analyze assignment uncertainty or elapsed visit times.

xAc3nvRPtM.one_liner: Trains a shared-Transformer sequential multi-step retriever using same-context hard negatives, gold-prefix teacher forcing, and position-aware scoring.
xAc3nvRPtM.problem: Supervised multi-step retrievers lag behind RL-based retrievers due to easy in-batch negatives, noisy retrieval prefixes, and position-agnostic scoring.
xAc3nvRPtM.method: S^2LMR models multi-step retrieval as evolving an explicit textual state in a single shared Transformer, trained via teacher-forced InfoNCE with same-context negatives and updated positional encodings after each hop.
xAc3nvRPtM.key_idea: Fixes supervised multi-step retrieval via teacher-forced gold prefixes, same-context negatives, and hop-updated positional encodings in one Transformer.
xAc3nvRPtM.evidence: Evaluates on long-context reasoning, multi-hop QA, and needle-in-a-haystack benchmarks from 4K to 10M tokens.
xAc3nvRPtM.claimed_gains: Trains over 20x faster than Q-RAG while matching or outperforming compared multi-step retrieval methods.
xAc3nvRPtM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simplicity of replacing RL value/target networks with teacher-forced InfoNCE and the analysis of same-context negatives.
xAc3nvRPtM.main_concern: The 20x-24x speedup claim relies on a slow, underperforming Q-RAG reproduction, and gains on natural-language QA are mixed.

dyXYSlruJA.one_liner: Trains a discrete visual tokenizer and length predictor via local rate-distortion probes against frozen DINOv3 features.
dyXYSlruJA.problem: Adaptive-length discrete visual tokenizers typically require post-hoc search or a fixed set of rate modes rather than predicting per-image length directly.
dyXYSlruJA.method: STROP uses a four-phase curriculum with local rate-distortion probes against frozen DINOv3 features to train an ordered discrete visual program and a length head that predicts the active token prefix in a single forward pass.
dyXYSlruJA.key_idea: Supervises an image-dependent token-length predictor in a single forward pass using local rate-distortion probes over frozen DINOv3 features.
dyXYSlruJA.evidence: Evaluates semantic segmentation on four benchmarks against fixed-length baselines and FlexTok, One-D-Piece, and ALIT under a shared readout.
dyXYSlruJA.claimed_gains: At ~250 nominal bits per crop, improves segmentation by 1.6-3.1 mIoU over a fixed-length baseline across four benchmarks and beats a fixed K=32 baseline.
dyXYSlruJA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the semantic focus over pixel reconstruction and the rate-matched comparisons across four segmentation benchmarks.
dyXYSlruJA.main_concern: Variable-length prefix training itself may explain gains over fixed-length models without isolating per-image length adaptation, and comparisons omit KARL.

wD2AKOEkZo.one_liner: Accelerates SO(2)-equivariant materials GNNs by executing layers on INT8 matrix units via fused Ozaki-scheme precision emulation.
wD2AKOEkZo.problem: SO(2)-equivariant layers dominate runtime in materials GNNs because native low-precision formats like FP8 degrade accuracy while FP32 limits throughput.
wD2AKOEkZo.method: FlashSO(2) fuses operations and emulates high-precision matrix multiplication on INT8 tensor cores using the integer Ozaki scheme for SO(2)-equivariant layers in ML interatomic potentials and Hamiltonian models.
wD2AKOEkZo.key_idea: Fuses SO(2)-equivariant GNN layers onto INT8 matrix multiplication units using integer Ozaki-scheme precision emulation.
wD2AKOEkZo.evidence: Benchmarks layer and model throughput, memory, and accuracy on MALOQ and UMA on NVIDIA GH200 GPUs.
wD2AKOEkZo.claimed_gains: Reaches 40x (MALOQ) and 7x (UMA) layer throughput (236 and 232 effective Tflop/s, 3.5x FP32 peak), training MALOQ 3.9x faster with 58% less peak memory at no accuracy loss.
wD2AKOEkZo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate targeting the dominant SO(2) bottleneck and achieving large memory and throughput gains with integer emulation.
wD2AKOEkZo.main_concern: Most of the 40x/3.9x speedup comes from kernel fusion rather than emulation against fused FP32/TF32 baselines, and UMA MD accuracy metrics are incomplete.

EnBpzU8b3z.one_liner: Executes zeroth-order LLM perturbations as low-rank adapters through inference-serving engines to eliminate dense weight writes.
EnBpzU8b3z.problem: Standard zeroth-order LLM training wastes compute and memory bandwidth on repeated dense weight perturbations and unoptimized padding.
EnBpzU8b3z.method: Infer-ZO represents ZO perturbations and updates as low-rank adapters on frozen base weights, decoupling algorithmic evaluation from execution so candidate forward passes run on optimized inference engines and co-serve with live inference batches.
EnBpzU8b3z.key_idea: Expresses zeroth-order perturbations as low-rank adapters over frozen weights to execute ZO steps as co-servable inference workloads.
EnBpzU8b3z.evidence: Evaluates step latency, co-serving throughput, and fine-tuning across 15 Qwen3, Llama, and OPT models against released LoZO.
EnBpzU8b3z.claimed_gains: Adds 1.16% wall-clock time over matched inference on Qwen3-14B, keeps co-serving throughput within 0.5%, and achieves 2.10x-9.94x step speedups over released LoZO.
EnBpzU8b3z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clear memory-traffic breakdown showing why dense weight writes and padding slow down existing ZO implementations.
EnBpzU8b3z.main_concern: Speedups stem largely from avoiding dense writes and sequence packing rather than inference-engine serving, and accuracy is only shown on small legacy datasets.

z6nF0HuRlb.one_liner: Proves that training on compositional conjunctive tasks induces abstract disentangled representations when factors rebind across different partners.
z6nF0HuRlb.problem: How neural networks extract abstract, disentangled latent factors when observations only ever present entangled one-hot conjunctions remains unclear.
z6nF0HuRlb.method: The paper formalizes task-driven compositional rebinding—where a latent factor binds to different partner factors in inputs versus outputs—and derives exact optimal representations for single-hidden-layer ReLU networks on a Raven-style rule task and linear networks generally.
z6nF0HuRlb.key_idea: Shows that binding a latent factor to different partners in input versus output conjunctions forces task-trained networks to form abstract factor subspaces.
z6nF0HuRlb.evidence: Combines exact analytical derivations for ReLU and linear networks with representation-probing experiments across compositional tasks.
z6nF0HuRlb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the rebinding perspective on how task structure induces factor abstraction from conjunctive codes interesting.
z6nF0HuRlb.main_concern: Training includes all factor combinations without testing true unseen-combination generalization, and linear theory cannot capture nonlinear output-conjunction construction.

BfRhheMOI7.one_liner: Introduces a 42-problem benchmark pairing black-box optimization tasks with controlled natural-language context levels for LLM optimizers.
BfRhheMOI7.problem: Numerical black-box optimization methods such as Bayesian optimization struggle to incorporate real-world semantic context like domain knowledge and prior experiments.
BfRhheMOI7.method: SemanticBBOBench provides a uniform interface spanning 42 scientific and engineering optimization problems, each paired with curated context at multiple controlled detail levels, including rewritten, misleading, and unrelated conditions.
BfRhheMOI7.key_idea: Evaluates LLM-based and hybrid optimizers across nested natural-language context levels and misleading priors on a unified mixed-variable black-box optimization suite.
BfRhheMOI7.evidence: Experiments test LLM optimizers (GPT-5.6 Luna and Gemma 4 31B) and a hybrid switching to HEBO after ten evaluations across the 42-problem benchmark and surrogate ranking checks on 21 tasks.
BfRhheMOI7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that SemanticBBOBench addresses a real gap by isolating semantic context's contribution across multiple domains and controlled context conditions.
BfRhheMOI7.main_concern: Reviewers note insufficient baseline coverage, specifically testing only two LLMs with one prompting strategy and omitting dedicated semantic optimization methods like LLAMBO, LLINBO, LGBO, and GOLLuM as well as knowledge-informed BO baselines.

WGMT6igVde.one_liner: Fuses fresh wrist sEMG with delayed visual hand poses in a latency-conditioned two-stream forecaster for robot teleoperation.
WGMT6igVde.problem: Vision-based dexterous teleoperation suffers 150–400 ms pipeline latency that forces operators to slow down and wait for the robot hand.
WGMT6igVde.method: Muscles Know First (MKF) is a latency-conditioned two-stream forecaster that fuses live wrist surface electromyography (sEMG) with delayed visual hand poses to predict the current hand pose to execute.
WGMT6igVde.key_idea: Conditions a two-stream forecaster on the vision delay to combine live wrist sEMG signals with stale visual pose estimates.
WGMT6igVde.evidence: Evaluated offline on paired sEMG and motion-capture recordings from emg2pose across 20 unseen users (2,172 recordings), under calibrated egocentric vision degradations, and in a fixed-wrist MuJoCo Shadow Hand simulation.
WGMT6igVde.claimed_gains: At 300 ms vision latency and 100 ms horizon, MKF reduces tracking error from 9.26 degrees (uncompensated) and 6.86 degrees (Kin-only) to 5.73 degrees, an additional 16.4% ± 0.3% reduction and 38% total reduction below stale pose (recovering 61% of vision-latency tracking error per TL;DR).
WGMT6igVde.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using sEMG to compensate for vision latency is well-motivated, with convincing causal controls and strong cross-user generalization on emg2pose.
WGMT6igVde.main_concern: All three reviewers emphasize that the method is only tested offline and in simulation with a fixed wrist, lacking live closed-loop human-in-the-loop teleoperation experiments on a real robot.

6xLzoJMm9Z.one_liner: Defines adjudicative legibility to measure how accurately external forecasters can predict an LLM judge's future rulings.
6xLzoJMm9Z.problem: Reference agreement shows how often an LLM adjudicator matches human verdicts, not whether contracting parties can anticipate its future rulings.
6xLzoJMm9Z.method: The authors formalize adjudicative legibility via forecast error (decomposed into observer-eliminable error and judge randomness) and prove safety-margin bounds, evaluating eight LLM adjudicators and two LLM observers on contested disputes.
6xLzoJMm9Z.key_idea: Evaluate LLM adjudicators by an external forecaster's predictability of unseen rulings rather than reference accuracy alone, linking illegibility to contracting safety margins.
6xLzoJMm9Z.evidence: Empirical study of eight LLM adjudicators and two history-based LLM observers on 100 contested e-commerce disputes and 100 article-deletion debates supports the framework.
6xLzoJMm9Z.claimed_gains: On more than a third of tested disputes the outcome depends on adjudicator choice, and adjudicators of similar accuracy differ by up to 2.35x in illegibility.
6xLzoJMm9Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formalizing predictability of LLM adjudicators via legibility and safety margins addresses a timely, practical legal-AI problem.
6xLzoJMm9Z.main_concern: All reviewers warn that legibility rankings depend heavily on the observer (Spearman correlation 0.00-0.05 between F1 and F2 in dispute-only mode) and note small 100-case datasets.

YvQtWNELvO.one_liner: Replaces generic query-key attention in neural operators with a learned interaction kernel conditioned on physical coordinates and geometry.
YvQtWNELvO.problem: Standard attention in neural operators routes information via generic query-key dot products rather than physical-space geometry, hurting irregular-domain PDE learning.
YvQtWNELvO.method: LINK (Learned Interaction Kernels) scores point pairs using a network conditioned on endpoint states, absolute coordinates, and relative geometry, integrating into normalized attention with scalable realizations.
YvQtWNELvO.key_idea: Compute attention routing weights in neural operators through a pair network conditioned on physical coordinates, relative geometry, and endpoint states.
YvQtWNELvO.evidence: PDE benchmarks (including Poisson, Darcy, and nonlinear hyperelasticity), discretization-transfer tests, and Green's function correlation studies support the operator.
YvQtWNELvO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find conditioning attention routing on physical geometry well motivated and appreciate the Green's function correlation and discretization-transfer studies.
YvQtWNELvO.main_concern: Reviewers question fairness against Transformer baselines (different depths, parameter counts, and an extra MoE block), unclear gains from geometry versus pair scoring, and scope on nonlinear PDEs.

i47qii8cIZ.one_liner: Casts neuron concept identification as Empirical Risk Minimization to derive PAC fidelity bounds and bootstrap uncertainty sets.
i47qii8cIZ.problem: Neuron identification methods like Network Dissection and CLIP-Dissect rely on empirical heuristics without formal reliability or uncertainty guarantees.
i47qii8cIZ.method: The authors formulate concept selection as ERM over a concept hypothesis class, derive PAC-style fidelity bounds showing AUROC/recall instability on rare concepts, and propose Bootstrap Explanation (BE) sets.
i47qii8cIZ.key_idea: Frame probing-based neuron labeling as ERM over concept hypotheses to obtain PAC fidelity bounds and bootstrap plausible-concept sets.
i47qii8cIZ.evidence: Theoretical bounds (Table 1) and experiments on synthetic data and ResNet-50 layer-4 with Broden using CLIP-Dissect and Network Dissection support the framework.
i47qii8cIZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing neuron identification as ERM to derive PAC bounds and uncertainty-aware explanation sets is clean and principled.
i47qii8cIZ.main_concern: Reviewers note a mismatch between theoretical sample-size claims (~2,100) and large Broden disagreement (~31,652 images), narrow ResNet-50/Broden validation, and unmodeled CLIP label noise.

OvZLQDadmo.one_liner: Identifies learned inverse-problem regularizers from frequency-band response fingerprints under small random measurement perturbations.
OvZLQDadmo.problem: Different learned priors for inverse problems can yield indistinguishable reconstructions, making output-only model attribution ineffective.
OvZLQDadmo.method: The authors prove that the covariance of random re-solves under measurement perturbations recovers the solver Jacobian and identifies regularizer curvature on the reachable subspace. They introduce a response fingerprint from centered perturbation energies across spatial frequency bands, plus a label-free reliability indicator.
OvZLQDadmo.key_idea: Centered perturbation-response energies across spatial frequency bands fingerprint the reachable curvature of a learned regularizer without examining training data.
OvZLQDadmo.evidence: Evaluates denoising, deblurring, inpainting, super-resolution, MRI, and CT, including zero-shot transfer to external priors.
OvZLQDadmo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that identifying learned priors via perturbation response rather than static outputs is a well-motivated perspective backed by broad inverse-problem experiments.
OvZLQDadmo.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty over normalized radial noise power spectra (NPS) and ProbeSpec, and note restrictive assumptions requiring repeated black-box access and a closed candidate set.

0eKTCXX9Yl.one_liner: Generates a synthetic benchmark of causally linked fictional future events via CASCADE to evaluate knowledge acquisition and multi-event reasoning.
0eKTCXX9Yl.problem: Existing LLM knowledge-update benchmarks suffer from pretraining contamination or rely on counterfactual edits that conflict with parametric knowledge.
0eKTCXX9Yl.method: The authors present CASCADE, a generation pipeline that builds causally interconnected fictional future events with local and global consistency over an event graph, and use it to benchmark retrieval, continued pretraining (CPT), and reasoning-focused RL across proprietary and open-weight models.
0eKTCXX9Yl.key_idea: Constructing a causally consistent event DAG of fictional future events prevents pretraining contamination while testing multi-hop knowledge acquisition and reasoning.
0eKTCXX9Yl.evidence: Benchmarking retrieval and CPT on proprietary and open-weight LLMs across single-event and multi-event reasoning tasks with human-validated LLM judges.
0eKTCXX9Yl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that generating interconnected fictional future events is a useful, contamination-resistant approach to benchmarking knowledge updating and multi-event reasoning.
0eKTCXX9Yl.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about potential selection bias from filtering questions by model errors, insufficient isolation of what causal graph structure adds, and un-tuned CPT hyperparameters.

nK78TQuGnG.one_liner: Decomposes transductive CLIP accuracy gains into within-support discrimination and reduced absent-class obstruction via context interventions.
nK78TQuGnG.problem: Aggregate accuracy obscures whether transductive CLIP methods improve class discrimination or merely suppress classes absent from the test batch.
nK78TQuGnG.method: The authors introduce an exact decomposition separating within-support discrimination from absent-class obstruction, paired with support-only frozen-CLIP controls and interventions varying unlabeled batch composition.
nK78TQuGnG.key_idea: Applies true-support evaluation masking and frozen-CLIP support-only controls to separate within-batch class discrimination from absent-class suppression.
nK78TQuGnG.evidence: Experiments across fine-grained recognition datasets and CLIP variants evaluating methods such as MOON, StatA, and ADAPT.
nK78TQuGnG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the decomposition and support-only control are simple, exact, and reveal meaningful differences hidden by aggregate accuracy.
nK78TQuGnG.main_concern: Reviewers note limited mechanistic explanation of why methods differ, narrower support for some context-confusion findings, and missing related citations.

mPzKbJ5emp.one_liner: Combines one-step and two-step Bellman residuals with a future-feature adaptive critic for offline policy evaluation.
mPzKbJ5emp.problem: Standard minimax offline policy evaluation relies on one-step Bellman residuals with a fixed critic class that ignores transition dynamics.
mPzKbJ5emp.method: Mixed-AC optimizes a convex combination of one-step and two-step Bellman residuals using a minimax formulation whose data-dependent critic is constructed from predicted future feature directions with sample splitting.
mPzKbJ5emp.key_idea: Use predicted future feature directions to form a dynamics-adapted critic in a minimax objective mixing one-step and two-step Bellman residuals.
mPzKbJ5emp.evidence: Evaluations on simulation studies and MetaWorld tasks illustrate the effect of the mixing parameter and critic representation.
mPzKbJ5emp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge that predicting future features for an adaptive critic is a useful construction and that the empirical reporting is careful.
mPzKbJ5emp.main_concern: Reviewers find that residual mixing adds little over zero mixing in several tasks and that hyperparameter selection relies on ground-truth target values unavailable offline.

r3d1359mgO.one_liner: Constructs image-adaptive nested conformal prediction sets for medical segmentation via confidence-guided boundary exploitation and spatial exploration.
r3d1359mgO.problem: Conformal segmentation via pixel-wise thresholding yields fragmented masks, while uniform morphological dilation produces overly large prediction sets.
r3d1359mgO.method: CPAS builds a nested expansion path starting from the predicted mask by iteratively adding boundary pixels via confidence-guided exploitation and spatial exploration, then calibrates a path threshold for finite-sample object coverage.
r3d1359mgO.key_idea: Calibrates conformal thresholds along an image-adaptive nested boundary-expansion path combining confidence exploitation and spatial exploration.
r3d1359mgO.evidence: Theoretical coverage theorem and experiments across multiple medical image segmentation benchmarks.
r3d1359mgO.claimed_gains: On average, CPAS reduces stretch by approximately 20% compared to previous conformal segmentation methods.
r3d1359mgO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that replacing uniform dilation or independent pixel thresholding with an adaptive nested path is well-motivated and cleanly formulated.
r3d1359mgO.main_concern: Novelty over nested conformal prediction and seeded region growing is limited, and evaluation relies heavily on the stretch metric without Dice, IoU, or newer baselines.

ZO6Ny4Kbvk.one_liner: Augments off-policy actor-critic critics with event-forecasting general value functions to provide intermediate credit during sparse-reward VLA RL.
ZO6Ny4Kbvk.problem: Online RL fine-tuning of VLA models suffers from sparse terminal rewards where failed episodes provide no credit for intermediate progress.
ZO6Ny4Kbvk.method: Layered Value Forecasts (LVF) trains event-based general value functions from binary event labels to predict discounted event probabilities and adds their forecasts as cumulants in the critic's TD target.
ZO6Ny4Kbvk.key_idea: Adds learned event-forecasting general value function predictions into the critic's TD target to assign intermediate credit from failed episodes.
ZO6Ny4Kbvk.evidence: Simulation experiments on seven LIBERO tasks and real-robot online RL experiments across four tasks.
ZO6Ny4Kbvk.claimed_gains: On seven LIBERO tasks with low initial success, LVF reaches 65.1% success versus 48.7% for the same actor-critic without forecasts.
ZO6Ny4Kbvk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the well-controlled comparisons with RLT and the convincing real-robot and simulation gains under sparse rewards.
ZO6Ny4Kbvk.main_concern: Modifying the TD target changes the optimization objective, shaping baselines omit learned-forecast variants and equal tuning, and several recent VLA-RL baselines are missing.

apoYn2sWLy.one_liner: Adds lightweight per-KV-group gating heads that dynamically threshold and skip KV-cache chunks during autoregressive LLM decoding.
apoYn2sWLy.problem: Prior sparse attention methods enforce rigid fixed sparsity budgets across heads or context lengths, limiting decode efficiency.
apoYn2sWLy.method: Token-Gated Sparse Attention (TGSA) introduces small gating heads computed before regular attention to decide per-token, per-head which KV-cache chunks to load, enabling non-uniform dynamic sparsity trained from scratch.
apoYn2sWLy.key_idea: Computes small per-KV-group gating heads ahead of regular attention to dynamically threshold and skip loading unneeded KV-cache chunks.
apoYn2sWLy.evidence: Pretrained 600M, 1.7B, and 4B models from scratch and benchmarked vLLM decode throughput at 16K and 64K context lengths.
apoYn2sWLy.claimed_gains: Achieves up to 3.5x faster decoding than regular attention at 64K context length while matching dense and post-trained sparse baselines.
apoYn2sWLy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate pretraining TGSA from scratch up to 4B parameters and delivering real vLLM kernel speedups (up to 3.5x at 64K context).
apoYn2sWLy.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the lack of from-scratch pretrained sparse baselines (NSA, MoBA, DSA at 1.7B/4B) and matched-budget post-hoc baselines, leaving variable-budget gating's advantage unisolated.

3MLBvjCN21.one_liner: Freezes a privileged-RL-distilled flow-matching action decoder and learns a visual-to-latent interface from few image demonstrations.
3MLBvjCN21.problem: Learning dexterous visual manipulation from scarce demonstrations is hard because policies must learn both perception and precise control simultaneously.
3MLBvjCN21.method: Latent RL Prior distills privileged simulation RL rollouts into a flow-matching action decoder conditioned on proprioception and latent task context, then freezes the decoder and trains a visual interface using action supervision alone (extending to bimanual coordination).
3MLBvjCN21.key_idea: Freezes a privileged-RL-distilled flow-matching action decoder and trains a visual encoder to predict its latent task context using action supervision alone.
3MLBvjCN21.evidence: Evaluated on three simulated dexterous manipulation tasks (including door lifting and bimanual assembly) against pi_0.5 and GR00T N1.7.
3MLBvjCN21.claimed_gains: Surpasses full-data baselines on door lifting and bimanual assembly using 10x and 5x fewer demonstrations, respectively.
3MLBvjCN21.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the two-stage latent transfer is clean, avoids paired privileged labels during visual adaptation, and achieves strong simulated low-data results.
3MLBvjCN21.main_concern: Reviewers note all experiments are in simulation with no real-robot validation, and compare 100k updates against 30k-update VLA baselines while ignoring RL pretraining cost.

SEyjhWfMoX.one_liner: Mines procedural hints from strong-vs-weak trajectory pairs and re-scores student rollouts to shape token-level GRPO advantages.
SEyjhWfMoX.problem: Outcome-based RL for tool use gives sparse credit assignment when models know individual actions but fail to sequence them into procedures.
SEyjhWfMoX.method: PHS extracts reusable procedural hints by comparing successful strong-model attempts with failed learner attempts, then uses hinted-vs-unhinted log-probability differences during training to shape token-level GRPO advantages (PHS-Multiplicative and PHS-Additive) without test-time hints.
SEyjhWfMoX.key_idea: Shapes token-level GRPO advantages using log-probability differences between hinted and unhinted teacher-forced passes over mined procedural hints.
SEyjhWfMoX.evidence: Evaluated on AppWorld and EnterpriseOps (held-out and cross-environment transfer) plus external benchmarks across three runs.
SEyjhWfMoX.claimed_gains: Averaged over three runs, pass@4 gains over GRPO reach 19.5 percentage points on AppWorld test, 15.5 on Challenge, and 5.5 on EnterpriseOps.
SEyjhWfMoX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the mined procedure re-scoring practical (requiring no hints at test time) and acknowledge large pass@4 gains on AppWorld.
SEyjhWfMoX.main_concern: Reviewers note missing baselines that directly distill the same expert trajectories (SFT+GRPO), small gains outside AppWorld, and a potentially degenerate Eq. (3) multiplicative formulation.

jzNkappRpa.one_liner: Recovers missing variable names by solving for semantic embeddings constrained by discovered causal structure and expressing them via an LLM.
jzNkappRpa.problem: System measurements often lack labels for observed or latent variables, and assigning meanings solely from human priors introduces bias.
jzNkappRpa.method: CausalBridge discovers a causal graph (including latent variables) from numerical measurements, optimizes unknown variable embeddings to satisfy graph-implied dependence relations relative to named anchor variables, and decodes those embeddings into variable names using a language model.
jzNkappRpa.key_idea: Uses discovered causal structure to constrain unknown variable embeddings relative to named anchors, then decodes the resulting embeddings into names through an LLM.
jzNkappRpa.evidence: Evaluated on five questionnaires, three robotics scenarios (plus simulated arms and vehicle drives) with 20%–90% variable-name masking, and component ablations.
jzNkappRpa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem of naming undocumented or latent variables interesting and appreciate the multi-domain evaluation across masking levels.
jzNkappRpa.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments do not isolate causal structure from non-causal correlation or random graphs, and question whether statistical dependence justifies semantic similarity.

TUETW1Yi2w.one_liner: Constructs explicit QK and VO matrices on spherical embeddings to prove quadratic-in-head-dimension associative memory capacity for one attention head.
TUETW1Yi2w.problem: How and how many position-specific associations a single softmax attention head can memorize remains theoretically under-characterized compared to linear-capacity bounds.
TUETW1Yi2w.method: Using random spherical representations for each sequence-position pair, the authors explicitly construct query-key and value-output matrices and bound QK retrieval interference, decoder interference, and VO operator-norm normalization via concentration inequalities and matrix Bernstein bounds.
TUETW1Yi2w.key_idea: Assigns random spherical embeddings per sequence-position pair and controls three interference terms to prove a single attention head stores quadratically-over-logarithmic many associations in head dimension.
TUETW1Yi2w.evidence: Supported by non-asymptotic concentration proofs and empirical validation against attention-based model weights.
TUETW1Yi2w.claimed_gains: Proves simultaneous storage of associations whenever sequence length and vocabulary size are polynomial in head dimension, achieving a quadratic-over-logarithmic capacity bound.
TUETW1Yi2w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clearly written and appreciate integrating both QK retrieval and OV decoding stages in a single-head capacity construction.
TUETW1Yi2w.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the artificial assumption of i.i.d. random spherical embeddings with pairwise-distinct target tokens, which lacks semantic structure and repeated-token sequence dynamics.

AEEYuIynfn.one_liner: Benchmarks physical reasoning in video generation using 250 prompts, 13 physical laws, observable sub-questions, and a trained VLM judge.
AEEYuIynfn.problem: Existing video physics benchmarks rely on coarse holistic scores, suffer from annotator fatigue/bias, and lack auditable per-law automated evaluators.
AEEYuIynfn.method: PhyGround pairs 250 prompts with expected outcomes across 13 physical laws decomposed into observable sub-questions, evaluated via a quality-controlled human study (459 annotators) and used to train an automated VLM evaluator (PhyJudge-9B).
AEEYuIynfn.key_idea: Decomposes 13 physical laws into observable sub-questions per prompt and trains PhyJudge-9B on quality-controlled human annotations for per-law diagnostics.
AEEYuIynfn.evidence: Evaluates eight video generation models using 5,796 complete human annotations (over 37.4K fine-grained labels) and compares PhyJudge-9B against general-purpose VLMs.
AEEYuIynfn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the fine-grained per-law diagnostic taxonomy and the large-scale, quality-controlled human annotation study.
AEEYuIynfn.main_concern: Reviewers question generalizability of PhyJudge-9B to newer models, potential conflation of event completion with physical plausibility, and lack of backbone scaling ablations.

o2aj8KYAsT.one_liner: Audits NoThink post-training in hybrid reasoning models via bidirectional causal interventions along a base Think-NoThink activation axis.
o2aj8KYAsT.problem: Accuracy gains from post-training hybrid reasoning models in NoThink mode may simply re-invoke existing Think behavior rather than improving non-thinking capability.
o2aj8KYAsT.method: The authors define a base-derived Think-NoThink activation direction and apply bidirectional causal mediation—steering the base model toward Think and counter-steering trained checkpoints—across models and post-training methods.
o2aj8KYAsT.key_idea: Measures and intervenes on checkpoint drift along a base-model Think-NoThink activation contrast vector to quantify thinking leakage.
o2aj8KYAsT.evidence: Evaluated across three models, three post-training methods, and nine aligned checkpoints on competition math benchmarks.
o2aj8KYAsT.claimed_gains: Across nine aligned checkpoints with positive NoThink gains, counter-steering removes 42% to 79% of the gains.
o2aj8KYAsT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper audits an important evaluation ambiguity in hybrid reasoning models using clean bidirectional interventions.
o2aj8KYAsT.main_concern: Reviewers question measuring drift relative to the base Think representation rather than post-trained Think, unverified engagement restoration during counter-steering, and confounding factors like response length.

VaE1JTfsZO.one_liner: Audits SDPO and OPSD self-distillation, finding gains stem from memorization, answer-only supervision, or Think-to-NoThink distillation.
VaE1JTfsZO.problem: It is unclear whether self-distillation from privileged information genuinely improves reasoning or relies on simpler shortcuts.
VaE1JTfsZO.method: The authors reproduce SDPO and OPSD and test them using problem-disjoint coding splits, final-answer SFT without chain-of-thought, thinking-mode ablations, and gradient alignment against held-out GRPO gradients.
VaE1JTfsZO.key_idea: Tests self-distillation against problem-disjoint splits, answer-only SFT, and held-out GRPO gradient alignment to isolate non-reasoning mechanisms.
VaE1JTfsZO.evidence: Experiments on LiveCodeBench v6, science reasoning, tool use, and math across multiple seeds and model families.
VaE1JTfsZO.claimed_gains: On LiveCodeBench v6 at step 200, held-out-problem changes are -2.5/-0.5/-9.9 points for SDPO versus +3.7/+4.9/+2.6 for GRPO across three models.
VaE1JTfsZO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree this is a valuable corrective study, particularly the problem-disjoint coding split and OPSD thinking-mode analysis.
VaE1JTfsZO.main_concern: Reviewers note that matching answer-only SFT does not prove no reasoning occurs and that Proposition 3.1's complete-sequence KL analysis does not directly establish the token-level gradient diagnosis.

JV2qLlquD3.one_liner: Learns basis functions for velocity fields and adapts flow-matching models to unseen distributions via least-squares projection.
JV2qLlquD3.problem: Adapting generative flow-matching models to new target distributions from example data points at inference time without retraining remains challenging.
JV2qLlquD3.method: Function Projection for Flow Matching (FP-FM) learns a shared set of basis functions spanning velocity fields across training distributions and adapts to unseen target distributions via least-squares projection of context samples. Three variants (Static, Temporal, Dynamic) trade off expressivity and compute by enriching how basis coefficients are computed.
JV2qLlquD3.key_idea: Spans velocity fields with learned basis functions and computes adaptation coefficients for unseen target distributions via least-squares projection.
JV2qLlquD3.evidence: Evaluated on synthetic datasets, MNIST, and ImageNet with precision, recall, and FID comparisons against baselines.
JV2qLlquD3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the function-space basis formulation is intuitive, clearly presented, and enables cheap training-free adaptation.
JV2qLlquD3.main_concern: Reviewers are concerned about weak visual quality and high FID on ImageNet, insufficient ImageNet ablations on context shots, and limited baseline comparisons.

2GHU6FSMiz.one_liner: Trains a projection network mapping on-device small-LLM personalized soft prompts into a large server-side LLM.
2GHU6FSMiz.problem: Large server-side LLMs cannot train on private user data, while small on-device LLMs lack the generation capability for complex tasks.
2GHU6FSMiz.method: The method first learns user-specific personalization soft prompts on-device using a small LLM, then trains a projection network that maps those soft prompts into the prompt space of a large server-side LLM. This allows the large LLM to personalize to unseen users without receiving raw user data.
2GHU6FSMiz.key_idea: Projects user-specific soft prompts learned on a small on-device LLM into the input space of a frozen large server-side LLM.
2GHU6FSMiz.evidence: Evaluated across multiple small-to-large LLM pairs on unseen-user text generation and 5-class rating prediction tasks.
2GHU6FSMiz.claimed_gains: Achieves over 60% F1 on a 5-class rating prediction task where prompting baselines fail to follow instructions.
2GHU6FSMiz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is intuitive, easy to follow, and evaluated across multiple model combinations and unseen-user splits.
2GHU6FSMiz.main_concern: Reviewers question the novelty over prior prompt-projection/PEFT-transfer methods and find the privacy validation weak against potential server-side attacks on transmitted prompts.

3JzTSbUpiu.one_liner: Deploys adversarial agents to mutate mathematical proofs and distills successful attacks into strategies that break agentic judges.
3JzTSbUpiu.problem: As AI agents are increasingly used as judges for complex mathematical reasoning, systematic methods are needed to uncover their blind spots and failure modes.
3JzTSbUpiu.method: The framework deploys adversarial agents to inject errors into sound mathematical proofs that fool agentic judges, then distills those successful attacks into a compact library of natural-language mutation strategies. Strategies are evaluated on held-out proofs across GPT-5.6-sol (Codex) and Claude Opus 5 (Claude Code) judges.
3JzTSbUpiu.key_idea: Adversarially mutates sound proofs to fool agentic judges and distills the attacks into transferable natural-language mutation strategies.
3JzTSbUpiu.evidence: Evaluated on held-out mathematical proof corpora (10–40 proofs per dataset) using GPT-5.6-sol/Codex and Claude Opus 5/Claude Code.
3JzTSbUpiu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem of auditing agentic math judges is important and appreciate the clean separation of discovery, distillation, and held-out evaluation.
3JzTSbUpiu.main_concern: Reviewers emphasize that the core judge miss-rate metric relies on same-model LLM checkers (MutationChecker and JudgeChecker) with minimal human validation.

ZnG7TNmdNY.one_liner: Augments JEPA world models with a bisimulation encoder to filter nuisance slow features for robust latent planning.
ZnG7TNmdNY.problem: Latent predictive world models such as DINO-WM degrade at test time when exposed to task-irrelevant slow features like background shifts and visual distractors.
ZnG7TNmdNY.method: JEPA-Bisim adds a patch-wise bisimulation encoder on top of frozen visual features (such as DINOv2, SimDINOv2, or iBOT) to enforce control-relevant state equivalence, mapping states with similar transition dynamics close together in a compact latent space while suppressing background and distractor variations.
ZnG7TNmdNY.key_idea: Augments a JEPA world model with a patch-wise bisimulation encoder that enforces transition-dynamics equivalence to suppress task-irrelevant visual features.
ZnG7TNmdNY.evidence: Evaluated on PointMaze navigation and PushT manipulation under test-time background changes and visual distractors across DINOv2, SimDINOv2, and iBOT.
ZnG7TNmdNY.claimed_gains: Operates in a reduced latent space up to 10x smaller than DINO-WM while improving robustness; PointMaze success under LCG shift improves from ~0.48 to 0.78.
ZnG7TNmdNY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the sensitivity of JEPA world models to slow features is an important problem and the patch-wise adaptation is lightweight and modular.
ZnG7TNmdNY.main_concern: Reviewers point out flaws in the reward-free bisimulation formulation and Theorem 3.1, missing projector-without-bisimulation ablations, and testing on only two environments.

vlidOF3462.one_liner: Trains pocket-prediction heads on frozen co-folding model features and introduces the PocketWatch temporal-split benchmark.
vlidOF3462.problem: Existing protein-ligand binding site benchmarks overlap with co-folding model training sets, and no public method leverages frozen co-folding features for pocket prediction.
vlidOF3462.method: The authors curate PocketWatch, a temporal-split dataset of post-cutoff ligand pockets stratified by sequence similarity, structural similarity, and crypticity. They train zPocket, lightweight prediction heads on top of frozen pair representations from co-folding models (Protenix and ESMFold2), to predict residue-level pocket probabilities and centroids.
vlidOF3462.key_idea: Trains lightweight binding-site prediction heads over frozen pair representations from pretrained co-folding models evaluated on a temporal-split benchmark.
vlidOF3462.evidence: Evaluated on PocketWatch against nine baselines including retrained UniSite-3D, VN-EGNN, UniSite-1D, P2Rank, DeepPocket, and AF2Bind.
vlidOF3462.claimed_gains: Best zPocket model achieves 0.745 overall per-target AUPRC versus 0.648 for retrained UniSite-3D, 0.598 for VN-EGNN, 0.595 for UniSite-1D, 0.477 for P2Rank, 0.475 for DeepPocket, and 0.456 for AF2Bind.
vlidOF3462.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree PocketWatch is a valuable temporal-split benchmark and leveraging frozen co-folding representations for pocket finding is effective.
vlidOF3462.main_concern: Reviewers note that 71.6% of test pockets have high structural similarity (max_qcov >= 80%) to known pockets, while AUPRC drops to 0.347 on structurally novel pockets.

bbu9Hy6fvQ.one_liner: Benchmarks LLM behavioral value consistency across multi-step branching scenarios covering all 45 Schwartz pairwise tradeoffs.
bbu9Hy6fvQ.problem: Single-turn value elicitation prompts cannot test whether LLMs behave consistently across multi-step contexts or whether a compact value profile explains cross-scenario decisions.
bbu9Hy6fvQ.method: The authors build a benchmark of 450 multi-step branching decision-graph scenarios (10 per pair across all 45 Schwartz value tradeoffs), annotating each option's promoted/sacrificed values and each node's narrative pressure. They evaluate 13 open-source LLMs and three proprietary models on within-scenario versus cross-scenario consistency and latent value-profile fit.
bbu9Hy6fvQ.key_idea: Uses annotated multi-step branching decision graphs across all 45 Schwartz value pairs to measure within-scenario versus cross-scenario consistency and value-profile explanatory power.
bbu9Hy6fvQ.evidence: Evaluations of 13 open-source LLMs from four families and three proprietary systems across 450 branching scenarios, plus a 90-scenario human audit.
bbu9Hy6fvQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate moving beyond isolated single-turn prompts to a comprehensive multi-step branching benchmark covering all 45 Schwartz value tradeoffs.
bbu9Hy6fvQ.main_concern: Two reviewers warn that the headline within-across consistency gap may be a finite-sample metric artifact from comparing majority proportions over short trajectories versus pooled trajectories without a calibrated null.

R5djXMSh35.one_liner: Links induction-head hidden-state movement during ICL to frequency-organized unembedding geometry shaped by cross-entropy training.
R5djXMSh35.problem: Mechanistic accounts of internal in-context learning representations and output-level accounts of predictive distribution shifts remain disconnected.
R5djXMSh35.method: The authors analyze how context-induced hidden-state displacements interact with a spectrally concentrated, frequency-organized unembedding geometry produced by cross-entropy training. They decompose the displacement into label-contrast and orthogonal components and use targeted ablations, attribution, and steering to identify induction heads as a primary causal driver.
R5djXMSh35.key_idea: Decomposes induction-head-driven ICL hidden-state displacement into label-contrast and orthogonal vocabulary-shift components interacting with cross-entropy-shaped unembedding geometry.
R5djXMSh35.evidence: Experiments across seven open-weight LLMs and seven classification tasks, synthetic-model training comparisons, theory, label remapping, and induction-head ablation/steering.
R5djXMSh35.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value framing the unembedding matrix as a bridge between internal and output-level ICL accounts, combining theory with empirical validation, and the counterintuitive orthogonal alignment shift.
R5djXMSh35.main_concern: Reviewers note that the functional significance of global unembedding alignment for ICL accuracy is not established (e.g., GLM4-9B succeeds with a negative shift), tasks are simple, and presentation lacks a clear hierarchy of findings.

pOwgZfiZzd.one_liner: Detects backdoor-poisoned training examples without clean reference data by finding dense subgraphs of pairwise mutual influence.
pOwgZfiZzd.problem: Clean-label and stealthy backdoor poisons are hard to detect as individual anomalies and often require a trusted clean validation set.
pOwgZfiZzd.method: TIDE estimates pairwise training influence between samples by splitting data into source and probe sets without needing clean reference data. Exploiting the higher mutual influence among samples sharing a backdoor trigger, it detects poisoned subsets as dense subgraphs in the resulting influence graph.
pOwgZfiZzd.key_idea: Estimates source-to-probe mutual training influence without clean reference data and extracts poisoned groups as dense subgraphs in the influence graph.
pOwgZfiZzd.evidence: Evaluations against clean-label and backdoor poisoning attacks on benchmarks including CIFAR-10 and GTSRB, plus an adaptive attack reducing mutual influence.
pOwgZfiZzd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical reference-free setting, the simple and fast bipartite dense-subgraph formulation, and broad evaluation across clean-label attacks and defenses.
pOwgZfiZzd.main_concern: Reviewers question robustness under very low poison ratios (where random probe splits may miss poisons) or multi-trigger attacks, fixed peeling budgets, and cancellation/specificity issues in the batch-influence approximation.

cWvrzw3TEk.one_liner: Triggers teacher recovery suffixes trained via behavior cloning whenever segment-level student-teacher divergence spikes during on-policy distillation.
cWvrzw3TEk.problem: On-policy distillation becomes unreliable and suffers gradient spikes when the student diverges from the teacher due to large policy gaps or compounding long-horizon errors.
cWvrzw3TEk.method: Divergence-Triggered Dynamic Distillation (DTDD) monitors segment-level student-teacher divergence during student rollouts. When divergence exceeds a threshold, the student prefix keeps standard OPD supervision while the teacher generates a recovery suffix trained via online behavior cloning.
cWvrzw3TEk.key_idea: Uses segment-level student-teacher divergence to dynamically switch from standard on-policy distillation on the prefix to behavior cloning on a teacher-generated recovery suffix.
cWvrzw3TEk.evidence: Experiments in long-horizon reasoning, base-model distillation without offline SFT, and multi-turn agents (ALFWorld and agentic code), plus trigger and loss-clamp ablations.
cWvrzw3TEk.claimed_gains: DTDD reduces post-warmup peak gradient norm by 8.6×, reaches 21.3% held-out math accuracy in 2.6× fewer optimizer updates than OPD from a base initialization (both finishing near 22%), and improves best-observed performance by 4.8 and 4.1 percentage points on ALFWorld and agentic code, respectively.
cWvrzw3TEk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the segment-level divergence switching mechanism is simple, interpretable, practically motivated, and evaluated with helpful controls.
cWvrzw3TEk.main_concern: Reviewers note that headline +4.8/+4.1 gains come from single-run best-observed checkpoints, a simple [-1, 1] OPD clamp already stabilizes gradients, and differentiation from AdaSwitch/DASH-OPD/Guided-OPD is narrow.

qy0AJWUh1L.one_liner: Computes a one-shot SVD activation basis per layer to perform forward-only zeroth-order LLM fine-tuning in low-rank coefficient space.
qy0AJWUh1L.problem: Zeroth-order LLM fine-tuning suffers from high-variance gradient estimates in full parameter space or limited flexibility under random low-dimensional perturbations.
qy0AJWUh1L.method: ZO-Act computes a fixed low-rank basis from input activations via a single SVD per linear layer at initialization and optimizes only lightweight coefficient matrices using forward-only loss evaluations. This explicit low-dimensional parameterization enables standard Adam momentum updates and frozen-weight INT4 quantized fine-tuning.
qy0AJWUh1L.key_idea: Fixes a one-shot SVD basis of layer input activations at initialization and applies zeroth-order Adam optimization solely to low-rank coefficient matrices.
qy0AJWUh1L.evidence: Dimension-alignment trade-off analysis and fine-tuning experiments on Llama-3-8B, OPT-13B, Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-32B, and INT4 Llama-3-8B.
qy0AJWUh1L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the simple, practical one-shot SVD parameterization that enables Adam momentum and low-memory INT4 fine-tuning with strong empirical performance.
qy0AJWUh1L.main_concern: One reviewer flags heavy conceptual and methodological overlap with AGZO (ICML 2026), questioning why a fixed initial activation basis is preferable to a dynamically updated basis when activations shift during fine-tuning.

covnFzcbi6.one_liner: Generates verified single-function web tools from page evidence and dynamically registers them by live page state.
covnFzcbi6.problem: Web agents struggle with low-level browser actions, while existing learned web tools bundle multi-page workflows or expose all tools regardless of page state.
covnFzcbi6.method: PACT extracts reusable single-function tools from website and page evidence, independently verifies their semantics, scope, and execution, dynamically registers tools according to live page state via WebMCP, and bounds tool execution at navigation boundaries so the agent retains control.
covnFzcbi6.key_idea: Derive and verify single-function page-coupled tools bounded at navigation edges and dynamically register them conditioned on live page state.
covnFzcbi6.evidence: Evaluations span 812 WebArena tasks across 16 agent-model configurations, plus WebArena Verified, fine-tuned web agents, mock websites, and tool-integration ablations.
covnFzcbi6.claimed_gains: On 812 WebArena tasks, PACT improves success across all 16 agent-model configurations and reduces token usage in most of them.
covnFzcbi6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that bounding single-function tools to live page state is a clean, practical design backed by broad evaluation across WebArena and 16 agent-model configurations.
covnFzcbi6.main_concern: Reviewers view PACT as combining existing ingredients (WebMCP, WALT, SkillWeaver, WebXSkill) without isolating which component drives gains or quantitatively comparing against prior tool-generation baselines.

Bb6SRelZWV.one_liner: Integrates persistence-guided patch masking and a persistent-homology count decoder into a 3D masked autoencoder for TPMS metamaterials.
Bb6SRelZWV.problem: Existing 3D representation learners for Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) metamaterials rarely supervise global structural connectivity that governs mechanical response.
Bb6SRelZWV.method: The authors augment a DMAE backbone with persistence-guided masking that prioritizes patches tied to persistent topological features and an auxiliary persistent-homology decoder predicting counts of connected components, tunnels, and voids.
Bb6SRelZWV.key_idea: Prioritize DMAE masking on patches linked to persistent topological features while decoding topological feature counts (components, tunnels, voids) from the latent representation.
Bb6SRelZWV.evidence: Evaluations on two TPMS datasets test structural family classification, mechanical-property classification, unsupervised clustering, and regression against nine baselines with multi-seed ablations.
Bb6SRelZWV.claimed_gains: The method improves family classification by up to 3.9% and unsupervised property-clustering performance by up to 26.7% and 51.5% across the two datasets.
Bb6SRelZWV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicitly injecting persistent homology into 3D metamaterial representation learning is physically well motivated and evaluated across multiple downstream tasks.
Bb6SRelZWV.main_concern: Reviewers flag irreconcilable clustering evaluation numbers (e.g., 0.044 matched accuracy), unconvincing ablations for persistence-guided masking, and missing comparisons to recent topological representation learning methods.

iEgCzPwlXu.one_liner: Benchmarks paired Chinese-English terminology substitutions to expose item-level disagreements across likelihood-based preference scoring rules.
iEgCzPwlXu.problem: Likelihood-based evaluations of language model preference depend on scoring scope and aggregation choices, which can silently flip individual preference judgments.
iEgCzPwlXu.method: ChiEngMixBench provides paired Chinese-English terminology substitutions and compares four likelihood-based preference definitions varying scoring scope (whole sentence vs. target span) and aggregation (sum vs. mean).
iEgCzPwlXu.key_idea: Evaluate identical paired Chinese-English terminology substitutions under four likelihood scoring rules (sentence vs. span, sum vs. mean) to compare aggregate versus item-level preference agreement.
iEgCzPwlXu.evidence: Experiments evaluate several language models on ChiEngMixBench and measure aggregate preference direction alongside item-level winner overlap across scoring rules.
iEgCzPwlXu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the controlled paired design cleanly isolates scoring-rule effects and highlights the gap between aggregate direction agreement and item-level consistency.
iEgCzPwlXu.main_concern: Reviewers note that the analysis is mostly descriptive without probing causal drivers (like tokenization) or external validation against generation/human preference, and that source sentences are omitted from the release.

bFigTBAQbo.one_liner: Optimizes one-shot encoded memory patterns at write time to minimize interference with previously stored distributed associative memories.
bFigTBAQbo.problem: Online distributed associative memory models suffer from severe interference when patterns arrive sequentially in fixed-size shared weights.
bFigTBAQbo.method: Inspired by hippocampal neuronal memory allocation, ENCORE introduces write-time encoding optimization that iteratively selects sparse expanded codes balancing input fidelity, neuron usage, and interference with stored memories while keeping architecture and storage fixed.
bFigTBAQbo.key_idea: Optimize each incoming pattern's sparse internal representation at encoding time to minimize interference with previously stored patterns in shared associative memory weights.
bFigTBAQbo.evidence: Experiments measure online retrieval capacity on synthetic patterns, MNIST, and ImageNet latents compared against fixed-size distributed memory and same-expansion Hopfield baselines.
bFigTBAQbo.claimed_gains: With architecture and storage held fixed, ENCORE raises online retrieval capacity by 2x on synthetic patterns, 9x on MNIST, and 1.3x on ImageNet latents.
bFigTBAQbo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that optimizing internal representations at encoding time is an interesting, complementary axis to retrieval dynamics and learning rules for online associative memory.
bFigTBAQbo.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the weak online Modern Hopfield baseline (backprop on single samples), unaccounted storage and compute overhead of expanded matrices and iterative encoding, and weak biological grounding.

iwbEqoOHki.one_liner: Provides an agent-native post-training system linking hypothesis submission, asynchronous GPU training, protected evaluation, and persistent research records.
iwbEqoOHki.problem: Autonomous post-training research requires sustaining multi-step hypothesis testing, GPU job execution, evaluation integrity, and state persistence across long-running agent campaigns.
iwbEqoOHki.method: Athanor separates agent hypothesis and recipe submission from system services that schedule asynchronous GPU training, guard evaluation, and link recipes, code, checkpoints, and notes into a persistent inspectable research record.
iwbEqoOHki.key_idea: Decouple agent recipe submission from persistent system services that manage asynchronous GPU training, protected evaluation, and linked experimental records.
iwbEqoOHki.evidence: Evaluated across six campaigns with Opus 5 on eight-GPU nodes post-training Qwen3-4B-Base over seven benchmarks (839 accepted experiments, 711 evaluations, nearly 1,000 notes).
iwbEqoOHki.claimed_gains: Opus 5 improves Qwen3-4B-Base from 26.4 to 63.2 across seven benchmarks using a fixed decontaminated data pool, compared to 70.4 for the official instruction-tuned model.
iwbEqoOHki.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that Athanor is a substantial, practical systems demonstration with a valuable inspectable trajectory history over hundreds of real GPU experiments.
iwbEqoOHki.main_concern: Reviewers state that experiments do not isolate the added value of the agent or infrastructure against matched-budget recipe search or other autoresearch harnesses, and note weak technical novelty and writing clarity.

31YeSXrkoq.one_liner: Encodes 3D assets directly from meshes and materials and composes them with placements into scene embeddings via identification and language objectives.
31YeSXrkoq.problem: Global 3D scene encoders cannot reuse object representations across arrangements, while feature-prediction composition operators take layout shortcuts that ignore object content.
31YeSXrkoq.method: ROSE-3D encodes each 3D asset without rendering by binding local surface orientation and appearance to continuous surface coordinates, then applies a learned composition operator over object embeddings and 3D placements trained with feature prediction, location-based object identification, and language alignment.
31YeSXrkoq.key_idea: Compose render-free mesh-and-material object embeddings with 3D placements using identification and language supervision to prevent layout-only shortcuts.
31YeSXrkoq.evidence: Evaluated on 3D question answering and scene benchmarks using InternScenes reconstructions alongside shortcut and efficiency analyses.
31YeSXrkoq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusable render-free compositional 3D scene representation and the layout-shortcut diagnosis are well motivated and interesting.
31YeSXrkoq.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about potentially unfair benchmark and timing comparisons using known InternScenes assets and placements, limited evaluation of cross-scene generalization, and lack of direct representation quality metrics.

4y5b0cQBcL.one_liner: Solves zero-shot blind image inpainting with pretrained flow-matching priors by modeling unknown corruptions as nested pixel- and superpixel-sparse residuals.
4y5b0cQBcL.problem: Prior zero-shot blind inpainting methods optimize explicit sparsity-regularized masks that are sensitive to unknown corruption budgets and prone to degenerate interpolation.
4y5b0cQBcL.method: ZSBI-FM avoids explicit mask estimation by optimizing a pretrained flow-matching prior under a nested SCAD objective combining pixel-level sparsity and SLIC superpixel group sparsity on the reconstruction residual, paired with an unsupervised early stopping criterion.
4y5b0cQBcL.key_idea: Optimize a pretrained flow-matching prior with a nested pixel- and SLIC-superpixel SCAD residual penalty and unsupervised early stopping instead of an explicit corruption mask.
4y5b0cQBcL.evidence: Evaluated across diverse mask geometries, fillings, and measurement noise on FFHQ and ImageNet, plus defect localization on simulated BTAD.
4y5b0cQBcL.claimed_gains: ZSBI-FM improves PSNR over the strongest competing method by 2.02–2.49 dB on FFHQ and 0.78–1.40 dB on ImageNet.
4y5b0cQBcL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling unknown corruptions as structured sparse residuals without explicit masks is well motivated and achieves strong quantitative reconstruction on FFHQ and ImageNet.
4y5b0cQBcL.main_concern: Reviewers note missing component ablations and direct comparisons against FMPlug, limited conceptual novelty over RGI's additive sparse model, and sparse visual comparisons.

cFxQZaXblA.one_liner: Projects token distributions onto task-specific security policies at every denoising step of discrete diffusion language models to block prompt injection.
cFxQZaXblA.problem: Detection-based defenses against prompt injection in agentic AI remain vulnerable to adaptive attacks that optimize malicious instructions.
cFxQZaXblA.method: CoDA enforces task-dependent security policies directly inside discrete diffusion language models by projecting sequence-wide token distributions onto policy-compliant sets (using prefix tries for multi-token values) at each denoising step without extra training.
cFxQZaXblA.key_idea: Project discrete diffusion token distributions onto policy-compliant sets at every denoising step rather than relying on input detection or post-hoc filtering.
cFxQZaXblA.evidence: Evaluated across static and adaptive prompt injection benchmarks (four AgentDojo suites) on two diffusion language model families against last-step projection.
cFxQZaXblA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that enforcing task policies across diffusion denoising steps is a clean, training-free design that reduces prompt-injection attack success rates without relying on attack detection.
cFxQZaXblA.main_concern: Reviewers note that strong guarantees rely on manually crafted oracle policies and reliable field parsing, with nonzero ASR under LLM-selected policies and no direct comparisons to autoregressive constrained decoding or existing agent defenses.

DCkOCAgPex.one_liner: Distills multiple expert LLMs on-policy by transferring post-training proficiency deltas relative to each expert's pre-specialization reference model.
DCkOCAgPex.problem: Matching full teacher output distributions in multi-teacher on-policy distillation introduces competing supervision that interferes with skills learned from other experts.
DCkOCAgPex.method: LEAP computes each expert's acquired proficiency as the difference between the specialized expert and its pre-specialization reference model, then integrates these delta signals (with advantage centering and consistency gating) on student-generated trajectories.
DCkOCAgPex.key_idea: Supervise student rollouts with expert-minus-reference post-training proficiency deltas rather than raw teacher distributions to reduce cross-expert gradient conflicts.
DCkOCAgPex.evidence: Evaluated via supervision conflict analysis, sequential expert distillation, and domain-routed mixed-query training on Qwen3 models and math benchmarks (including AIME24/25).
DCkOCAgPex.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that isolating post-training proficiency deltas to reduce spurious teacher conflicts is intuitive, clearly presented, and consistently outperforms standard OPD.
DCkOCAgPex.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty over prior delta-distillation methods (OPD^2, Direct-OPD) and note missing component ablations—especially isolating the consistency gate that filters ~75% of signals—and narrow evaluation.

sXb0yoKcfS.one_liner: Stores reusable web-agent workflows as versioned notebooks with validation gates that selectively execute code cells or fall back to natural language.
sXb0yoKcfS.problem: Reusable agent scripts and workflows that succeed once frequently break under environment drift, underspecified tasks, or shifting distributions in web automation.
