sXb0yoKcfS.method: SKILL.nb governs agent workflows as auditable, versioned notebooks interleaving natural-language guidance, executable code cells, validation gates, fallback paths, and multimodal execution traces, using execution evidence to selectively formalize steps and fall back locally when gates fail.
sXb0yoKcfS.key_idea: Use evidence-calibrated selective formalization and cell-level validation gates in versioned notebooks so each workflow step runs code or falls back locally to natural language.
sXb0yoKcfS.evidence: Evaluated on WebArena-Verified online rounds and GitLab version-drift reuse/repair experiments.
sXb0yoKcfS.claimed_gains: On WebArena-Verified, SKILL.nb achieves 56.3% success in an online round.
sXb0yoKcfS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating persistent workflows across repeated use, version drift, and repair is valuable and that gated hybrid notebooks improve reuse consistency.
sXb0yoKcfS.main_concern: Reviewers note that system-level comparisons confound lifecycle policies with different inference/update configurations, lack wall-clock latency measurements, and report only a single task-order stream without matched-compute repair controls.

5BWkyZYihB.one_liner: Selects exogenous time-series features using the temporal standard deviation of bin-wise conditional distribution differences to filter unstable predictors.
5BWkyZYihB.problem: Incorporating exogenous features into time-series forecasting models often degrades accuracy when feature-target conditional relationships drift over time.
5BWkyZYihB.method: The authors define Conditional Distribution Difference (CDD) via a bin-wise representation of feature-target conditional relationships and use its temporal standard deviation (CDD-std) to filter out temporally unstable exogenous features.
5BWkyZYihB.key_idea: Rank and filter exogenous features by the temporal standard deviation of bin-wise conditional distribution differences rather than static correlation.
5BWkyZYihB.evidence: Validated on controlled synthetic experiments and real-world forecasting datasets (including Neuro and SP500) across iTransformer, TimeMixer, CrossLinear, and TimeFilter.
5BWkyZYihB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that filtering exogenous features by temporal conditional stability is a well-motivated, simple, model-agnostic approach that reduces error over using all features.
5BWkyZYihB.main_concern: Reviewers note that univariate bin-wise CDD ignores conditional utility given target history and other covariates, lacks baselines that measure time-varying correlation, and shows small gains over univariate forecasting.

jlK8YpYELd.one_liner: Decouples PPO's Gaussian optimization anchor from environment interaction by reshaping sampled actions with a Q-guided residual flow.
jlK8YpYELd.problem: Coupling a single Gaussian policy for both PPO optimization and environment exploration limits behavioral expressiveness, while direct Q-guided policy updates are sensitive to critic error.
jlK8YpYELd.method: Proximal Behavior Reshaping (PBR) keeps a Gaussian anchor updated by PPO and trains a residual flow via conditional flow matching on Q-reweighted local candidates (using recent rollout buffers) to transform sampled actions into a richer executed behavior policy.
jlK8YpYELd.key_idea: Optimize a Gaussian anchor with PPO while applying a Q-guided residual flow to reshape its sampled actions into a richer behavior distribution.
jlK8YpYELd.evidence: Evaluated on a 2D wall-avoidance goal-reaching task and six high-dimensional Isaac Lab locomotion and manipulation benchmarks across five seeds with component ablations.
jlK8YpYELd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that PBR is a clear, practical addition to PPO that achieves strong, computationally efficient results on high-dimensional Isaac Lab tasks.
jlK8YpYELd.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty relative to QFLEX and point out that executing the reshaped policy at test time confounds exploration benefits with test-time critic-guided action refinement.

fI8nH4BwBY.one_liner: Introduces a 554-problem astronomy computational-reasoning benchmark with five task types, five cognitive dimensions, and code-formalized isomorphic variants.
fI8nH4BwBY.problem: Existing LLM benchmarks underexplore cross-disciplinary computational reasoning in astronomy and are vulnerable to data contamination.
fI8nH4BwBY.method: AstroMathBench curates 554 manually verified astronomy problems across five task types (formula calculation, derivation, unimodal, multimodal, and code-based computation), annotates five cognitive dimensions, and uses a private/public split with code-formalized isomorphic variant generation to mitigate contamination.
fI8nH4BwBY.key_idea: Combine five astronomy computational task types, five cognitive reasoning dimensions, and code-formalized isomorphic problem variants for contamination-mitigated evaluation.
fI8nH4BwBY.evidence: Evaluated 10 LLMs on 554 verified seed problems (90.1% code-formalized) alongside human assessments, evaluator comparisons, and variant stability checks.
fI8nH4BwBY.claimed_gains: Among 10 evaluated LLMs on 554 seed problems (90.1% code-formalized), the highest accuracy reaches only 76%.
fI8nH4BwBY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that AstroMathBench addresses a meaningful cross-disciplinary evaluation gap with a thorough data-curation pipeline and detailed cognitive-dimension error analysis.
fI8nH4BwBY.main_concern: Reviewers note that numerical-value mutation only mitigates exact-instance memorization rather than strategy contamination, and point to modest methodological novelty, small multimodal subset size (28 problems), and missing newest frontier models.

LWZJlrMwtU.one_liner: Uses representation kernels and kernel signal-to-noise ratios to diagnose whether robot policies memorize, adapt to, or ignore training variations.
LWZJlrMwtU.problem: Practitioners tune domain randomization and demonstration diversity for robot manipulation by trial and error because internal generalization mechanisms remain poorly understood.
LWZJlrMwtU.method: The authors apply representation kernels (including eNTK) and kernel-based signal-to-noise ratios on controlled factor probes to distinguish memorization, task-relevant adaptation, and invariance to task-irrelevant nuisance factors across RL, imitation learning, and VLA fine-tuning.
LWZJlrMwtU.key_idea: Diagnose memorization, adaptation, and nuisance-factor invariance in robot policies via representation-kernel structure and kernel signal-to-noise ratios on controlled probes.
LWZJlrMwtU.evidence: Case studies varying object size, color, type, lighting, and prompts across ManiSkill RL, ACT, and VLA fine-tuning on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and a small hardware study.
LWZJlrMwtU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that diagnosing internal robot learning mechanisms beyond task success rates via representation kernels provides an informative perspective on domain randomization.
LWZJlrMwtU.main_concern: Reviewers question whether kernel diagnostics establish causal mechanisms rather than probe-dependent correlations, note high eNTK cost and prior factor knowledge requirements without simpler baselines, and find predictive claims weakly supported.

D0OX8xAwE4.one_liner: Derives closed-form pseudo-label budget and student-width thresholds showing an active-bottleneck mechanism for ridgeless weak-to-strong generalization.
D0OX8xAwE4.problem: It is unclear when a student trained on a weak teacher's predictions can outperform the teacher without early stopping or explicit regularization.
D0OX8xAwE4.method: The authors analyze fully converged, ridgeless two-stage linear and random-feature regression via deterministic equivalents, deriving closed-form intervals for pseudo-label budget m and student feature width where a bottleneck filters teacher noise without starving the student of signal.
D0OX8xAwE4.key_idea: Characterizes ridgeless weak-to-strong generalization via an active-bottleneck phase boundary in pseudo-label budget and student width that implicitly filters teacher error.
D0OX8xAwE4.evidence: Exact geometric and deterministic-equivalent theoretical derivations under power-law covariance and random-feature models.
D0OX8xAwE4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the active-bottleneck mechanism and exact phase conditions on student width and pseudo-label count clear and insightful.
D0OX8xAwE4.main_concern: Reviewers question whether identical-class linear regression represents weak-to-strong generalization rather than self-distillation, and flag rigor concerns in taking ridgeless limits of positive-ridge deterministic equivalents.
